120: var {parentEntities} = await _dbContext.{ParentEntities}
121:     .Include(o => o.Members.Where(m => m.IsApproved))
122:     .ToListAsync();
123: 
124: // ✅ Only include upcoming {entities}
125: var {parentEntities} = await _dbContext.{ParentEntities}
126:     .Include(o => o.{Entities}.Where(e => e.StartDate > DateTime.Now))
127:     .ToListAsync();
128: ```
129: 
130: ---
131: 
132: ## Projection (Select)
133: 
134: ### Project to DTO
135: 
136: ```csharp
137: // ✅ RECOMMENDED: Project directly to DTO
138: var {entity}Dtos = await _dbContext.{Entities}
139:     .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
140:     .Select(e => new {Entity}ListDto
141:     {
142:         Id = e.Id,
143:         Title = e.Title,
144:         Description = e.Description,
145:         {ParentEntity}Name = e.{ParentEntity}.FullName,  // ✅ No N+1 query
146:         StartDate = e.StartDate
147:     })
148:     .ToListAsync();
149: ```
150: 
151: **Benefits**:
152: - ✅ Only selected columns retrieved
153: - ✅ No change tracking
154: - ✅ Faster than loading entire entities
155: 
156: ### Anonymous Type
157: 
158: ```csharp
159: // ✅ Project to anonymous type
160: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
161:     .Select(e => new
162:     {
163:         e.Id,
164:         e.Title,
165:         {ParentEntity}Name = e.{ParentEntity}.FullName
166:     })
167:     .ToListAsync();
168: ```
169: 
170: ### Conditional Projection
171: 
172: ```csharp
173: // ✅ Conditional fields in projection
174: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
175:     .Select(e => new {Entity}ListDto
176:     {
177:         Id = e.Id,
178:         Title = e.Title,
179:         IsUpcoming = e.StartDate > DateTime.Now,  // Computed
180:         DaysUntil = (e.StartDate - DateTime.Now).Days  // Computed
181:     })
182:     .ToListAsync();
183: ```
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ## Sorting
188: 
189: ### OrderBy
190: 
191: ```csharp
192: // ✅ Ascending
193: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
194:     .OrderBy(e => e.StartDate)
195:     .ToListAsync();
196: 
197: // ✅ Descending
198: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
199:     .OrderByDescending(e => e.StartDate)
200:     .ToListAsync();
201: 
202: // ✅ Multiple sort criteria
203: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
204:     .OrderBy(e => e.{ParentEntity}Id)
205:     .ThenByDescending(e => e.StartDate)
206:     .ToListAsync();
207: ```
208: 
209: ### Dynamic Sorting
210: 
211: ```csharp
212: public async Task<List<{Entity}ListDto>> Get{Entities}(string sortBy, bool descending)
213: {
214:     var query = _dbContext.{Entities}.AsQueryable();
215: 
216:     query = sortBy switch
217:     {
218:         "title" => descending ? query.OrderByDescending(e => e.Title) : query.OrderBy(e => e.Title),
219:         "date" => descending ? query.OrderByDescending(e => e.StartDate) : query.OrderBy(e => e.StartDate),
220:         "views" => descending ? query.OrderByDescending(e => e.ViewCount) : query.OrderBy(e => e.ViewCount),
221:         _ => query.OrderByDescending(e => e.StartDate)  // Default
222:     };
223: 
224:     return await query
225:         .Select(e => new {Entity}ListDto { /* ... */ })
226:         .ToListAsync();
227: }
228: ```
229: 
230: ---
231: 
232: ## Pagination
233: 
234: ### Skip and Take
235: 
236: ```csharp
237: public async Task<List<{Entity}ListDto>> Get{Entities}Paginated(int page, int pageSize)
238: {
239:     return await _dbContext.{Entities}
240:         .OrderByDescending(e => e.StartDate)
241:         .Skip((page - 1) * pageSize)
242:         .Take(pageSize)
243:         .Select(e => new {Entity}ListDto { /* ... */ })
244:         .ToListAsync();
245: }
246: ```
247: 
248: ### With Total Count
249: 
250: ```csharp
251: public async Task<(List<{Entity}ListDto> {Entities}, int TotalCount)> Get{Entities}Paginated(
252:     int page,
253:     int pageSize)
254: {
255:     var query = _dbContext.{Entities}.AsQueryable();
256: 
257:     var totalCount = await query.CountAsync();
258: 
259:     var {entities} = await query
260:         .OrderByDescending(e => e.StartDate)
261:         .Skip((page - 1) * pageSize)
262:         .Take(pageSize)
263:         .Select(e => new {Entity}ListDto { /* ... */ })
264:         .ToListAsync();
265: 
266:     return ({entities}, totalCount);
267: }
268: ```
269: 
270: ---
271: 
272: ## Aggregation
273: 
274: ### Count
275: 
276: ```csharp
277: // Total count
278: var total{Entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}.CountAsync();
279: 
280: // Conditional count
281: var upcomingCount = await _dbContext.{Entities}
282:     .CountAsync(e => e.StartDate > DateTime.Now);
283: ```
284: 
285: ### Sum, Average, Min, Max
286: 
287: ```csharp
288: // Sum
289: var totalViews = await _dbContext.{Entities}.SumAsync(e => e.ViewCount);
290: 
291: // Average
292: var avgPrice = await _dbContext.{Entities}.AverageAsync(e => e.Price);
293: 
294: // Min and Max
295: var earliest{Entity} = await _dbContext.{Entities}.MinAsync(e => e.StartDate);
296: var latest{Entity} = await _dbContext.{Entities}.MaxAsync(e => e.StartDate);
297: ```
298: 
299: ### GroupBy
300: 
301: ```csharp
302: // Group {entities} by {parentEntity}
303: var {entities}By{ParentEntity} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
304:     .GroupBy(e => e.{ParentEntity}Id)
305:     .Select(g => new
306:     {
307:         {ParentEntity}Id = g.Key,
308:         {Entity}Count = g.Count(),
309:         TotalViews = g.Sum(e => e.ViewCount)
310:     })
311:     .ToListAsync();
312: ```
313: 
314: ---
315: 
316: ## Joining
317: 
318: ### Explicit Join
319: 
320: ```csharp
321: var result = await (
322:     from e in _dbContext.{Entities}
323:     join o in _dbContext.{ParentEntities} on e.{ParentEntity}Id equals o.Id
324:     select new {Entity}ListDto
325:     {
326:         Id = e.Id,
327:         Title = e.Title,
328:         {ParentEntity}Name = o.FullName
329:     })
330:     .ToListAsync();
331: ```
332: 
333: ### Include vs Join
334: 
335: ```csharp
336: // ❌ Include (loads entire related entity)
337: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
338:     .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
339:     .ToListAsync();
340: 
341: // ✅ Select (only needed fields)
342: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
343:     .Select(e => new {Entity}ListDto
344:     {
345:         Id = e.Id,
346:         Title = e.Title,
347:         {ParentEntity}Name = e.{ParentEntity}.FullName  // Automatic join
348:     })
349:     .ToListAsync();
350: ```
351: 
352: ---
353: 
354: ## Advanced Patterns
355: 
356: ### AsNoTracking
357: 
358: ```csharp
359: // ✅ Use for read-only queries (faster)
360: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
361:     .AsNoTracking()
362:     .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
363:     .ToListAsync();
364: ```
365: 
366: ### AsSplitQuery
367: 
368: ```csharp
369: // ✅ Avoid cartesian explosion with multiple Includes
370: var {parentEntities} = await _dbContext.{ParentEntities}
371:     .Include(o => o.{Entities})
372:     .Include(o => o.Members)
373:     .AsSplitQuery()  // Executes as 3 separate SQL queries
374:     .ToListAsync();
375: 
376: // ❌ Single query (can cause performance issues)
377: var {parentEntities} = await _dbContext.{ParentEntities}
378:     .Include(o => o.{Entities})
379:     .Include(o => o.Members)
380:     .ToListAsync();
381: ```
382: 
383: ### FromSqlRaw (Raw SQL)
384: 
385: ```csharp
386: // ✅ Use for complex queries not supported by LINQ
387: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
388:     .FromSqlRaw(@"
389:         SELECT * FROM ""{Entities}""
390:         WHERE ""StartDate"" > {0}
391:         ORDER BY ""ViewCount"" DESC
392:     ", DateTime.Now)
393:     .ToListAsync();
394: 
395: // ⚠️ Use parameters to prevent SQL injection
396: var searchTerm = "conference";
397: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
398:     .FromSqlRaw(@"
399:         SELECT * FROM ""{Entities}""
400:         WHERE ""Title"" ILIKE {0}
401:     ", $"%{searchTerm}%")
402:     .ToListAsync();
403: ```
404: 
405: ### Any / All / Contains
406: 
407: ```csharp
408: // Any: Check if any records exist
409: var hasUpcoming{Entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
410:     .AnyAsync(e => e.StartDate > DateTime.Now);
411: 
412: // All: Check if all records match condition
413: var allFree = await _dbContext.{Entities}
414:     .AllAsync(e => e.Price == 0);
415: 
416: // Contains: Check if value in list
417: var {parentEntity}Ids = new[] { guid1, guid2, guid3 };
418: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
419:     .Where(e => {parentEntity}Ids.Contains(e.{ParentEntity}Id))
420:     .ToListAsync();
421: ```
422: 
423: ---
424: 
425: ## Performance Optimization
426: 
427: ### N+1 Query Problem
428: 
429: ```csharp
430: // ❌ N+1 PROBLEM: Loads {parentEntity} for each {entity}
431: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}.ToListAsync();
432: foreach (var item in {entities})
433: {
434:     Console.WriteLine(item.{ParentEntity}.FullName);  // ❌ Separate query per item!
435: }
436: 
437: // ✅ FIX 1: Use Include
438: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
439:     .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
440:     .ToListAsync();
441: 
442: // ✅ FIX 2: Use Select (RECOMMENDED)
443: var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
444:     .Select(e => new
445:     {
446:         e.Id,
447:         e.Title,
448:         {ParentEntity}Name = e.{ParentEntity}.FullName  // ✅ Single query
449:     })
450:     .ToListAsync();
451: ```
452: 
453: ### Avoid Loading Entire Entity
454: 
455: ```csharp
456: // ❌ Loads entire entity (all columns)
457: var titles = await _dbContext.{Entities}
458:     .ToListAsync()
459:     .Select(e => e.Title);  // ❌ Executes in memory
460: 
461: // ✅ Project to only needed columns
462: var titles = await _dbContext.{Entities}
463:     .Select(e => e.Title)
464:     .ToListAsync();  // ✅ Only selects Title column
465: ```
466: 
467: ### Compiled Queries
468: 
469: ```csharp
470: // Define compiled query (cached)
471: private static readonly Func<{DbContext}, {IdType}, Task<{Entity}?>> _get{Entity}ById =
472:     EF.CompileAsyncQuery(({DbContext} context, {IdType} id) =>
473:         context.{Entities}.FirstOrDefault(e => e.Id == id));
474: 
475: // Use compiled query
476: var {entity} = await _get{Entity}ById(_dbContext, {entity}Id);
477: ```
478: 
479: ---
480: 
481: ## Best Practices
482: 
483: | Practice | Reason |
484: |----------|--------|
485: | ✅ Use `Select` for projections | Only retrieves needed columns |
486: | ✅ Use `AsNoTracking()` for read-only | Faster, no change tracking |
487: | ✅ Use `Include` for related data | Avoid N+1 queries |
488: | ✅ Use `AsSplitQuery()` for multiple includes | Avoid cartesian explosion |
489: | ✅ Filter before sorting/paging | Reduces data processed |
490: | ✅ Use `CountAsync()` instead of `Count()` | Non-blocking |
491: | ✅ Use parameters in raw SQL | Prevent SQL injection |
492: | ❌ Don't use `ToList()` before filtering | Loads all data into memory |
493: | ❌ Don't access navigation properties without Include | Causes N+1 |
494: | ❌ Don't track entities for read-only queries | Unnecessary overhead |
495: 
496: ---
497: 
498: **Related Resources**:
499: - [repository-pattern.md](repository-pattern.md) - Repository implementations
500: - [dbcontext-patterns.md](dbcontext-patterns.md) - DbContext configuration
501: - [entity-configuration.md](entity-configuration.md) - Entity relationships
````

## File: .claude/skills/error-tracking/resources/db-performance-monitoring.md
````markdown
  1: # Database Performance Monitoring
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Performance Monitoring Patterns**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: Effective database performance monitoring is crucial for identifying and resolving bottlenecks in your application. This document outlines patterns for tracking database query performance, leveraging .NET's `ActivitySource` for OpenTelemetry compatibility.
  8: 
  9: ---
 10: 
 11: ## 1. Using `ActivitySource` for Tracing
 12: 
 13: `ActivitySource` is part of `System.Diagnostics` and is the recommended way to create custom traces that can be integrated with OpenTelemetry. These traces are visible in tools like the Aspire dashboard, making it easy to visualize performance.
 14: 
 15: ### `ActivitySource` Setup
 16: 
 17: You typically define a static `ActivitySource` instance per logical component (e.g., your Persistence layer).
 18: 
 19: **File**: `{Project}.Persistence/ActivitySourceProvider.cs` (New File)
 20: 
 21: ```csharp
 22: using System.Diagnostics;
 23: 
 24: namespace {Project}.Persistence;
 25: 
 26: /// <summary>
 27: /// Provides a centralized ActivitySource for tracing operations within the Persistence layer.
 28: /// This enables custom spans for database interactions to be captured by OpenTelemetry.
 29: /// </summary>
 30: public static class ActivitySourceProvider
 31: {
 32:     // Define an ActivitySource instance for the Persistence layer.
 33:     // The name should be unique and descriptive.
 34:     public static readonly ActivitySource PersistenceActivitySource = new("{Project}.Persistence");
 35: }
 36: ```
 37: 
 38: ---
 39: 
 40: ## 2. Manual Span Creation in Repositories
 41: 
 42: Wrap database operations in `using (var activity = ...)` blocks to create spans that track their duration and context.
 43: 
 44: **File**: `{Project}.Persistence/Repositories/{Entity}Repository.cs`
 45: 
 46: ```csharp
 47: using System.Diagnostics;
 48: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
 49: using {Project}.Domain;
 50: using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
 51: using System.Collections.Generic;
 52: using System.Threading.Tasks;
 53: 
 54: namespace {Project}.Persistence.Repositories;
 55: 
 56: public class {Entity}Repository : GenericRepository<{Entity}, {IdType}>, I{Entity}Repository
 57: {
 58:     private readonly {DbContext} _dbContext;
 59: 
 60:     public {Entity}Repository({DbContext} dbContext) : base(dbContext)
 61:     {
 62:         _dbContext = dbContext;
 63:     }
 64: 
 65:     public async Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}WithDetails()
 66:     {
 67:         // ✅ Create a new Activity (span) for this specific database operation.
 68:         using var activity = ActivitySourceProvider.PersistenceActivitySource.StartActivity(
 69:             "{Entity}Repository.Get{Entities}WithDetails",
 70:             ActivityKind.Internal
 71:         );
 72: 
 73:         // Optional: Add tags to the activity for more context.
 74:         activity?.AddTag("db.operation", "SELECT");
 75:         activity?.AddTag("db.collection", "{Entities}");
 76:         // activity?.AddTag("tenant.id", _tenantContext.TenantId);
 77: 
 78:         try
 79:         {
 80:             var {entities} = await _dbContext.{Entities}
 81:                 .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
 82:                 .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity1})
 83:                 .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
 84:                 .Include(e => e.Status)
 85:                 .ToListAsync();
 86: 
 87:             // Optional: Set the status of the activity on success.
 88:             activity?.SetStatus(ActivityStatusCode.Ok);
 89: 
 90:             return {entities};
 91:         }
 92:         catch (System.Exception ex)
 93:         {
 94:             // Optional: Set the status of the activity on error.
 95:             activity?.SetStatus(ActivityStatusCode.Error, ex.Message);
 96:             activity?.RecordException(ex);
 97:             throw;
 98:         }
 99:     }
100: 
101:     // ... other repository methods would follow a similar pattern ...
102: }
103: ```
104: 
105: ---
106: 
107: ## 3. Integrating with OpenTelemetry (Conceptual)
108: 
109: To make these custom activities visible, your application's `Program.cs` needs to configure an OpenTelemetry `TracerProvider`. This involves adding instrumentation for ASP.NET Core, Entity Framework Core, and your custom `ActivitySource`.
110: 
111: **File**: `{Project}.API/Program.cs` (Conceptual, requires OpenTelemetry packages)
112: 
113: ```csharp
114: // Example: Add OpenTelemetry packages
115: // <PackageReference Include="OpenTelemetry.Exporter.OpenTelemetryProtocol" Version="..." />
116: // <PackageReference Include="OpenTelemetry.Extensions.Hosting" Version="..." />
117: // <PackageReference Include="OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.AspNetCore" Version="..." />
118: // <PackageReference Include="OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.EntityFrameworkCore" Version="..." />
119: 
120: using OpenTelemetry.Resources;
121: using OpenTelemetry.Trace;
122: using {Project}.Persistence;
123: 
124: var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);
125: 
126: // Configure OpenTelemetry tracing
127: builder.Services.AddOpenTelemetry()
128:     .WithTracing(tracerProviderBuilder =>
129:     {
130:         tracerProviderBuilder
131:             .AddSource(ActivitySourceProvider.PersistenceActivitySource.Name) // ✅ Add your custom ActivitySource
132:             .SetResourceBuilder(
133:                 ResourceBuilder.CreateDefault()
134:                     .AddService(builder.Environment.ApplicationName))
135:             .AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation()
136:             .AddEntityFrameworkCoreInstrumentation()
137:             .AddOtlpExporter(otlpOptions =>
138:             {
139:                 // Configure OTLP exporter to send traces to an OpenTelemetry collector
140:                 // otlpOptions.Endpoint = new Uri("http://localhost:4317");
141:             });
142:     });
143: 
144: // ... rest of Program.cs ...
145: ```
146: 
147: ---
148: 
149: ## 4. Benefits of this Pattern
150: 
151: *   **Granular Performance Insight**: Provides detailed timing information for specific database operations beyond what automatic EF Core instrumentation might offer.
152: *   **Correlation**: Custom spans are automatically correlated with parent HTTP requests, making it easy to trace a user request from the API gateway down to individual database calls.
153: *   **Observability Platform Agnostic**: `ActivitySource` is a standard .NET mechanism that works with any OpenTelemetry-compatible collector and dashboard (e.g., Jaeger, Zipkin, Prometheus, Aspire dashboard).
154: *   **Troubleshooting**: Helps identify slow queries, N+1 problems, or other database-related performance issues.
155: 
156: ---
157: 
158: ## 5. Key Considerations
159: 
160: *   **Automatic EF Core Instrumentation**: OpenTelemetry already provides instrumentation for Entity Framework Core that captures basic database operations. Manual `ActivitySource` spans are useful for grouping multiple EF Core operations or adding custom context.
161: *   **Performance Overhead**: While generally low, adding excessive manual spans can introduce some overhead. Use judiciously for critical paths.
162: *   **Context Propagation**: `ActivitySource` automatically handles context propagation (e.g., `TraceId`, `SpanId`), ensuring that your custom spans are correctly nested within the overall trace.
163: 
164: ---
165: 
166: **Related Resources**:
167: - [api-exception-handling.md](api-exception-handling.md) - Context for overall API observability.
168: - [`dotnet-efcore-guidelines`](../../dotnet-efcore-guidelines/SKILL.md) - General EF Core best practices.
````

## File: .claude/skills/error-tracking/resources/mediatr-logging-behavior.md
````markdown
  1: # MediatR Handler Logging Behavior
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Logging Behavior Patterns**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: This document describes how to implement a logging behavior for MediatR requests using a pipeline behavior. This pattern allows for centralized logging of request processing, providing insight into the application's flow without cluttering individual handlers.
  8: 
  9: ---
 10: 
 11: ## 1. `LoggingBehavior` Implementation
 12: 
 13: Create a class that implements `IPipelineBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>`. This class will intercept all MediatR requests before they are handled and after they complete.
 14: 
 15: **File**: `{Project}.Application/Behaviors/LoggingBehavior.cs`
 16: 
 17: ```csharp
 18: using MediatR;
 19: using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
 20: using System.Threading;
 21: using System.Threading.Tasks;
 22: 
 23: namespace {Project}.Application.Behaviors;
 24: 
 25: /// <summary>
 26: /// MediatR pipeline behavior for logging requests and responses.
 27: /// </summary>
 28: /// <typeparam name="TRequest">The type of the MediatR request.</typeparam>
 29: /// <typeparam name="TResponse">The type of the MediatR response.</typeparam>
 30: public sealed class LoggingBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>(ILogger<LoggingBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>> logger)
 31:     : IPipelineBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>
 32:     where TRequest : IRequest<TResponse>
 33: {
 34:     public async Task<TResponse> Handle(
 35:         TRequest request,
 36:         RequestHandlerDelegate<TResponse> next,
 37:         CancellationToken cancellationToken)
 38:     {
 39:         // Log information BEFORE the request is handled
 40:         logger.LogInformation("Handling MediatR Request: {RequestName} ({RequestType})",
 41:             typeof(TRequest).Name, typeof(TRequest).FullName);
 42: 
 43:         TResponse response;
 44:         try
 45:         {
 46:             // Call the next delegate in the pipeline, which eventually invokes the handler
 47:             response = await next();
 48:         }
 49:         catch (System.Exception ex)
 50:         {
 51:             logger.LogError(ex, "MediatR Request: {RequestName} ({RequestType}) failed with exception: {ErrorMessage}",
 52:                 typeof(TRequest).Name, typeof(TRequest).FullName, ex.Message);
 53:             throw; // Re-throw for higher-level exception handlers
 54:         }
 55: 
 56:         // Log information AFTER the request has been successfully handled
 57:         logger.LogInformation("Handled MediatR Request: {RequestName} ({RequestType}) - Response: {ResponseType}",
 58:             typeof(TRequest).Name, typeof(TRequest).FullName, typeof(TResponse).Name);
 59: 
 60:         return response;
 61:     }
 62: }
 63: ```
 64: 
 65: ---
 66: 
 67: ## 2. Registering the Behavior
 68: 
 69: The `LoggingBehavior` needs to be registered with MediatR in the application's `Program.cs` file.
 70: 
 71: **File**: `{Project}.API/Program.cs` (or `{Project}.Blazor/Program.cs` if using MediatR in Blazor)
 72: 
 73: ```csharp
 74: using MediatR;
 75: using {Project}.Application.Behaviors;
 76: 
 77: var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);
 78: 
 79: // Add MediatR services to the DI container
 80: builder.Services.AddMediatR(cfg => {
 81:     // Register the assembly containing your handlers and requests
 82:     cfg.RegisterServicesFromAssembly(typeof({Project}.Application.ApplicationServicesRegistration).Assembly);
 83: 
 84:     // Register the LoggingBehavior as a pipeline behavior
 85:     cfg.AddBehavior(typeof(IPipelineBehavior<,>), typeof(LoggingBehavior<,>));
 86: });
 87: ```
 88: 
 89: ---
 90: 
 91: ## 3. Benefits of this Pattern
 92: 
 93: *   **Centralized Logging**: All request processing logs are consolidated in one place, making it easier to track the flow of operations.
 94: *   **Decoupled Concerns**: Handlers remain clean, focusing solely on business logic, while logging is handled by the pipeline.
 95: *   **Debugging and Monitoring**: Provides a clear audit trail of what requests are being processed and their outcomes, aiding in debugging and monitoring.
 96: *   **Error Visibility**: Catches and logs exceptions at the pipeline level, ensuring that any unhandled errors during request processing are recorded.
 97: 
 98: ---
 99: 
100: ## 4. Key Considerations
101: 
102: *   **Performance**: While generally efficient, be mindful of what you log within the behavior. Logging large request/response objects can impact performance and log storage.
103: *   **Sensitive Data**: Be cautious about logging sensitive data from requests or responses. Implement redaction or filtering if necessary.
104: *   **Error Handling Flow**: Exceptions caught in the behavior are re-thrown (`throw;`). This is crucial to ensure they propagate to higher-level exception handlers (like `UseExceptionHandler` in the API) for a consistent error response to the client.
105: 
106: ---
107: 
108: **Related Resources**:
109: - [api-exception-handling.md](api-exception-handling.md) - How exceptions caught by this behavior are eventually handled by the API.
110: - [`cqrs-mediatr-guidelines`](../../cqrs-mediatr-guidelines/SKILL.md) - General MediatR guidelines.
````

## File: .claude/skills/error-tracking/resources/sentry-middleware-config.md
````markdown
  1: # Sentry Middleware Configuration (Conceptual)
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Sentry Integration Patterns**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: This document provides conceptual guidance on integrating Sentry into ASP.NET Core applications. This integration aims to automatically capture exceptions, log messages, and collect performance data.
  8: 
  9: ---
 10: 
 11: ## 1. Sentry Integration in `Program.cs`
 12: 
 13: Sentry integration typically involves configuring the Sentry SDK early in your application's `Program.cs` file. This setup enables automatic error capturing and performance monitoring for your ASP.NET Core application.
 14: 
 15: **File**: `{Project}.API/Program.cs` (or `{Project}.Blazor/Program.cs` for Blazor Server)
 16: 
 17: ```csharp
 18: // Example: Add Sentry NuGet packages
 19: // <PackageReference Include="Sentry.AspNetCore" Version="4.0.0" />
 20: // <PackageReference Include="Sentry.Extensions.Logging" Version="4.0.0" />
 21: // <PackageReference Include="Sentry.Serilog" Version="4.0.0" /> // If using Serilog
 22: 
 23: using Sentry;
 24: using Sentry.AspNetCore;
 25: 
 26: var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);
 27: 
 28: // ✅ Configure Sentry for the Web Host
 29: builder.WebHost.UseSentry(options =>
 30: {
 31:     // Configure your DSN (Data Source Name) - this is crucial!
 32:     options.Dsn = builder.Configuration["Sentry:Dsn"];
 33: 
 34:     // Set the application environment
 35:     options.Environment = builder.Environment.EnvironmentName;
 36: 
 37:     // Set the release version for better tracking in Sentry
 38:     // options.Release = "my-app@1.0.0";
 39: 
 40:     // Performance Monitoring configuration
 41:     options.TracesSampleRate = 0.1;
 42:     options.ProfilesSampleRate = 0.1;
 43: 
 44:     // Optional: Enable automatic session tracking
 45:     options.AutoSessionTracking = true;
 46: 
 47:     // Optional: Enables Sentry to capture more global context
 48:     options.IsGlobalModeEnabled = true;
 49: 
 50:     // Optional: Custom filtering or data modification before sending to Sentry
 51:     options.BeforeSend = (sentryEvent) =>
 52:     {
 53:         // ✅ Remove sensitive information from HTTP request headers
 54:         if (sentryEvent.Request?.Headers != null)
 55:         {
 56:             sentryEvent.Request.Headers.Remove("Authorization");
 57:             sentryEvent.Request.Headers.Remove("Cookie");
 58:         }
 59: 
 60:         return sentryEvent;
 61:     };
 62: });
 63: 
 64: var app = builder.Build();
 65: 
 66: // ✅ Add Sentry middleware EARLY in the pipeline for comprehensive tracking
 67: app.UseSentryTracing();
 68: app.UseSentryTracing().UseSentryRequestErrorCatching();
 69: 
 70: // ... rest of your application's middleware pipeline ...
 71: ```
 72: 
 73: ---
 74: 
 75: ## 2. Using `SentrySdk` Directly
 76: 
 77: For manual error capturing, adding custom context, or performance monitoring outside of standard HTTP requests, you can use the `SentrySdk` static class directly.
 78: 
 79: ### Capturing Exceptions
 80: 
 81: ```csharp
 82: using Sentry;
 83: 
 84: try
 85: {
 86:     // ... code that might throw an exception ...
 87:     throw new InvalidOperationException("Something bad happened!");
 88: }
 89: catch (Exception ex)
 90: {
 91:     // ✅ Capture the exception to Sentry
 92:     SentrySdk.CaptureException(ex, scope =>
 93:     {
 94:         // ✅ Add additional context to the error report
 95:         scope.User = new User { Id = "user-123", Email = "user@example.com" };
 96:         scope.SetTag("feature", "{entity}-creation");
 97:         scope.SetTag("tenant_id", "tenant-abc");
 98:         scope.SetContext("request_data", new { Title = "My {Entity}", UserAgent = "..." });
 99:         scope.Level = SentryLevel.Error;
100:     });
101:     throw;
102: }
103: ```
104: 
105: ### Capturing Messages
106: 
107: ```csharp
108: using Sentry;
109: 
110: // ✅ Capture an informational message
111: SentrySdk.CaptureMessage("User logged in successfully.", SentryLevel.Info);
112: 
113: // ✅ Capture a warning message
114: SentrySdk.CaptureMessage("Low disk space warning on server.", SentryLevel.Warning);
115: ```
116: 
117: ### Manual Performance Transactions and Spans
118: 
119: For background jobs or specific code blocks where you want to track performance, you can create manual Sentry transactions and spans.
120: 
121: ```csharp
122: using Sentry;
123: 
124: public class BackgroundSyncService
125: {
126:     public async Task SyncDataAsync()
127:     {
128:         // ✅ Start a new Sentry transaction for the background operation
129:         var transaction = SentrySdk.StartTransaction("background.job.sync_{entities}", "sync");
130:         transaction.Description = "Synchronizing {entities} from external API";
131: 
132:         try
133:         {
134:             // ✅ Start a child span for a specific part of the operation
135:             var fetchSpan = transaction.StartChild("http.client", "fetch_external_{entities}");
136:             try
137:             {
138:                 await Task.Delay(500);
139:                 fetchSpan.SetTag("http.url", "https://external.api/{entities}");
140:                 fetchSpan.SetTag("http.method", "GET");
141:             }
142:             finally
143:             {
144:                 fetchSpan.Finish(SpanStatus.Ok);
145:             }
146: 
147:             var dbSpan = transaction.StartChild("db.query", "save_{entities}_to_db");
148:             try
149:             {
150:                 await Task.Delay(800);
151:             }
152:             finally
153:             {
154:                 dbSpan.Finish(SpanStatus.Ok);
155:             }
156: 
157:             transaction.Status = SpanStatus.Ok;
158:         }
159:         catch (Exception ex)
160:         {
161:             transaction.Status = SpanStatus.InternalError;
162:             transaction.SetTag("error", "true");
163:             SentrySdk.CaptureException(ex, scope => scope.Transaction = transaction);
164:             throw;
165:         }
166:         finally
167:         {
168:             transaction.Finish();
169:         }
170:     }
171: }
172: ```
173: 
174: ---
175: 
176: ## 3. Configuration (from `appsettings.json`)
177: 
178: Sentry settings are typically managed through `appsettings.json`, allowing easy modification across environments.
179: 
180: ```json
181: {
182:   "Sentry": {
183:     "Dsn": "https://your-public-key@o000000.ingest.sentry.io/0000000",
184:     "Environment": "Development",
185:     "Release": "1.0.0",
186:     "Debug": false,
187:     "DiagnosticLevel": "Error",
188:     "TracesSampleRate": 1.0,
189:     "ProfilesSampleRate": 1.0,
190:     "SendDefaultPii": false,
191:     "AttachStackTraces": true
192:   }
193: }
194: ```
195: 
196: ---
197: 
198: ## 4. NuGet Packages
199: 
200: Ensure the necessary Sentry NuGet packages are installed in the relevant projects.
201: 
202: ### `{Project}.API`
203: ```xml
204: <PackageReference Include="Sentry.AspNetCore" Version="4.0.0" />
205: <PackageReference Include="Sentry.Extensions.Logging" Version="4.0.0" />
206: ```
207: 
208: ### `{Project}.Blazor` (for Blazor Server)
209: ```xml
210: <PackageReference Include="Sentry.AspNetCore" Version="4.0.0" />
211: <PackageReference Include="Sentry.Extensions.Logging" Version="4.0.0" />
212: ```
213: 
214: ### `{Project}.Blazor.Client` (for Blazor WebAssembly)
215: ```xml
216: <PackageReference Include="Sentry.Blazor.WebAssembly" Version="4.0.0" />
217: <PackageReference Include="Sentry.Extensions.Logging" Version="4.0.0" />
218: ```
219: 
220: ### `{Project}.Application` (Optional, if using `SentrySdk` for business logic exceptions)
221: ```xml
222: <PackageReference Include="Sentry" Version="4.0.0" />
223: ```
224: 
225: ---
226: 
227: ## 5. Key Considerations
228: 
229: *   **Sensitive Data**: Always be mindful of sensitive data (PII, secrets, tokens) and configure `BeforeSend` to strip it from payloads.
230: *   **Performance Overhead**: While Sentry is optimized, capturing too many transactions or very large payloads can introduce overhead. Adjust `TracesSampleRate` and `ProfilesSampleRate` based on your performance needs.
231: *   **Error Reporting Discipline**: Ensure that exceptions are logged and reported consistently, preferably through the centralized exception handler. Avoid swallowing errors silently.
232: *   **Sentry DSN**: The DSN is your project's unique identifier in Sentry. It must be kept secret and should not be committed to source control directly (use environment variables or secret management).
233: 
234: ---
235: 
236: **Related Resources**:
237: - [api-exception-handling.md](api-exception-handling.md) - Context for how Sentry can integrate with centralized API error handling.
238: - [db-performance-monitoring.md](db-performance-monitoring.md) - How Sentry can complement OpenTelemetry for database performance.
239: - [`blazor-error-boundary.md`](blazor-error-boundary.md) - How Sentry can capture errors caught by Blazor's `ErrorBoundary`.
````

117: - `Explore.Blazor.Client/Components/Event/IslamicAspectEditDialog.razor` - NEW
118: - `Explore.Blazor.Client/Components/Event/TechAspectEditDialog.razor` - NEW
119: 
120: **Generated Client:**
121: - `Explore.Blazor.Client/Clients/EventApiClient.g.cs` - NSwag generated (DO NOT EDIT DIRECTLY)
122: 
123: ---
124: 
125: ## Key Decisions Made
126: 
127: ### 1. HATEOAS Consumption Strategy
128: 
129: **Decision**: Wrap existing NSwag client with link-aware layer
130: 
131: **Rationale**:
132: - Preserves type safety from NSwag generation
133: - Minimal changes to existing code
134: - Links can be parsed from raw responses
135: 
136: **Alternative Rejected**: Replace NSwag with custom HttpClient (too disruptive)
137: 
138: ### 2. Aspect UI Location
139: 
140: **Decision**: Aspects shown as expandable cards in EventDetail
141: 
142: **Rationale**:
143: - Follows existing section pattern (`.event-detail__section-card`)
144: - Non-intrusive - collapses when not relevant
145: - Edit via dialogs matches Organization pattern
146: 
147: **Alternative Rejected**: Separate aspect pages (too fragmented)
148: 
149: ### 3. Aspect Edit Pattern
150: 
151: **Decision**: MudDialog pattern for aspect editing
152: 
153: **Rationale**:
154: - Consistent with existing dialogs (EditSessionDialog, ReviewDialog)
155: - No page navigation required
156: - Good for optional data
157: 
158: ### 4. Priority Order
159: 
160: **Decision**: Event Aspects (Phases 2-3) before HATEOAS (Phase 1)
161: 
162: **Rationale**:
163: - Aspects provide immediate user value
164: - HATEOAS is infrastructure improvement, can defer
165: - Aspects use existing NSwag client patterns
166: 
167: ---
168: 
169: ## Technical Constraints
170: 
171: ### NSwag Generated Client
172: 
173: The `EventApiClient.g.cs` is auto-generated. Changes to this file will be overwritten.
174: 
175: **Workaround**:
176: - Create wrapper services that add functionality
177: - Do NOT modify `*.g.cs` files directly
178: - If API changes, regenerate client: `dotnet nswag run`
179: 
180: ### Enum Synchronization
181: 
182: Enums must match between API and Blazor:
183: - `SkillLevel` (AllLevels=0, Beginner=1, Intermediate=2, Advanced=3)
184: - `PrayerTime` (Fajr=1, Sunrise=2, Dhuhr=3, Asr=4, Maghrib=5, Isha=6)
185: - `GenderSegregationMode` (Mixed=0, MenOnly=1, WomenOnly=2, Segregated=3, Family=4)
186: 
187: **Action**: Verify enums exist in NSwag client or create manual copies in Phase 6
188: 
189: ### BFF Pattern
190: 
191: Blazor communicates with API through BFF (Backend-for-Frontend):
192: - `BffClient.cs` handles token forwarding
193: - `BrowserCredentialsMessageHandler.cs` adds credentials
194: - YARP proxies `/api/*` to actual API
195: 
196: **Impact**: HATEOAS links returned from API will have correct BFF paths
197: 
198: ---
199:

205: 2. **Read the plan**: `blazor-api-sync-plan.md` - Full 7-phase plan
206: 3. **Check tasks file**: `blazor-api-sync-tasks.md` - Checkable task list

212: 2. **Phase 4**: Create flow integration - Medium
213: 3. **Phase 1 & 5**: HATEOAS foundation - Can be deferred
214: 4. **Phase 6 & 7**: Lookups and polish - Low priority

 54: ## Important Decisions
 55: 
 56: 1. **net10.0 upgrade is Phase 1** because .NET 10 provides 76% smaller blazor.web.js, WasmStripILAfterAOT, [PersistentState], ParameterState<T>, and other optimizations that later phases depend on.

 59: 
 60: 3. **Virtualize only where appropriate** - Not all 46 @foreach loops need virtualization. Only lists that can grow beyond ~50 items with uniform height.
 61: 
 62: 4. **Conservative caching** - Client-side cache TTLs should be short (30s-2min) with explicit invalidation on write operations to avoid stale data.
 63:

 66: ## Technical Constraints
 67: 
 68: - **BFF Pattern**: Blazor Server proxies all API calls via YARP. Client-side caching must work at the HttpClient level in WASM, not at the BFF level.

## File: dev/active/s3-storage-abstraction/s3-storage-abstraction-context.md
````markdown
  1: # S3 Object Storage Abstraction - Context
  2: 
  3: ## SESSION PROGRESS (2026-02-11)
  4: 
  5: ### Completed
  6: - Full research of current S3 implementation (all files read and analyzed)
  7: - Web research on S3-compatible providers, multi-tenant patterns, credential storage
  8: - Codebase exploration agent completed with comprehensive gap analysis
  9: - Plan document created with 7 phases
 10: - Research report on private/public buckets, archive tiers, WASM/SSR considerations
 11: - Context and tasks files created
 12: - Phase 1: Created `S3Configuration` POCO and `IS3ConfigResolver` interface
 13: - Phase 2: Added 8 S3 governance setting keys to `GovernanceSettingKeys.cs`
 14: - Phase 3: Added 8 seed IDs (0530-0537) and 8 SystemSetting seed entries
 15: - Phase 4: Implemented `S3ConfigResolver` in `Infrastructure/Storage/`
 16: - Phase 5: Refactored `ObjectStorageService` to use `IS3ConfigResolver`, updated DI, added `TestConnectionAsync`, updated `GeneratePresignedDownloadUrl` to `Task<string>` and all 15 callers
 17: - Phase 6: Created 13 unit tests in `S3ConfigResolverTests.cs` — all 203 app unit tests pass
 18: - Phase 7: Updated `CODEBASE_STRUCTURE.md`, updated dev docs
 19: 
 20: ### Blockers
 21: - None
 22: 
 23: ---
 24: 
 25: ## Key Decisions
 26: 
 27: 1. **Mirror email pattern exactly** — Same architecture as SmtpConfigResolver (ISettingsResolver cascade, IMemoryCache, per-tenant resolution)
 28: 2. **Keep IObjectStorageService interface unchanged** — All 23+ consumer files don't need changes
 29: 3. **No public bucket support** — Private + presigned URLs is sufficient (YAGNI)
 30: 4. **No archive tiers** — Not supported by all providers; premature optimization
 31: 5. **ForcePathStyle defaults to true** — Required by most non-AWS providers (Hetzner, MinIO, B2, R2)
 32: 6. **Cache IAmazonS3 client per tenant in resolver** — Avoid creating TCP connections per request
 33: 7. **Keep env var bootstrap** — S3Settings.cs stays during transition; env vars populate initial seed data
 34: 8. **S3 seed IDs use range 0530-0537** — After email range 0520-0528
 35: 
 36: ## Key Files
 37: 
 38: ### Current Implementation (To Be Refactored)
 39: 
 40: **`Explore.Infrastructure/Services/ObjectStorageService.cs`**
 41: - Main S3 service implementation
 42: - Uses singleton `IAmazonS3` client + `IOptions<S3Settings>`
 43: - Has `_presignClient` for PublicEndpoint presigned URLs
 44: - Hardcoded 40-min upload URL expiration
 45: - **Will be refactored** to use `IS3ConfigResolver` instead
 46: 
 47: **`Explore.Infrastructure/S3Settings.cs`**
 48: - Simple 6-property POCO (Region, BucketName, AccessKeyId, SecretAccessKey, Endpoint, PublicEndpoint)
 49: - Located in Infrastructure layer (should be Application for Clean Architecture)
 50: - **Will be superseded** by `S3Configuration` in Application/Models but kept for env var bootstrap
 51: 
 52: **`Explore.Infrastructure/InfrastructureServicesRegistration.cs`** (lines 29-78)
 53: - Singleton `IAmazonS3` client factory with complex endpoint logic
 54: - Transient `IObjectStorageService` registration
 55: - **Will be simplified** to scoped `IS3ConfigResolver` + scoped service
 56: 
 57: **`Explore.Application/Contracts/Infrastructure/IObjectStorageService.cs`**
 58: - 3 methods: GeneratePresignedUploadUrl, GeneratePresignedDownloadUrl, GetFileStream
 59: - **Minor change**: Add `TestConnectionAsync` method
 60: 
 61: ### Reference Pattern (Email — Already Implemented)
 62: 
 63: **`Explore.Infrastructure/Mail/SmtpConfigResolver.cs`**
 64: - The exact pattern to replicate for S3
 65: - Uses `ISettingsResolver`, `ITenantContext`, `IMemoryCache`
 66: - 5-min cache with `SmtpConfig:{tenantId}` key
 67: - Returns null if host is empty → S3 equivalent: return null if endpoint is empty
 68: 
 69: **`Explore.Application/Contracts/Infrastructure/ISmtpConfigResolver.cs`**
 70: - Interface: `ResolveAsync()` + `InvalidateCache(Guid?)`
 71: - S3 will have identical interface shape
 72: 
 73: **`Explore.Application/Models/SmtpConfiguration.cs`**
 74: - Clean POCO with all config properties
 75: - S3 equivalent will have: Region, BucketName, AccessKeyId, SecretAccessKey, Endpoint, PublicEndpoint, ForcePathStyle, UploadUrlExpirationMinutes
 76: 
 77: **`Explore.Domain/Constants/GovernanceSettingKeys.cs`**
 78: - Has email keys (Email*) at the bottom
 79: - S3 keys will be added in new section below email
 80: 
 81: **`Explore.Persistence/Seed/SeedIds.cs`**
 82: - Email IDs: 0520-0528
 83: - S3 IDs: 0530-0537
 84: 
 85: **`Explore.Persistence/Seed/LookupTableSeeder.cs`**
 86: - Contains `SeedSystemSettings()` method with all SystemSetting entries
 87: - S3 entries will be added at the end with Category = "ObjectStorage"
 88: 
 89: ### Consumers (No Changes Needed)
 90: 
 91: - `StorageObjectController.cs` — API endpoints
 92: - 4 CQRS handlers in `Features/StorageObjects/Handlers/`
 93: - `ImageStorageService.cs` — Blazor client
 94: - `StorageObjectRepository.cs` — persistence
 95: 
 96: ### Test Files (To Be Created)
 97: 
 98: - `Event.Application.UnitTests/Infrastructure/S3ConfigResolverTests.cs` — new
 99: 
100: ## Provider Compatibility Notes
101: 
102: - **Hetzner** (current): `ServiceURL=https://fsn1.your-objectstorage.com`, ForcePathStyle=true, AuthenticationRegion="fsn1"
103: - **MinIO** (Docker dev): `ServiceURL=http://localhost:9000`, ForcePathStyle=true
104: - **AWS S3**: Use `RegionEndpoint` (not ServiceURL), ForcePathStyle=false
105: - **Critical**: Never set both `ServiceURL` and `RegionEndpoint` — throws `AmazonClientException`
106: 
107: ## Quick Resume
108: 
109: To continue:
110: 1. Read this file for current state
111: 2. Read `s3-storage-abstraction-tasks.md` for checklist
112: 3. Start with Phase 1 (Application layer)
113: 4. Build after each phase to catch errors early
114: 5. Run tests after Phase 6
115: ## Context Reset Session Update (2026-02-15 21:25 Europe/Brussels)
116: 
117: - Current implementation state: No new implementation changes in this session for this track.
118: - Key decisions made this session: Priority shifted to analytics implementation completion and verification.
119: - Files modified and why: None in this track during this session.
120: - Blockers/issues discovered: None newly discovered for this track.
121: - Next immediate steps: Continue from highest-priority unchecked items in `s3-storage-abstraction-tasks.md`.
````

225: ## Domain Model Summary
226: 
227: ### Core Entities
228: 
229: | Entity | Purpose | Relationships |
230: |--------|---------|---------------|
231: | `Event` | Primary aggregate | EventSessions, Categories, Tags, Location |
232: | `EventSession` | Session within event | AgendaItems, Speakers, Languages |
233: | `Organization` | Event organizer | Members, Reviews, Events |
234: | `Actor` | People/groups | Can be User or external |
235: | `Location` | Physical/virtual venues | Events |
236: | `Category` | Event categorization | Events (many-to-many) |
237: | `Tag` | Flexible tagging | Events (many-to-many) |
238: 
239: ### Lookup Tables
240: 
241: `EventType` • `EventStatus` • `EventFormat` • `AudienceAge` • `AudienceGender` • `Madhab` • `Language` • `ActorType` • `ApprovalStatus` • `VisibilityType` • `RegistrationMode` • `Role` • `OrganizationPosition` • `FileType` • `TagType` • `DidCustodyType`
242: 
243: ### Multi-Tenancy
244: 
245: All entities implement `ITenantEntity` with `TenantId` for data isolation:
246: - `Tenant` - Tenant configuration
247: - `TenantSettings` - Per-tenant settings
248: - `TenantUser` - User-tenant membership
249: 
250: **See**: [MULTI_TENANCY.md](MULTI_TENANCY.md) for the complete tenant isolation model, and [ADMIN_HIERARCHY.md](ADMIN_HIERARCHY.md) for the authority model.
251: 
252: ### Federation (ATProto)
253: 
254: - `IndexedDid` - Indexed DIDs from network
255: - `AtprotoRecord` - Federated records
256: - `ActorKeyStore` - Cryptographic keys
257: - `SyncState` - Synchronization tracking
258:

  1: # Naming Conventions
  2: 
  3: > Comprehensive naming patterns used across the codebase.
  4: > Follow these exactly when creating new files, classes, or members.
  5: > Last Updated: February 2026
  6: 
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: ## Project Naming
 10: 
 11: | Project | Pattern | Purpose |
 12: |---|---|---|
 13: | `Explore.Domain` | `Explore.{Layer}` | Core domain entities |
 14: | `Explore.Application` | `Explore.{Layer}` | Business logic / CQRS |
 15: | `Explore.Persistence` | `Explore.{Layer}` | Data access / EF Core |
 16: | `Explore.Infrastructure` | `Explore.{Layer}` | External services |
 17: | `Explore.API` | `Explore.{Layer}` | Web API host |
 18: | `Explore.Blazor` | `Explore.Blazor` | Blazor Server host |
 19: | `Explore.Blazor.Client` | `Explore.Blazor.Client` | Blazor WASM client |
 20: | `Explore.Secrets` | `Explore.{Library}` | Standalone library |
 21: | `Event.Application.UnitTests` | `Event.{Layer}.{TestType}` | Test projects (legacy "Event" prefix) |
 22: | `Event.Architecture.Tests` | `Event.Architecture.Tests` | Architecture fitness tests |
 23: 
 24: **Note:** Main projects use the `Explore.*` prefix (historical naming, will be renamed to `Event.*` in the future). Test projects already use `Event.*` prefix.
 25: 
 26: ---
 27: 
 28: ## File Naming
 29: 
 30: All source files use **PascalCase** matching the primary class/type name:
 31: 
 32: | File type | Pattern | Example |
 33: |---|---|---|
 34: | Entity | `{EntityName}.cs` | `Event.cs`, `Organization.cs` |
 35: | Enum | `{EntityName}Enum.cs` | `EventTypeEnum.cs`, `EventStatusEnum.cs` |
 36: | Interface | `I{Name}.cs` | `IEventRepository.cs`, `ITenantContext.cs` |
 37: | DTO | `{Prefix}{EntityName}Dto.cs` | `CreateEventDto.cs`, `EventListDto.cs` |
 38: | Command | `{Verb}{EntityName}Command.cs` | `CreateEventCommand.cs` |
 39: | Query | `Get{EntityName}{Suffix}Request.cs` | `GetEventListRequest.cs` |
 40: | Handler | `{CommandOrQuery}Handler.cs` | `CreateEventCommandHandler.cs` |
 41: | Repository interface | `I{EntityName}Repository.cs` | `IEventRepository.cs` |
 42: | Repository implementation | `{EntityName}Repository.cs` | `EventRepository.cs` |
 43: | EF Configuration | `{EntityName}Configuration.cs` | `EventConfiguration.cs` |
 44: | Controller | `{EntityName}Controller.cs` | `EventController.cs` |
 45: | Blazor page | `{PageName}.razor` + `{PageName}.razor.cs` | `EventList.razor` |
 46: | Blazor CSS | `{PageName}.razor.css` | `EventList.razor.css` |
 47: | Client service | `{EntityName}Service.cs` | `EventService.cs` |
 48: | Validator | `{Prefix}{EntityName}DtoValidator.cs` | `CreateEventDtoValidator.cs` |
 49: 
 50: ---
 51: 
 52: ## Namespace Conventions
 53: 
 54: **File-scoped namespaces** are required (C# 10+ style):
 55: 
 56: ```
 57: namespace Explore.Application.Features.Events.Handlers.Commands;
 58: ```
 59: 
 60: Namespace structure mirrors folder structure exactly:
 61: 
 62: | Layer | Namespace |
 63: |---|---|
 64: | Domain entities | `Explore.Domain` |
 65: | Domain enums | `Explore.Domain.Enums` |
 66: | Domain interfaces | `Explore.Domain.Interfaces` |
 67: | Application DTOs | `Explore.Application.DTOs.{EntityName}` |
 68: | Application features | `Explore.Application.Features.{EntityNames}.Handlers.{Commands\|Queries}` |
 69: | Application requests | `Explore.Application.Features.{EntityNames}.Requests.{Commands\|Queries}` |
 70: | Application contracts | `Explore.Application.Contracts.{Persistence\|Infrastructure\|Identity}` |
 71: | Persistence repos | `Explore.Persistence.Repositories` |
 72: | Persistence configs | `Explore.Persistence.Configurations.Entities` |
 73: | API controllers | `Explore.API.Controllers` |
 74: | API services | `Explore.API.Services` |
 75: | Blazor client services | `Explore.Blazor.Client.Services` |
 76: | Blazor client pages | `Explore.Blazor.Client.Pages.{Area}` |
 77: 
 78: ---
 79: 
 80: ## Entity Naming
 81: 
 82: ### Primary Entities (Guid PK)
 83: 
 84: Singular noun, PascalCase. One class per file at `Explore.Domain/` root.
 85: 
 86: - `Event`, `Organization`, `Actor`, `User`, `Tenant`, `Location`, `StorageObject`, `Category`, `Tag`
 87: 
 88: ### Lookup Tables (int PK)
 89: 
 90: Singular noun. These are reference data that rarely changes.
 91: 
 92: - `EventType`, `EventStatus`, `EventFormat`, `AudienceAge`, `AudienceGender`
 93: - `Madhab`, `Language`, `VisibilityType`, `RegistrationMode`
 94: - `Role`, `OrganizationPosition`, `ActorType`, `FileType`, `DidCustodyType`
 95: 
 96: ### Link/Junction Tables (Composite PK)
 97: 
 98: Named as `{Parent}{Child}` (plural for many-to-many collections):
 99: 
100: - `EventCategories` — Event ↔ Category
101: - `EventTags` — Event ↔ Tag
102: - `EventSessionLanguage` — EventSession ↔ Language
103: - `EventSessionSpeaker` — EventSession ↔ Speaker (User)
104: - `TagTypeTags` — TagType ↔ Tag
105: - `OrganizationMember` — Organization ↔ User (with Role via `RoleId`)
106: - `TenantUser` — Tenant ↔ User (with Role via `RoleId`)
107: - `RolePermission` — Role ↔ Permission
108: 
109: **Note:** Some junction table names are plural (`EventCategories`, `EventTags`) while others are singular (`OrganizationMember`, `EventSessionLanguage`). Follow the existing pattern when extending.
110: 
111: ### Aspect Tables (1:1 Optional Extension)
112: 
113: Named as `{Parent}{Module}Aspect`:
114: 
115: - `EventIslamicAspect` — Islamic-specific fields for Event
116: - `EventTechAspect` — Tech-specific fields for Event
117: 
118: ### Settings Entities
119: 
120: - `SystemSetting` — Instance-wide settings (global)
121: - `TenantSetting` — Per-tenant setting overrides
122: - `TenantSettings` — Tenant settings snapshot entity (different from TenantSetting)
123: - `AppSetting` — Application-level settings
124: 
125: ---
126: 
127: ## Enum Naming
128: 
129: Enums are named `{EntityName}Enum` and placed in `Explore.Domain/Enums/`. They mirror the int IDs used in lookup tables:
130: 
131: ```
132: EventTypeEnum.cs       → values: Conference = 1, Workshop = 2, ...
133: EventStatusEnum.cs     → values: Draft = 1, Published = 2, ...
134: AudienceAgeEnum.cs     → values: AllAges = 1, Children = 2, ...
135: ```
136: 
137: Each enum value maps to a lookup table row's int `Id`.
138: 
139: ---
140: 
141: ## DTO Naming
142: 
143: DTOs follow a strict prefix/suffix pattern per entity:
144: 
145: | DTO Purpose | Pattern | Example |
146: |---|---|---|
147: | Full details (read) | `{EntityName}Dto` | `EventDto`, `OrganizationDto` |
148: | List view (read) | `{EntityName}ListDto` | `EventListDto`, `OrganizationListDto` |
149: | Create payload (write) | `Create{EntityName}Dto` | `CreateEventDto` |
150: | Update payload (write) | `Update{EntityName}Dto` | `UpdateEventDto` |
151: 
152: DTOs live in `Explore.Application/DTOs/{EntityName}/` — one folder per entity, all DTOs for that entity in the same folder.
153: 
154: ---
155: 
156: ## CQRS Naming
157: 
158: ### Commands (Write Operations)
159: 
160: | Component | Pattern | Example |
161: |---|---|---|
162: | Command request | `{Verb}{EntityName}Command` | `CreateEventCommand` |
163: | Command handler | `{Verb}{EntityName}CommandHandler` | `CreateEventCommandHandler` |
164: 
165: Common verbs: `Create`, `Update`, `Delete`, `Add`, `Remove`
166: 
167: ### Queries (Read Operations)
168: 
169: | Component | Pattern | Example |
170: |---|---|---|
171: | Query request | `Get{EntityName}{Suffix}Request` | `GetEventListRequest`, `GetEventDetailsRequest` |
172: | Query handler | `Get{EntityName}{Suffix}RequestHandler` | `GetEventListRequestHandler` |
173: 
174: Common suffixes: `List`, `Details`, `ById`, `By{RelatedEntity}`
175: 
176: ### Folder Structure
177: 
178: Features are pluralized: `Events/`, `Organizations/`, `AudienceAges/`
179: 
180: ```
181: Features/{EntityNames}/
182: ├── Requests/
183: │   ├── Commands/    — {Verb}{EntityName}Command.cs
184: │   └── Queries/     — Get{EntityName}{Suffix}Request.cs
185: └── Handlers/
186:     ├── Commands/    — {Verb}{EntityName}CommandHandler.cs
187:     └── Queries/     — Get{EntityName}{Suffix}RequestHandler.cs
188: ```
189: 
190: ---
191: 
192: ## Repository Naming
193: 
194: | Component | Pattern | Example |
195: |---|---|---|
196: | Interface | `I{EntityName}Repository` | `IEventRepository` |
197: | Implementation | `{EntityName}Repository` | `EventRepository` |
198: | Generic base | `IGenericRepository<T, TKey>` | `GenericRepository<T, TKey>` |
199: 
200: Interfaces in: `Explore.Application/Contracts/Persistence/`
201: Implementations in: `Explore.Persistence/Repositories/`
202: 
203: ---
204: 
205: ## Controller Naming
206: 
207: Controllers are named `{EntityName}Controller` and placed in `Explore.API/Controllers/`. They map 1:1 with domain aggregates:
208: 
209: | Controller | Route |
210: |---|---|
211: | `EventController` | `api/event` |
212: | `OrganizationController` | `api/organization` |
213: | `EventSessionController` | `api/eventsession` |
214: 
215: Route convention: `api/[controller]` (controller name lowercased, no hyphens).
216: 
217: ---
218: 
219: ## Blazor Page Naming
220: 
221: Pages use PascalCase and are organized by area:
222: 
223: | Area | Page pattern | Example |
224: |---|---|---|
225: | Event pages | `Pages/Event/{Action}.razor` | `EventList.razor`, `CreateEvent.razor` |
226: | Organization | `Pages/Organization/{Action}.razor` | `OrganizationDetails.razor` |
227: | Admin | `Pages/Admin/{Area}.razor` | `LookupTables.razor` |
228: 
229: Each page has a code-behind: `{PageName}.razor.cs` (partial class).
230: Optional scoped CSS: `{PageName}.razor.css`.
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: ## Service Naming (Blazor Client)
235: 
236: Client services follow `{EntityName}Service` with interface `I{EntityName}Service`:
237: 
238: | Service | Purpose |
239: |---|---|
240: | `EventService` / `IEventService` | Event API calls |
241: | `OrganizationService` / `IOrganizationService` | Organization API calls |
242: | `LookupCacheService` / `ILookupCacheService` | Caches lookup table data |
243: | `AuthStateService` / `IAuthStateService` | Centralized auth state |
244: | `BffClient` | Low-level BFF HTTP calls with XSRF |
245: | `ImageStorageService` / `IImageStorageService` | S3 presigned URL uploads |
246: 
247: ---
248: 
249: ## Database Column Naming
250: 
251: EF Core is configured with **snake_case naming convention** (via `UseSnakeCaseNamingConvention()`):
252: 
253: | C# Property | Database Column |
254: |---|---|
255: | `EventTypeId` | `event_type_id` |
256: | `CreatedAt` | `created_at` |
257: | `IsDeleted` | `is_deleted` |
258: | `TenantId` | `tenant_id` |
259: 
260: Table names are also snake_case plurals of the entity name.
261: 
262: ---
263: 
264: ## Seed Data ID Conventions
265: 
266: - **Lookup tables** (int PK): IDs defined in enum files, seeded via `HasData()` in EF configurations
267: - **Main entities** (Guid PK): IDs defined in `SeedIds.cs` using deterministic **UUIDv7** format
268: - UUIDv7 pattern: `018e4e5c-xxxx-7xxx-8xxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx` (time-ordered, unique per entity type)
269: - Seed IDs must never change once used in production
270: 
271: ---
272: 
273: ## Test Naming
274: 
275: ### Test Projects
276: 
277: | Project | Test type | Framework |
278: |---|---|---|
279: | `Event.Application.UnitTests` | Unit | TUnit |
280: | `Event.Domain.UnitTests` | Unit | TUnit |
281: | `Event.Architecture.Tests` | Architecture | TUnit |
282: | `Event.Persistence.IntegrationTests` | Integration | TUnit |
283: | `Event.API.IntegrationTests` | Integration | TUnit |
284: | `Explore.Blazor.Client.Tests` | Component | bUnit + TUnit |
285: | `Explore.Secrets.UnitTests` | Unit | TUnit |
286: 
287: ### Test Class Naming
288: 
289: Test classes mirror the class under test with a `Tests` suffix:
290: 
291: - `CreateEventCommandHandlerTests` — Tests `CreateEventCommandHandler`
292: - `EventRepositoryTests` — Tests `EventRepository`
293: - `CleanArchitectureTests` — Architecture rule tests
294: 
295: ### Test Method Naming
296: 
297: Methods use descriptive names: `{Method}_{Scenario}_{ExpectedResult}`
298: 
299: ---
300: 
301: ## Configuration Naming
302: 
303: ### EF Core Configuration
304: 
305: | Component | Pattern | Location |
306: |---|---|---|
307: | Entity config class | `{EntityName}Configuration` | `Configurations/Entities/` |
308: | Implements | `IEntityTypeConfiguration<{EntityName}>` | — |
309: 
310: ### DI Registration
311: 
312: | Registration file | Pattern |
313: |---|---|
314: | `PersistenceServicesRegistration.cs` | `CongfigurePersistenceServices()` (note: typo is intentional/existing) |
315: | `InfrastructureServicesRegistration.cs` | `ConfigureInfrastructureServices()` |
316: | `Explore.Blazor.Client/Program.cs` | Direct service registration |
317: | `Explore.API/Program.cs` | Calls all registration methods |
318: 
319: ---
320: 
321: ## Constants and Settings Key Naming
322: 
323: Governance setting keys use dot-separated hierarchical names:
324: 
325: ```
326: Deployment.Mode
327: Events.MaxSessionsPerEvent
328: Events.RequireApproval
329: Modules.Islamic.Enabled
330: Modules.Tech.Enabled
331: Branding.DisplayName
332: Domains.InstanceBaseDomain
333: ```
334: 
335: Defined in `Explore.Domain/Constants/GovernanceSettingKeys.cs`.
336: 
337: ---
338: 
339: ## Summary: Quick Rules
340: 
341: 1. **Entities** = singular PascalCase, one per file at Domain root
342: 2. **Enums** = `{Entity}Enum` in `Domain/Enums/`
343: 3. **DTOs** = `{Prefix}{Entity}Dto` in `Application/DTOs/{Entity}/`
344: 4. **Commands** = `{Verb}{Entity}Command` in `Features/{Entities}/Requests/Commands/`
345: 5. **Queries** = `Get{Entity}{Suffix}Request` in `Features/{Entities}/Requests/Queries/`
346: 6. **Handlers** = mirror command/query name + `Handler` suffix
347: 7. **Repositories** = `I{Entity}Repository` (interface) / `{Entity}Repository` (impl)
348: 8. **Controllers** = `{Entity}Controller`, route `api/[controller]`
349: 9. **Blazor pages** = `{Action}{Entity}.razor` or `{Entity}{Action}.razor` (varies by area)
350: 10. **Client services** = `{Entity}Service` / `I{Entity}Service`
351: 11. **DB columns** = snake_case (automatic via EF Core convention)
352: 12. **Namespaces** = file-scoped, mirror folder structure exactly
````

173:     public async Task NavMenu_InstanceAdmin_ContainsCorrectRoutes()
174:     {
175: 
176:         _ctx.SetAuthenticatedUserWithClaims(
177:             AuthenticationTestConstants.AdminUserId,
178:             "Admin User",
179:             new Claim("explore:admin:instance", "true"));
180:         SetupNavMenuServices();
181: 
182: 
183:         var cut = _ctx.RenderComponent<NavMenu>();
184:         OpenDropdown(cut);
185: 
186: 
187:         await Assert.That(cut.Markup).Contains("href=\"/admin\"");
188:         await Assert.That(cut.Markup).Contains("href=\"/admin/instance/settings\"");
189:         await Assert.That(cut.Markup).DoesNotContain("href=\"/admin/tenant/settings\"");
190:     }
191: 
192:     [Test]
193:     public async Task NavMenu_TenantAdmin_ContainsCorrectRoutes()
194:     {
195: 
196:         var tenantId = AuthenticationTestConstants.DefaultTenantId;
197:         _ctx.SetAuthenticatedUserWithClaims(
198:             AuthenticationTestConstants.AdminUserId,
199:             "Tenant Admin",
200:             new Claim("explore:admin:tenant", tenantId.ToString()));
201:         SetupNavMenuServices();
202: 
203: 
204:         var cut = _ctx.RenderComponent<NavMenu>();
205:         OpenDropdown(cut);
206: 
207: 
208:         await Assert.That(cut.Markup).DoesNotContain("href=\"/admin\"");
209:         await Assert.That(cut.Markup).Contains("href=\"/admin/tenant/settings\"");
210:         await Assert.That(cut.Markup).DoesNotContain("href=\"/admin/instance/settings\"");
211:     }
212: 
213:     private static void OpenDropdown(IRenderedComponent<NavMenu> cut)
214:     {
215:         var dropdownButton = cut.Find(".navbar__user-btn");
216:         dropdownButton.Click();
217:     }
218: 
219:     private void SetupNavMenuServices()
220:     {
221:         var userService = Substitute.For<IUserService>();
222:         userService.GetCurrentUserAsync().Returns((UserDto?)null);
223:         _ctx.Services.AddSingleton(userService);
224: 
225:         var publicExperienceService = Substitute.For<IPublicExperienceService>();
226:         publicExperienceService.GetSettingsAsync().Returns((PublicExperienceSettingsModel?)null);
227:         _ctx.Services.AddSingleton(publicExperienceService);
228: 
229:         var tenantNavigationService = Substitute.For<ITenantNavigationService>();
230:         tenantNavigationService.GetNavigationLinksAsync().Returns(new List<TenantNavigationLinkDto>());
231:         _ctx.Services.AddSingleton(tenantNavigationService);
232: 
233:         var eligibilityService = Substitute.For<IEventCreationEligibilityService>();
234:         eligibilityService.GetEligibilityAsync().Returns(EventCreationEligibility.NotEligible);
235:         _ctx.Services.AddSingleton(eligibilityService);
236:     }
237: }

638:     private static HalResourceOfOrganizationDto CreateOrgResourceResponse(OrganizationDto dto)
639:     {
640:         var json = System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.Serialize(dto);
641:         return System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.Deserialize<HalResourceOfOrganizationDto>(json)
642:                ?? new HalResourceOfOrganizationDto();
643:     }
644: 
645:     private static HalCollectionResourceOfCategoryListDto CreateCategoryCollectionResponse(
646:         IList<CategoryListDto> items)
647:     {
648:         return new HalCollectionResourceOfCategoryListDto
649:         {
650:             _embedded = new HalCollectionEmbeddedOfCategoryListDto
651:             {
652:                 Items = items.Cast<object>().ToList()
653:             }
654:         };
655:     }
656: 
657:     private static HalCollectionResourceOfTagListDto CreateTagCollectionResponse(
658:         IList<TagListDto> items)
659:     {
660:         return new HalCollectionResourceOfTagListDto
661:         {
662:             _embedded = new HalCollectionEmbeddedOfTagListDto
663:             {
664:                 Items = items.Cast<object>().ToList()
665:             }
666:         };
667:     }
668: 
669:     private static HalCollectionResourceOfLocationListDto CreateLocationCollectionResponse(
670:         IList<LocationListDto> items)
671:     {
672:         return new HalCollectionResourceOfLocationListDto
673:         {
674:             _embedded = new HalCollectionEmbeddedOfLocationListDto
675:             {
676:                 Items = items.Cast<object>().ToList()
677:             }
678:         };
679:     }
680: 
681:     private static ApiException CreateApiException(string message, int statusCode, string response = "")
682:     {
683:         return new ApiException(
684:             message,
685:             statusCode,
686:             response,
687:             new Dictionary<string, IEnumerable<string>>(),
688:             new InvalidOperationException(message));
689:     }
690: 
691:     #endregion
692: }

````razor
  1: @using MudBlazor
  2: @using Explore.Blazor.Client.Services
  3: @using Explore.Blazor.Client.Clients
  4: 
  5: <MudTable Items="Items" Hover="true" Breakpoint="Breakpoint.Sm" Elevation="0" Dense="true" Class="border-solid border-1 mud-border-lines-default rounded-lg">
  6:     <HeaderContent>
  7:         <MudTh>Submitted</MudTh>
  8:         <MudTh>ID</MudTh>
  9:         <MudTh>Organization</MudTh>
 10:         <MudTh>Status</MudTh>
 11:         <MudTh Style="text-align:center">Actions</MudTh>
 12:         <MudTh Style="text-align:center">Details</MudTh>
 13:     </HeaderContent>
 14: 
 15:     <RowTemplate>
 16:         <MudTd DataLabel="Submitted">
 17:             <MudText Typo="Typo.body2" Style="font-weight: 600;">
 18:                 @(context.CreatedAt?.ToLocalTime().ToString("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm") ?? "N/A")
 19:             </MudText>
 20:             <MudText Typo="Typo.caption" Color="Color.Secondary">@GetRelative(context.CreatedAt ?? DateTimeOffset.UtcNow)</MudText>
 21:         </MudTd>
 22: 
 23:         <MudTd DataLabel="ID">
 24:             <MudText Typo="Typo.body2" Class="font-monospace">@context.Id.ToString()[..8]…</MudText>

 26: 
 27:         <MudTd DataLabel="Organization">

 31:                 </MudAvatar>
 32: 
 33:                 <div>
 34:                     <MudText Typo="Typo.subtitle2" Style="font-weight: 700;">
 35:                         @context.FullName
 36:                     </MudText>
 37:                     <MudText Typo="Typo.caption" Color="Color.Secondary">
 38:                         @(context.City ?? "Unknown"), @(context.Country ?? "Unknown") • @context.Email
 39:                     </MudText>
 40:                 </div>
 41:             </div>
 42:         </MudTd>
 43: 
 44:         <MudTd DataLabel="Status">
 45:             <MudChip T="string"
 46:                      Color="@StatusColor((RequestStatus)context.ApprovalStatusId)"
 47:                      Variant="Variant.Filled"
 48:                      Size="Size.Small"
 49:                      Class="rounded-pill px-3">
 50:                 @context.StatusTypeFullName
 51:             </MudChip>
 52:         </MudTd>
 53: 
 54:         <MudTd DataLabel="Actions" Style="text-align:center">
 55:             <div class="d-flex justify-center gap-2">
 56:                 @if (context.ApprovalStatusId == (int)RequestStatus.Pending)
 57:                 {
 58:                     <MudTooltip Text="Approve">
 59:                         <MudIconButton Icon="@Icons.Material.Filled.CheckCircle"
 60:                                        Color="Color.Success"
 61:                                        Variant="Variant.Filled"
 62:                                        Size="Size.Small"
 63:                                        OnClick="@(() => OnApprove.InvokeAsync(context))" />
 64:                     </MudTooltip>
 65:                     <MudTooltip Text="Reject">
 66:                         <MudIconButton Icon="@Icons.Material.Filled.Cancel"
 67:                                        Color="Color.Error"
 68:                                        Variant="Variant.Filled"
 69:                                        Size="Size.Small"
 70:                                        OnClick="@(() => OnReject.InvokeAsync(context))" />
 71:                     </MudTooltip>
 72:                 }
 73:                 else if (context.ApprovalStatusId == (int)RequestStatus.Approved)
 74:                 {
 75:                     <MudTooltip Text="Revoke approval">
 76:                         <MudIconButton Icon="@Icons.Material.Filled.Restore"
 77:                                        Color="Color.Warning"
 78:                                        Variant="Variant.Filled"
 79:                                        Size="Size.Small"
 80:                                        OnClick="@(() => OnRevert.InvokeAsync(context))" />
 81:                     </MudTooltip>
 82:                 }
 83:                 else if (context.ApprovalStatusId == (int)RequestStatus.Rejected)
 84:                 {
 85:                     <MudTooltip Text="Move back to pending">
 86:                         <MudIconButton Icon="@Icons.Material.Filled.Restore"
 87:                                        Color="Color.Info"
 88:                                        Variant="Variant.Filled"
 89:                                        Size="Size.Small"
 90:                                        OnClick="@(() => OnRevert.InvokeAsync(context))" />
 91:                     </MudTooltip>
 92:                 }
 93:             </div>
 94:         </MudTd>
 95: 
 96:         <MudTd DataLabel="Details" Style="text-align:center">
 97:             <MudButton Variant="Variant.Filled"
 98:                        Color="Color.Primary"
 99:                        Size="Size.Small"
100:                        StartIcon="@Icons.Material.Filled.Visibility"
101:                        OnClick="@(() => OnViewDetails.InvokeAsync(context))"
102:                        Class="rounded-pill">
103:                 Details
104:             </MudButton>
105:         </MudTd>
106:     </RowTemplate>
107: 
108:     <NoRecordsContent>
109:         <div class="d-flex flex-column align-center justify-center pa-8">
110:             <MudIcon Icon="@Icons.Material.Filled.Inbox" Size="Size.Large" Color="Color.Default" />
111:             <MudText Typo="Typo.h6" Class="mt-2" Style="font-weight: 700;">No matching requests</MudText>
112:             <MudText Typo="Typo.body2" Color="Color.Secondary">Try clearing filters or changing your search.</MudText>
113:             <MudButton Variant="Variant.Outlined"
114:                        Color="Color.Primary"
115:                        OnClick="OnClearFilters"
116:                        Class="mt-4 rounded-pill">
117:                 Clear filters
118:             </MudButton>
119:         </div>
120:     </NoRecordsContent>
121: </MudTable>
122: 
123: @code {
124:     [Parameter] public IEnumerable<OrganizationListDto> Items { get; set; } = Enumerable.Empty<OrganizationListDto>();
125:     [Parameter] public EventCallback<OrganizationListDto> OnApprove { get; set; }
126:     [Parameter] public EventCallback<OrganizationListDto> OnReject { get; set; }
127:     [Parameter] public EventCallback<OrganizationListDto> OnRevert { get; set; }
128:     [Parameter] public EventCallback<OrganizationListDto> OnViewDetails { get; set; }
129:     [Parameter] public EventCallback OnClearFilters { get; set; }
130: 
131:     // Helpers duplicated here for display logic
132:     private enum RequestStatus { Pending = 1, Approved = 2, Rejected = 3 }
133: 
134:     private Color StatusColor(RequestStatus s) => s switch
135:     {
136:         RequestStatus.Pending => Color.Info,
137:         RequestStatus.Approved => Color.Success,
138:         RequestStatus.Rejected => Color.Error,
139:         _ => Color.Default
140:     };
141: 
142:     private string GetRelative(DateTimeOffset utc)
143:     {
144:         var ts = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow - utc;
145:         if (ts.TotalDays >= 1) return $"{(int)ts.TotalDays}d ago";
146:         if (ts.TotalHours >= 1) return $"{(int)ts.TotalHours}h ago";
147:         if (ts.TotalMinutes >= 1) return $"{(int)ts.TotalMinutes}m ago";
148:         return "just now";
149:     }
150: }
````
