## File: .claude/skills/dotnet-efcore-guidelines/resources/repository-pattern.md
````markdown
  1: # Repository Pattern
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Repository Patterns**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: ## Why Repository Pattern?
 10: 
 11: ```
 12: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 13: │                    BENEFITS OF REPOSITORY PATTERN                   │
 14: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 15: │                                                                     │
 16: │  ✅ Abstraction: Application layer doesn't depend on EF Core        │
 17: │  ✅ Testability: Easy to mock repositories for unit tests          │
 18: │  ✅ Clean Architecture: Maintains dependency inversion              │
 19: │  ✅ Centralized Data Access: Common queries in one place            │
 20: │  ✅ Consistent API: Uniform data access across entities             │
 21: │                                                                     │
 22: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 23: ```
 24: 
 25: ---
 26: 
 27: ## Generic Repository
 28: 
 29: Base repository with common CRUD operations.
 30: 
 31: ### Interface (Application Layer)
 32: 
 33: ```csharp
 34: // File: {Project}.Application/Contracts/Persistence/IGenericRepository.cs
 35: namespace {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
 36: 
 37: public interface IGenericRepository<T, TKey> where T : class
 38: {
 39:     Task<T> Create(T entity);
 40:     Task<T?> GetById(TKey id);
 41:     Task<IReadOnlyList<T>> GetAll();
 42:     Task Update(T entity);
 43:     Task Delete(T entity);
 44:     Task<bool> Exists(TKey id);
 45: }
 46: ```
 47: 
 48: ### Implementation (Persistence Layer)
 49: 
 50: ```csharp
 51: // File: {Project}.Persistence/Repositories/GenericRepository.cs
 52: using System;
 53: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
 54: using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
 55: using Npgsql;
 56: 
 57: namespace {Project}.Persistence.Repositories;
 58: 
 59: public class GenericRepository<T, TKey> : IGenericRepository<T, TKey> where T : class
 60: {
 61:     private readonly {DbContext} _dbContext;
 62: 
 63:     public GenericRepository({DbContext} dbContext)
 64:     {
 65:         _dbContext = dbContext;
 66:     }
 67: 
 68:     public async Task<T> Create(T entity)
 69:     {
 70:         try
 71:         {
 72:             await _dbContext.AddAsync(entity);
 73:             await _dbContext.SaveChangesAsync();
 74:             return entity;
 75:         }
 76:         catch (DbUpdateException ex) when (ex.InnerException is PostgresException pgEx && pgEx.SqlState == "23505")
 77:         {
 78:             // Duplicate key violation - detach the entity and rethrow with more context
 79:             _dbContext.Entry(entity).State = EntityState.Detached;
 80:             throw new InvalidOperationException(
 81:                 $"A record with the same unique key already exists. Constraint: {pgEx.ConstraintName}. Detail: {pgEx.Detail}",
 82:                 ex);
 83:         }
 84:     }
 85: 
 86:     public async Task<T?> GetById(TKey id)
 87:     {
 88:         return await _dbContext.Set<T>().FindAsync(id);
 89:     }
 90: 
 91:     public async Task<IReadOnlyList<T>> GetAll()
 92:     {
 93:         return await _dbContext.Set<T>().ToListAsync();
 94:     }
 95: 
 96:     public async Task Update(T entity)
 97:     {
 98:         _dbContext.Entry(entity).State = EntityState.Modified;
 99:         await _dbContext.SaveChangesAsync();
100:     }
101: 
102:     public async Task Delete(T entity)
103:     {
104:         _dbContext.Set<T>().Remove(entity);
105:         await _dbContext.SaveChangesAsync();
106:     }
107: 
108:     public async Task<bool> Exists(TKey id)
109:     {
110:         var entity = await GetById(id);
111:         return entity != null;
112:     }
113: }
114: ```
115: 
116: ---
117: 
118: ## Entity-Specific Repository
119: 
120: Inherit from GenericRepository and add custom methods.
121: 
122: ### Interface (Application Layer)
123: 
124: ```csharp
125: // File: {Project}.Application/Contracts/Persistence/I{Entity}Repository.cs
126: using {Project}.Domain;
127: 
128: namespace {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
129: 
130: public interface I{Entity}Repository : IGenericRepository<{Entity}, {IdType}>
131: {
132:     Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}WithDetails();
133:     Task<{Entity}?> Get{Entity}WithDetails({IdType} id);
134:     Task<List<{Entity}>> GetMy{Entities}WithDetails(string userId);
135: }
136: ```
137: 
138: ### Implementation (Persistence Layer)
139: 
140: ```csharp
141: // File: {Project}.Persistence/Repositories/{Entity}Repository.cs
142: using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
143: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
144: using {Project}.Domain;
145: 
146: namespace {Project}.Persistence.Repositories;
147: 
148: public class {Entity}Repository : GenericRepository<{Entity}, {IdType}>, I{Entity}Repository
149: {
150:     private readonly {DbContext} _dbContext;
151: 
152:     public {Entity}Repository({DbContext} dbContext) : base(dbContext)
153:     {
154:         _dbContext = dbContext;
155:     }
156: 
157:     // ✅ REPOSITORIES RETURN ENTITIES, NOT DTOs
158:     public async Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}WithDetails()
159:     {
160:         return await _dbContext.{Entities}
161:             .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
162:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity1})
163:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity2})
164:             .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
165:             .Include(e => e.Status)
166:             .Include(e => e.Visibility)
167:             .Include(e => e.FeaturedImage)
168:             .ToListAsync();
169:     }
170: 
171:     public async Task<{Entity}?> Get{Entity}WithDetails({IdType} id)
172:     {
173:         return await _dbContext.{Entities}
174:             .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
175:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity1})
176:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity2})
177:             .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
178:             .Include(e => e.Status)
179:             .Include(e => e.Visibility)
180:             .Include(e => e.FeaturedImage)
181:             .FirstOrDefaultAsync(e => e.Id == id);
182:     }
183: 
184:     public async Task<List<{Entity}>> GetMy{Entities}WithDetails(string userId)
185:     {
186:         {IdType} userIdParsed;
187:         var isValid = {IdType}.TryParse(userId, out userIdParsed);
188: 
189:         var query = _dbContext.{Entities}
190:             .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
191:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity1})
192:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity2})
193:             .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
194:             .Include(e => e.Status)
195:             .Include(e => e.Visibility)
196:             .Include(e => e.FeaturedImage)
197:             .AsQueryable();
198: 
199:         if (isValid)
200:         {
201:             query = query.Where(e =>
202:                 _dbContext.Users.Any(u => u.Id == userIdParsed && u.{ParentEntity}Id == e.{ParentEntity}Id));
203:         }
204: 
205:         return await query.ToListAsync();
206:     }
207: 
208:     // NOTE: In the Application layer handler, entities are mapped to DTOs:
209:     //
210:     // public async Task<List<{Entity}ListDto>> Handle(Get{Entity}ListRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
211:     // {
212:     //     // Repository returns ENTITIES
213:     //     var {entities} = await _{entity}Repository.Get{Entities}WithDetails();
214:     //
215:     //     // AutoMapper maps ENTITIES to DTOs
216:     //     return _mapper.Map<List<{Entity}ListDto>>({entities});
217:     // }
218: }
219: ```
220: 
221: ---
222: 
223: ## Repository Registration (DI)
224: 
225: ```csharp
226: // File: {Project}.Persistence/PersistenceServicesRegistration.cs
227: using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;
228: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
229: using {Project}.Persistence.Repositories;
230: 
231: namespace {Project}.Persistence;
232: 
233: public static class PersistenceServicesRegistration
234: {
235:     public static IServiceCollection AddPersistenceServices(
236:         this IServiceCollection services)
237:     {
238:         // Register generic repository
239:         services.AddScoped(typeof(IGenericRepository<,>), typeof(GenericRepository<,>));
240: 
241:         // Register specific repositories
242:         services.AddScoped<I{Entity}Repository, {Entity}Repository>();
243:         services.AddScoped<I{ParentEntity}Repository, {ParentEntity}Repository>();
244:         services.AddScoped<IUserRepository, UserRepository>();
245:         services.AddScoped<I{LinkEntity}Repository, {LinkEntity}Repository>();
246: 
247:         return services;
248:     }
249: }
250: ```
251: 
252: **Usage in Program.cs**:
253: ```csharp
254: builder.Services.AddPersistenceServices();
255: ```
256: 
257: ---
258: 
259: ## Repository Method Patterns
260: 
261: ### Return Entities (Standard Pattern)
262: 
263: **CRITICAL**: Repositories return ENTITIES, not DTOs. DTO mapping happens in Application layer handlers via AutoMapper.
264: 
265: ```csharp
266: // ✅ CORRECT: Repository returns entities
267: public async Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}WithDetails()
268: {
269:     return await _dbContext.{Entities}
270:         .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
271:         .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity1})
272:         .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity2})
273:         .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
274:         .ToListAsync();
275: }
276: 
277: // ✅ CORRECT: Handler maps entities to DTOs
278: public class Get{Entity}ListRequestHandler : IRequestHandler<Get{Entity}ListRequest, List<{Entity}ListDto>>
279: {
280:     private readonly I{Entity}Repository _{entity}Repository;
281:     private readonly IMapper _mapper;
282: 
283:     public async Task<List<{Entity}ListDto>> Handle(Get{Entity}ListRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
284:     {
285:         // Repository returns ENTITIES
286:         var {entities} = await _{entity}Repository.Get{Entities}WithDetails();
287: 
288:         // AutoMapper maps ENTITIES to DTOs
289:         return _mapper.Map<List<{Entity}ListDto>>({entities});
290:     }
291: }
292: ```
293: 
294: **Benefits**:
295: - ✅ Clean separation of concerns
296: - ✅ Repositories focus on data access only
297: - ✅ Handlers handle DTO mapping with AutoMapper
298: - ✅ Reusable repositories for different DTO shapes
299: 
300: ### AsNoTracking for Read-Only Queries
301: 
302: ```csharp
303: public async Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}ReadOnly()
304: {
305:     // ✅ No change tracking (faster for read-only)
306:     return await _dbContext.{Entities}
307:         .AsNoTracking()
308:         .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
309:         .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
310:         .ToListAsync();
311: }
312: ```
313: 
314: ---
315: 
316: ## Advanced Repository Patterns
317: 
318: ### Specification Pattern
319: 
320: ```csharp
321: // File: Application/Specifications/ISpecification.cs
322: public interface ISpecification<T>
323: {
324:     Expression<Func<T, bool>> Criteria { get; }
325:     List<Expression<Func<T, object>>> Includes { get; }
326: }
327: 
328: // File: Application/Specifications/{Entity}Specification.cs
329: public class {Entities}By{ParentEntity}Spec : ISpecification<{Entity}>
330: {
331:     public {Entities}By{ParentEntity}Spec({IdType} {parentEntity}Id)
332:     {
333:         Criteria = e => e.{ParentEntity}Id == {parentEntity}Id;
334:         Includes = new List<Expression<Func<{Entity}, object>>>
335:         {
336:             e => e.{ParentEntity},
337:             e => e.{LookupEntity}
338:         };
339:     }
340: 
341:     public Expression<Func<{Entity}, bool>> Criteria { get; }
342:     public List<Expression<Func<{Entity}, object>>> Includes { get; }
343: }
344: 
345: // Repository method
346: public async Task<List<{Entity}>> Find(ISpecification<{Entity}> spec)
347: {
348:     var query = _dbContext.{Entities}.Where(spec.Criteria);
349: 
350:     query = spec.Includes
351:         .Aggregate(query, (current, include) => current.Include(include));
352: 
353:     return await query.ToListAsync();
354: }
355: ```
356: 
357: ### Pagination
358: 
359: ```csharp
360: public async Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}Paginated(
361:     int page,
362:     int pageSize,
363:     string? searchTerm)
364: {
365:     var query = _dbContext.{Entities}
366:         .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
367:         .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
368:         .AsQueryable();
369: 
370:     if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(searchTerm))
371:     {
372:         query = query.Where(e =>
373:             e.Title.Contains(searchTerm) ||
374:             e.Description.Contains(searchTerm));
375:     }
376: 
377:     var totalCount = await query.CountAsync();
378: 
379:     var items = await query
380:         .OrderByDescending(e => e.StartDate)
381:         .Skip((page - 1) * pageSize)
382:         .Take(pageSize)
383:         .ToListAsync();
384: 
385:     return items;
386: }
387: ```
388: 
389: ---
390: 
391: ## Best Practices
392: 
393: | Practice | Reason |
394: |----------|--------|
395: | ✅ Interface in Application, implementation in Persistence | Clean Architecture |
396: | ✅ Inherit from GenericRepository | Code reuse |
397: | ✅ Return entities, not DTOs | Separation of concerns |
398: | ✅ Use `AsNoTracking()` for read-only | No unnecessary tracking |
399: | ✅ Include related entities with `Include` | Avoid N+1 queries |
400: | ✅ Register repositories in DI | Dependency injection |
401: | ✅ Use async methods (`Async` suffix) | Non-blocking I/O |
402: | ❌ Don't return IQueryable from repository | Encapsulation |
403: | ❌ Don't inject DbContext in Application layer | Breaks abstraction |
404: | ❌ Don't track entities for read-only queries | Performance overhead |
405: 
406: ---
407: 
408: **Related Resources**:
409: - [dbcontext-patterns.md](dbcontext-patterns.md) - DbContext configuration
410: - [querying-patterns.md](querying-patterns.md) - Query optimization
411: - [entity-configuration.md](entity-configuration.md) - Entity configuration
````

## File: docs/CONTRIBUTING.md
````markdown
  1: # Contribution Workflow
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Contribution Guidelines**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: ## Placeholder Substitutions
  8: 
  9: | Placeholder | Replace With | Example (ISLAMU Event) |
 10: |-------------|--------------|------------------------|
 11: | `{Project}` | Your solution name | `Explore` |
 12: | `{Project}.API` | API project | `{Project}.API` |
 13: | `{Project}.AppHost` | Aspire AppHost | `{Project}.AppHost` |
 14: | `{Project}ApiClient` | Generated API client | `{Project}ApiClient` |
 15: 
 16: ---
 17: 
 18: ## Branch Strategy
 19: 
 20: ```
 21: main                    # Default branch
 22: ├── feature/xxx         # New features
 23: ├── bugfix/xxx          # Bug fixes
 24: └── refactor/xxx        # Code improvements
 25: ```
 26: 
 27: ## Commit Convention
 28: 
 29: ```
 30: type(scope): subject
 31: 
 32: body (optional)
 33: 
 34: footer (optional)
 35: ```
 36: 
 37: **Types**: `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `style`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`
 38: 
 39: **Examples**:
 40: ```
 41: feat(events): add prayer-relative scheduling
 42: fix(federation): correct HTTP signature validation
 43: docs(api): update endpoint documentation
 44: ```
 45: 
 46: ## Pull Request Process
 47: 
 48: 1. Create a branch from `main`
 49: 2. Implement changes with tests
 50: 3. Ensure all tests pass: `dotnet test`
 51: 4. Ensure code formatting: `dotnet format`
 52: 5. Create PR with description and linked issue
 53: 6. Request review from maintainers
 54: 7. Address feedback
 55: 8. Squash and merge when approved
 56: 
 57: ## Issue Templates
 58: 
 59: - **Bug Report**: Describe bug, steps to reproduce, expected behavior
 60: - **Feature Request**: Describe need, proposed solution, alternatives
 61: - **Task**: Technical work without user-facing change
 62: 
 63: ---
 64: 
 65: ## DTO Change Workflow (API → Blazor Client)
 66: 
 67: When making changes to DTOs in the API project, follow this specific workflow to ensure the Blazor client is properly updated.
 68: 
 69: ### Why This Workflow Matters
 70: 
 71: The project uses **.NET Aspire** for orchestration, which:
 72: 1. Fetches secrets from Infisical and injects them as environment variables
 73: 2. Starts all projects in the correct order
 74: 3. **Triggers OpenAPI schema regeneration** in the API project on startup
 75: 4. **NSwag watches for schema changes** and automatically regenerates the Blazor API client
 76: 
 77: **Key Point**: You must run Aspire to regenerate the client. Building alone won't update the generated client code.
 78: 
 79: ### The Vicious Cycle Problem
 80: 
 81: Understanding **why** this workflow exists prevents frustrating debugging sessions.
 82: 
 83: #### The Problem: Build Errors Block Client Regeneration
 84: 
 85: When you change DTOs in the API and then try to build the **full solution**, you enter a vicious cycle:
 86: 
 87: ```
 88: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 89: │                    ❌ THE VICIOUS CYCLE                              │
 90: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 91: │                                                                     │
 92: │  1. You change a DTO in the API (add new property)                  │
 93: │     ↓                                                               │
 94: │  2. You try to build the FULL SOLUTION                              │
 95: │     ↓                                                               │
 96: │  3. ❌ BUILD FAILS - Blazor references the OLD generated client     │
 97: │     │   (The generated client doesn't have the new property yet)    │
 98: │     ↓                                                               │
 99: │  4. ❌ ASP.NET API won't run (solution didn't build)                │
100: │     ↓                                                               │
101: │  5. ❌ swagger.json can't regenerate (API isn't running)            │
102: │     ↓                                                               │
103: │  6. ❌ NSwag can't update the client (no new schema)                │
104: │     ↓                                                               │
105: │  7. ❌ Generated client stays outdated                              │
106: │     ↓                                                               │
107: │  8. ❌ Build errors persist → BACK TO STEP 3                        │
108: │                                                                     │
109: │  💀 YOU ARE STUCK IN AN INFINITE LOOP                               │
110: │                                                                     │
111: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
112: ```
113: 
114: #### The Solution: Build API Separately First
115: 
116: By building **only the API project** first, you break the cycle:
117: 
118: ```
119: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
120: │                    ✅ THE CORRECT WORKFLOW                           │
121: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
122: │                                                                     │
123: │  1. You change a DTO in the API (add new property)                  │
124: │     ↓                                                               │
125: │  2. Build ONLY the API project: `dotnet build {Project}.API`          │
126: │     ↓                                                               │
127: │  3. ✅ API builds successfully (no Blazor dependency issues)        │
128: │     ↓                                                               │
129: │  4. Run Aspire: `dotnet run --project {Project}.AppHost`              │
130: │     ↓                                                               │
131: │  5. ✅ API starts and generates new swagger.json                    │
132: │     ↓                                                               │
133: │  6. ✅ NSwag detects changes, regenerates client                    │
134: │     ↓                                                               │
135: │  7. ✅ Generated client now has the new property                    │
136: │     ↓                                                               │
137: │  8. NOW update Blazor services/components                           │
138: │     ↓                                                               │
139: │  9. ✅ Build full solution: `dotnet build {Project}.sln`              │
140: │                                                                     │
141: │  🎉 SUCCESS - No build errors!                                      │
142: │                                                                     │
143: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
144: ```
145: 
146: #### Common Trap: Updating Blazor Services Too Early
147: 
148: A particularly frustrating mistake is updating **Blazor services that interact with the generated API client** before the client is regenerated:
149: 
150: ```
151: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
152: │              ❌ THE SERVICE UPDATE TRAP                              │
153: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
154: │                                                                     │
155: │  Scenario: You add `Description` property to `EventDto`             │
156: │                                                                     │
157: │  1. You update EventDto in API (✅ correct)                         │
158: │     ↓                                                               │
159: │  2. You update EventService in Blazor to use `.Description`         │
160: │     ↓                                                               │
161: │  3. ❌ ERROR: 'EventDto' does not contain 'Description'             │
162: │     │                                                               │
163: │     │   WHY? The generated client ({Project}ApiClient.cs) still       │
164: │     │   has the OLD EventDto without Description!                   │
165: │     │                                                               │
166: │     │   Your service references: Generated.EventDto (OLD)           │
167: │     │   You expect:              Generated.EventDto.Description     │
168: │     │   Reality:                 Property doesn't exist yet         │
169: │     ↓                                                               │
170: │  4. Build fails on BOTH sides:                                      │
171: │     • API side: Works fine (your DTO has the property)              │
172: │     • Blazor side: Fails (generated client is outdated)             │
173: │                                                                     │
174: │  💡 The generated client is OUT OF SYNC with the API!               │
175: │                                                                     │
176: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
177: ```
178: 
179: **Rule of Thumb**:
180: - **API-only changes** → Build API only, run Aspire, then update Blazor
181: - **UI-only changes** (no DTO changes) → Can work directly in Blazor
182: - **Both API + Blazor changes** → Follow the full checklist, API first
183: 
184: ### Standard Workflow
185: 
186: ```
187: API Changes → Build API → Run Aspire → Client Regenerates → Update Blazor UI
188: ```
189: 
190: ### Process Checklist for DTO Changes
191: 
192: Follow this checklist whenever you add/modify DTO properties:
193: 
194: ```markdown
195: ## DTO Change Checklist
196: 
197: ### 1. Application Layer Changes
198: - [ ] Add/update properties in `{Project}.Application/DTOs/{Entity}/` files
199: - [ ] Update `{Entity}Dto.cs` (full details)
200: - [ ] Update `{Entity}ListDto.cs` (list view) if applicable
201: - [ ] Update `Create{Entity}Dto.cs` / `Update{Entity}Dto.cs` if applicable
202: 
203: ### 2. Mapping & Data Access
204: - [ ] Update `MappingProfile.cs` if new navigation properties
205: - [ ] Update Repository `.Include()` statements if loading related data
206: - [ ] Update Handler if new processing logic needed
207: 
208: ### 3. Build & Regenerate
209: - [ ] Build API project only: `dotnet build {Project}.API`
210: - [ ] Start Aspire: `dotnet run --project {Project}.AppHost`
211: - [ ] Wait for swagger.json to regenerate (automatic on API startup)
212: - [ ] NSwag regenerates client automatically (watches schema file)
213: 
214: ### 4. Blazor UI Updates
215: - [ ] NOW update Blazor components to use new properties
216: - [ ] Build full solution: `dotnet build {Project}.sln`
217: - [ ] Test the changes in browser
218: ```
219: 
220: ### Quick Fix: If You Forgot the Workflow
221: 
222: If you already updated Blazor UI before running Aspire and the generated client is missing properties:
223: 
224: **Option 1: Proper Fix (Recommended)**
225: ```powershell
226: # Stop any running instances
227: # Run Aspire to regenerate everything
228: dotnet run --project {Project}.AppHost
229: ```
230: 
231: **Option 2: Manual Fix (Quick Workaround)**
232: Manually add the missing properties to the generated client file as a temporary fix, then run Aspire later to properly regenerate.
233: 
234: ### Architecture Diagram
235: 
236: ```
237: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
238: │                         .NET Aspire Orchestration                    │
239: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
240: │                                                                     │
241: │  1. Aspire Starts                                                   │
242: │     └── Fetches secrets from Infisical                              │
243: │     └── Injects environment variables to all projects               │
244: │                                                                     │
245: │  2. API Project Starts                                              │
246: │     └── Generates swagger.json (OpenAPI schema)                     │
247: │     └── Schema reflects current DTO structure                       │
248: │                                                                     │
249: │  3. Blazor Project Watches                                          │
250: │     └── NSwag detects swagger.json changes                          │
251: │     └── Regenerates API client ({Project}ApiClient.cs)                │
252: │                                                                     │
253: │  4. Blazor Components                                               │
254: │     └── Use the regenerated client with new properties              │
255: │                                                                     │
256: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
257: ```
258: 
259: ### Common Mistakes
260: 
261: | Mistake | Why It Fails | Fix |
262: |---------|--------------|-----|
263: | Build solution without running Aspire | swagger.json not regenerated | Run Aspire first |
264: | Update Blazor before API | Generated client missing new properties | Follow the checklist order |
265: | Manually edit generated files | Changes overwritten on next regeneration | Add to source DTOs, regenerate |
266: | Skip the MappingProfile update | AutoMapper doesn't map new properties | Always update profile |
267: 
268: ### Related Documentation
269: 
270: - [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) - Overall system architecture
271: - [API.md](API.md) - API endpoint patterns
272: - [BLAZOR.md](BLAZOR.md) - Blazor client architecture
273: - [GOVERNANCE.md](GOVERNANCE.md) - DTO patterns and conventions
````

````markdown
  1: # Deployment Modes & Customization
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Operations & Deployment Guide**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: ## Placeholder Substitutions
  8: 
  9: | Placeholder | Replace With | Example (ISLAMU Event) |
 10: |-------------|--------------|------------------------|
 11: | `{Project}` | Your solution name | `Explore` |
 12: | `{Project}.Infrastructure` | Infrastructure project | `Explore.Infrastructure` |
 13: | `{Instance Name}` | Your instance display name | `ISLAMU Event` |
 14: 
 15: ---
 16: 
 17: This platform is designed to be **highly customizable** to support diverse deployment scenarios—from single-organization instances to full SaaS platforms serving multiple tenants. This section covers all customization options.
 18: 
 19: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
 20: The ISLAMU Event platform (project name: Explore) is the reference implementation of this system, designed for Islamic event discovery globally.
 21: 
 22: ## Deployment Modes
 23: 
 24: The platform supports two primary deployment modes:
 25: 
 26: ```
 27: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 28: │                      DEPLOYMENT MODES                               │
 29: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 30: │                                                                     │
 31: │  MODE 1: Single-Instance Deployment                                 │
 32: │  ─────────────────────────────────────                              │
 33: │  • Multi-tenancy DISABLED                                           │
 34: │  • One organization/community per deployment                        │
 35: │  • Simpler configuration and maintenance                            │
 36: │  • Example: ISLAMU's own Islamic events instance                    │
 37: │  • Example: A university running their own event platform           │
 38: │                                                                     │
 39: │  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
 40: │  │              Single Instance                                │    │
 41: │  │  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │    │
 42: │  │  │  events.islamu.org                                  │    │    │
 43: │  │  │  • All events in one space                          │    │    │
 44: │  │  │  • Single admin team                                │    │    │
 45: │  │  │  • Unified branding                                 │    │    │
 46: │  │  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │    │
 47: │  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
 48: │                                                                     │
 49: │  MODE 2: Multi-Tenant SaaS Deployment                               │
 50: │  ────────────────────────────────────                               │
 51: │  • Multi-tenancy ENABLED                                            │
 52: │  • Multiple isolated organizations/communities                      │
 53: │  • For SaaS providers offering ISLAMU Event as a service            │
 54: │  • Each tenant has custom domain, branding, settings                │
 55: │  • Shared infrastructure, isolated data                             │
 56: │                                                                     │
 57: │  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    │
 58: │  │              Multi-Tenant SaaS Platform                     │    │
 59: │  │  ┌───────────────┐ ┌───────────────┐ ┌───────────────┐      │    │
 60: │  │  │ Tenant A      │ │ Tenant B      │ │ Tenant C      │      │    │
 61: │  │  │ mosque-a.com  │ │ uni-events.eu │ │ community.org │      │    │
 62: │  │  │ Own settings  │ │ Own settings  │ │ Own settings  │      │    │
 63: │  │  │ Own branding  │ │ Own branding  │ │ Own branding  │      │    │
 64: │  │  └───────────────┘ └───────────────┘ └───────────────┘      │    │
 65: │  │                    Shared Infrastructure                    │    │
 66: │  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    │
 67: │                                                                     │
 68: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 69: ```
 70: 
 71: ### Environment Configuration for Deployment Mode
 72: 
 73: ```yaml
 74: # docker-compose.yml
 75: services:
 76:   explore-api:
 77:     environment:
 78:       # Deployment Mode
 79:       - EXPLORE__MULTITENANCY__ENABLED=false          # true for SaaS mode
 80:       - EXPLORE__MULTITENANCY__DEFAULT_TENANT=default # Used when disabled
 81:       
 82:       # Instance Identity (Single-Instance Mode)
 83:       - EXPLORE__INSTANCE__NAME=ISLAMU Event
 84:       - EXPLORE__INSTANCE__DOMAIN=events.islamu.ngo
 85:       - EXPLORE__INSTANCE__DESCRIPTION=Islamic Event Discovery Platform
 86: ```
 87: 
 88: ## Blazor Rendering Modes
 89: 
 90: The platform supports **three Blazor rendering modes** configurable via environment variables:
 91: 
 92: | Mode | Description | Use Case |
 93: |------|-------------|----------|
 94: | **Server** | Server-side rendering | real-time updates |
 95: | **WebAssembly** | Client-side rendering in browser | Offline capability, reduced server load |
 96: | **Auto** | Server initially, then WebAssembly | Best of both worlds (recommended) |
 97: 
 98: ### Configuration
 99: 
100: ```yaml
101: # docker-compose.yml
102: services:
103:   explore-blazor:
104:     environment:
105:       # Blazor Rendering Mode: Server | WebAssembly | Auto
106:       - BLAZOR__RENDER_MODE=Auto
107:       
108:       # Additional Blazor Settings
109:       - BLAZOR__PRERENDER=true                    # Enable prerendering for SEO
110:       - BLAZOR__DETAILED_ERRORS=false             # Show detailed errors (dev only)
111:       - BLAZOR__WEBSOCKET_COMPRESSION=true        # Compress SignalR traffic
112: ```
113: 
114: ```csharp
115: // Program.cs - Runtime configuration
116: var renderMode = builder.Configuration["Blazor:RenderMode"] ?? "Auto";
117: 
118: builder.Services.AddRazorComponents()
119:     .AddInteractiveServerComponents()
120:     .AddInteractiveWebAssemblyComponents();
121: 
122: // In App.razor - Dynamic render mode
123: @code {
124:     private IComponentRenderMode RenderMode => 
125:         Configuration["Blazor:RenderMode"] switch
126:         {
127:             "Server" => RenderMode.InteractiveServer,
128:             "WebAssembly" => RenderMode.InteractiveWebAssembly,
129:             "Auto" => RenderMode.InteractiveAuto,
130:             _ => RenderMode.InteractiveAuto
131:         };
132: }
133: ```
134: 
135: ## Observability Pipeline (Aspire + Serilog + OpenTelemetry + Loki)
136: 
137: The recommended production flow is:
138: 
139: ```
140: App logs -> Microsoft.Extensions.Logging -> OpenTelemetry provider -> OTLP -> OpenTelemetry Collector -> Loki
141: ```
142: 
143: ### Required Rules
144: 
145: - Use Serilog for structured JSON logs and enrichers.
146: - Keep `UseSerilog(..., writeToProviders: true)` in app hosts so logs continue through the provider pipeline.
147: - Configure OTLP once via Aspire ServiceDefaults using `builder.Services.AddOpenTelemetry().UseOtlpExporter()`.
148: - Do not use `Serilog.Sinks.Loki` for this architecture.
149: 
150: ### Critical OpenTelemetry Constraint
151: 
152: Do not mix these two patterns in the same app:
153: 
154: - Cross-cutting exporter: `UseOtlpExporter()`
155: - Signal-specific exporters: `AddOtlpExporter()` (logs, metrics, or traces)
156: 
157: Mixing both causes a runtime `NotSupportedException` in OpenTelemetry .NET.
158: 
159: ### Environment Variables
160: 
161: ```yaml
162: services:
163:   explore-api:
164:     environment:
165:       - OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://otel-collector:4318
166:       - OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf
167: 
168:   explore-blazor:
169:     environment:
170:       - OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://otel-collector:4318
171:       - OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf
172: ```
173: 
174: ### Loki/Collector Notes
175: 
176: - Send logs to Loki through OpenTelemetry Collector OTLP pipelines.
177: - Ensure Loki OTLP ingestion is enabled with structured metadata support (`allow_structured_metadata: true`).
178: - Keep Prometheus scraping enabled on `/metrics` for metric collection.
179: 
180: ## Instance-Level Administration
181: 
182: Instance Administrators (not organization admins) can configure platform-wide behavior through the **Instance Settings** panel or environment variables.
183: 
184: ### Organization & Event Publishing Policies
185: 
186: Configurable inside the **Instance Settings** panel in the webapp for instance administrator.
187: 
188: ```
189: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
190: │              INSTANCE-LEVEL POLICY CONFIGURATION                    │
191: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
192: │                                                                     │
193: │  ORGANIZATION CREATION POLICY                                       │
194: │  ────────────────────────────                                       │
195: │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
196: │  │  Option A: Open Registration (Default)                       │   │
197: │  │  • Anyone can create an organization                         │   │
198: │  │  • Organizations start as "Unverified"                       │   │
199: │  │  • Can publish events immediately                            │   │
200: │  │                                                              │   │
201: │  │  Option B: Approval Required (ISLAMU Instance)               │   │
202: │  │  • Anyone can REQUEST to create an organization              │   │
203: │  │  • Instance admin must APPROVE before org is active          │   │
204: │  │  • Only approved orgs can publish events                     │   │
205: │  │                                                              │   │
206: │  │  Option C: Invite Only                                       │   │
207: │  │  • Only instance admins can create organizations             │   │
208: │  │  • Most restrictive, for curated platforms                   │   │
209: │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
210: │                                                                     │
211: │  USER EVENT PUBLISHING POLICY                                       │
212: │  ────────────────────────────                                       │
213: │  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
214: │  │  Option A: Users Can Publish (marked as "User Reported")     │   │
215: │  │  • Individual users can post events                          │   │
216: │  │  • Events flagged with "User Reported" badge                 │   │
217: │  │  • Subject to community moderation                           │   │
218: │  │                                                              │   │
219: │  │  Option B: Users Cannot Publish Directly                     │   │
220: │  │  • Only organizations can publish events                     │   │
221: │  │  • Higher quality control                                    │   │
222: │  │                                                              │   │
223: │  │  Option C: Users Publish with Approval                       │   │
224: │  │  • Users submit events for review                            │   │
225: │  │  • Instance moderators approve before publishing             │   │
226: │  │  • Balance between openness and quality                      │   │
227: │  │                                                              │   │
228: │  │  Option D: Users Publish without approval nor verification   │   │
229: │  │  • Users submit events                                       │   │
230: │  │  • fully open                                                │   │
231: │  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
232: │                                                                     │
233: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
234: ```

237: ## Cerbos Authorization Service
238: 
239: Cerbos is the Policy Decision Point (PDP) for fine-grained authorization. It runs as an opt-in Docker service.
240: 
241: ### Deployment
242: 
243: ```bash
244: # Start Cerbos alongside the platform
245: docker compose --profile authz up -d
246: 
247: # Verify health
248: curl http://localhost:3592/_cerbos/health
249: ```
250: 
251: ### Schema Initialization
252: 
253: For Tier 2+ deployments using PostgreSQL-backed policy storage:
254: 
255: ```bash
256: # Initialize the Cerbos schema in a dedicated database or schema
257: psql -h localhost -U cerbos_user -d cerbos -f cerbos/init/cerbos-schema.sql
258: ```
259: 
260: The schema creates 5 tables (`policy`, `policy_dependency`, `policy_ancestor`, `policy_revision`, `attr_schema_defs`) plus an audit trigger that tracks all policy changes.
261: 
262: ### Configuration
263: 
264: Cerbos is configured via `cerbos/config/.cerbos.yaml`:
265: 
266: | Setting | Default | Description |
267: |---------|---------|-------------|
268: | `server.httpListenAddr` | `:3592` | HTTP API port |
269: | `server.grpcListenAddr` | `:3593` | gRPC port |
270: | `server.adminAPI.enabled` | `true` | Admin API for PolicySyncService |
271: | `storage.driver` | `overlay` | PG primary + disk fallback |
272: | `compile.cacheDuration` | `60s` | Policy compilation cache |
273: 
274: Environment variables:
275: - `CERBOS_ADMIN_USER` — Admin API username
276: - `CERBOS_ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH` — Bcrypt hash of admin password
277: - `CERBOS_PG_URL` — PostgreSQL connection string for policy store
278: 
279: ### Policy Management
280: 
281: **Base policies** (18 resource kinds) are shipped as YAML files in `cerbos/policies/` and mounted into the container. These define the default authorization rules for each resource type.
282: 
283: **Dynamic policies** are generated by `PolicySyncService` when role permissions change (e.g., admin creates a custom role). These are pushed to Cerbos via the Admin API and stored in PostgreSQL.
284: 
285: The overlay driver ensures: PostgreSQL policies take precedence → disk policies as fallback.
286: 
287: ### Health Monitoring
288: 
289: | Endpoint | Method | Description |
290: |----------|--------|-------------|
291: | `/_cerbos/health` | GET | Returns 200 if Cerbos is healthy |
292: | `/_cerbos/metrics` | GET | Prometheus metrics (if enabled) |
293: 
294: The `RuntimeAuthorizationProvider` has a Polly circuit breaker (trips after 50% failure rate over 30s, breaks for 15s). When tripped, all authorization falls back to `LocalAuthorizationProvider`.
295: 
296: ### Backup & Restore
297: 
298: **Policy store backup:**
299: ```bash
300: pg_dump -h localhost -U cerbos_user -d cerbos --schema=cerbos > cerbos-backup.sql
301: ```
302: 
303: **Restore:**
304: ```bash
305: psql -h localhost -U cerbos_user -d cerbos < cerbos-backup.sql
306: ```
307: 
308: Base YAML policies are version-controlled in `cerbos/policies/` — no separate backup needed.
309: 
310: ### Upgrade Procedure
311: 
312: 1. Pull new Cerbos image: `docker pull ghcr.io/cerbos/cerbos:latest`
313: 2. Rolling restart (Tier 2+): restart one instance at a time
314: 3. Verify health after each restart: `curl http://<instance>:3592/_cerbos/health`
315: 4. Run policy compilation check: `cerbos compile cerbos/policies/`
316: 
317: ### Troubleshooting
318: 
319: | Symptom | Cause | Resolution |
320: |---------|-------|------------|
321: | `Connection refused` on port 3592 | Cerbos not running | `docker compose --profile authz up -d` |
322: | Policy compile errors in CI | Invalid YAML syntax | Run `cerbos compile cerbos/policies/` locally |
323: | Circuit breaker tripped (logs: "Cerbos circuit open") | Cerbos unreachable or slow | Check Cerbos container logs, restart if needed |
324: | `authorization.provider = local` but Cerbos running | SystemSetting override | Update SystemSetting to `cerbos` via admin panel |
325: | PolicySyncService 401 Unauthorized | Wrong admin credentials | Verify `CERBOS_ADMIN_USER` and `CERBOS_ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH` env vars |
326: 
327: For deployment tier guidance, see [DEPLOYMENT_TIERS.md](DEPLOYMENT_TIERS.md).
328: 
329: ---
330: 
331: ## Tenant-Level Configuration (BYOK - Bring Your Own Keys)
332: 
333: Tenant-level BYOK integrations are a **roadmap** capability.
334: 
335: **Current state**:
336: 
337: - Object storage integration exists (S3-compatible) via `{Project}.Infrastructure`.
338: - Other per-tenant integrations (analytics, payments, AI services, email/SMS routing) are not implemented yet.
339: 
340: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
341: In the Explore project, object storage is implemented in `Explore.Infrastructure` with S3-compatible providers.

378: ## Organization-Level Integrations
379:

117:     {

119:         _canEdit = status?.IsCurrentUserTenantAdministrator == true;
120:

122:         {

128:         _isLoading = false;

132:     {

134:         _errorMessage = null;
135:

137:         _isSaving = false;

145:

147:             ? "Failed to save tenant settings."

## File: Explore.Blazor.Client/Pages/Onboarding/StartupGate.razor
````razor
 1: @page "/startup"
 2: @using MudBlazor
 3: @inject IInstanceOnboardingService InstanceOnboardingService
 4: @inject NavigationManager Navigation
 5: @inject ILogger<StartupGate> Logger
 6: @rendermode @(new InteractiveAutoRenderMode(prerender: false))
 7: 
 8: <MudContainer Class="d-flex justify-center align-center" Style="min-height: 60vh;">
 9:     @if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(_error))
10:     {
11:         <MudAlert Severity="Severity.Error" Variant="Variant.Filled">
12:             @_error
13:         </MudAlert>
14:     }
15:     else
16:     {
17:         <MudStack AlignItems="AlignItems.Center" Spacing="3">
18:             <MudProgressCircular Color="Color.Primary" Size="Size.Large" Indeterminate="true" />
19:             <MudText Typo="Typo.h6">Preparing your workspace...</MudText>
20:             <MudText Typo="Typo.caption">Checking instance and tenant onboarding status.</MudText>
21:         </MudStack>
22:     }
23: </MudContainer>
24: 
25: @code {
26:     private string? _error;
27: 
28:     protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
29:     {
30:         await ResolveStartupRouteAsync();
31:     }
32: 
33:     private async Task ResolveStartupRouteAsync()
34:     {
35:         try
36:         {
37:             var instanceStatus = await InstanceOnboardingService.GetStatusAsync();
38:             if (instanceStatus == null)
39:             {
40:                 _error = "Could not determine onboarding status. Try refreshing.";
41:                 return;
42:             }
43: 
44:             if (!instanceStatus.IsCompleted)
45:             {
46:                 Navigation.NavigateTo("/setup");
47:                 return;
48:             }
49: 
50:             if (instanceStatus.IsAuthenticated &&
51:                 instanceStatus.SelectedDeploymentMode?.Equals("MultiTenant", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) == true)
52:             {
53:                 Navigation.NavigateTo("/admin/instance/settings");
54:                 return;
55:             }
56: 
57:             Navigation.NavigateTo("/events");
58:         }
59:         catch (Exception ex)
60:         {
61:             Logger.LogError(ex, "Startup routing failed.");
62:             _error = "Startup routing failed. Try refreshing.";
63:         }
64:     }
65: }

 10: 
 11: public partial class OrganizationProfile
 12: {
 13:     [Inject] protected IOrganizationService OrganizationService { get; set; } = null!;
 14:     [Inject] protected IOrganizationReviewService OrganizationReviewService { get; set; } = null!;
 15:     [Inject] protected NavigationManager Navigation { get; set; } = null!;
 16:     [Inject] protected RouterStateService RouterState { get; set; } = null!;
 17:     [Inject] protected ILogger<OrganizationProfile> Logger { get; set; } = null!;
 18: 
 19:     private Guid Id { get; set; }
 20: 
 21:     private OrganizationDto? _organization;
 22:     private bool _isLoading = true;
 23:     private List<OrganizationReviewDto> _reviews = new();
 24:     private OrganizationAppearanceSettings _appearance = new();
 25:     private string _bannerStyle = OrganizationAppearanceMetadataHelper.BuildBannerStyle(new OrganizationAppearanceSettings(), "#1f6feb");
 26: 
 27:     private string? _errorMessage;
 28: 
 29:     [PersistentState]
 30:     public OrganizationProfileState? PersistedState { get; set; }
 31: 
 32:     protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
 33:     {
 34: 
 35:         var idStr = RouterState.GetParam("id");
 36:         if (Guid.TryParse(idStr, out var id))
 37:         {
 38:             Id = id;
 39:         }
 40: 
 41:         if (TryRestoreState())
 42:         {
 43:             return;
 44:         }
 45: 
 46:         _isLoading = true;
 47:         _errorMessage = null;
 48: 
 49:         try
 50:         {
 51: 
 52:             _organization = await OrganizationService.GetOrganizationByIdAsync(Id);
 53:             _reviews = (await OrganizationReviewService.GetReviewsByOrganizationId(Id)).ToList();
 54:             _appearance = OrganizationAppearanceMetadataHelper.Parse(_organization?.MetadataJson);
 55:             _bannerStyle = OrganizationAppearanceMetadataHelper.BuildBannerStyle(_appearance, "#1f6feb");
 56:             Logger.LogDebug("Loaded organization {OrganizationId} with {ReviewCount} reviews", Id, _reviews.Count);
 57: 
 58:             PersistState();
 59:         }
 60:         catch (Exception ex)
 61:         {
 62:             _errorMessage = $"Failed to load organization data: {ex.Message}";
 63:             Logger.LogError(ex, "Error loading organization {OrganizationId}", Id);
 64:         }
 65:         finally
 66:         {
 67:             _isLoading = false;
 68:         }
 69:     }
 70: 
 71:     private void ShowAllReviews()
 72:     {
 73:         Navigation.NavigateTo($"/organization/reviews/{Id}");
 74:     }
 75: 
 76:     private string GetOrganizationPlaceholder()
 77:     {
 78:         if (_organization == null)
 79:             return ImageHelper.GetOrganizationPlaceholder(null, "ORG");
 80: 
 81:         return ImageHelper.GetOrganizationPlaceholder(null, _organization.FullName);
 82:     }
 83: 
 84:     private string? GetProfileImageUri()
 85:     {
 86:         if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(_organization?.ActorProfilePictureUri))
 87:         {
 88:             return _organization.ActorProfilePictureUri;
 89:         }
 90: 
 91:         if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(_appearance.ProfileImageUrl))
 92:         {
 93:             return _appearance.ProfileImageUrl.Trim();
 94:         }
 95: 
 96:         return null;
 97:     }
 98: 
 99:     private bool TryRestoreState()
100:     {
101:         if (PersistedState == null || PersistedState.OrganizationId != Id)
102:         {
103:             return false;
104:         }
105: 
106:         _organization = PersistedState.Organization;
107:         _reviews = PersistedState.Reviews;
108:         _appearance = OrganizationAppearanceMetadataHelper.Parse(_organization?.MetadataJson);
109:         _bannerStyle = OrganizationAppearanceMetadataHelper.BuildBannerStyle(_appearance, "#1f6feb");
110:         _isLoading = false;
111:         _errorMessage = null;
112:         return true;
113:     }
114: 
115:     private void PersistState()
116:     {
117:         PersistedState = new OrganizationProfileState
118:         {
119:             OrganizationId = Id,
120:             Organization = _organization,
121:             Reviews = _reviews.ToList()
122:         };
123:     }
124: 
125:     public sealed class OrganizationProfileState
126:     {
127:         public Guid OrganizationId { get; init; }
128:         public OrganizationDto? Organization { get; init; }
129:         public List<OrganizationReviewDto> Reviews { get; init; } = new();
130:     }
131: }

## File: Explore.Blazor.Client/Routing/Guards/AdminRouteGuard.cs
````csharp
 1: using Blazouter.Interfaces;
 2: using Blazouter.Models;
 3: using Explore.Blazor.Client.Services;
 4: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Authorization;
 5: 
 6: namespace Explore.Blazor.Client.Routing.Guards;
 7:

13: public sealed class AdminRouteGuard(
14:     AuthenticationStateProvider authStateProvider,
15:     IInstanceOnboardingService instanceOnboardingService) : IRouteGuard
16: {
17:     public async Task<bool> CanActivateAsync(RouteMatch match)
18:     {
19:         if (authStateProvider is null)
20:         {
21:             return false;
22:         }
23: 
24:         var authState = await authStateProvider.GetAuthenticationStateAsync().ConfigureAwait(false);
25:         var user = authState.User;
26:         if (user.Identity?.IsAuthenticated != true)
27:         {
28:             return false;
29:         }
30: 
31: 
32: 
33:         if (user.HasClaim(c => c.Type == "explore:admin:instance"))
34:         {
35:             return true;
36:         }
37: 
38: 
39: 
40:         var instanceStatus = await instanceOnboardingService.GetStatusAsync().ConfigureAwait(false);
41:         return instanceStatus?.IsAuthenticated == true && instanceStatus.IsCurrentUserInstanceAdmin;
42:     }
43: 
44:     public async Task<string?> GetRedirectPathAsync(RouteMatch match)
45:     {
46:         if (authStateProvider is not null)
47:         {
48:             var authState = await authStateProvider.GetAuthenticationStateAsync().ConfigureAwait(false);
49:             if (authState?.User?.Identity?.IsAuthenticated == true)
50:             {
51:                 return "/";
52:             }
53:         }
54: 
55:         var returnUrl = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(match.MatchedPath)
56:             ? "/"
57:             : match.MatchedPath;
58: 
59:         return $"/login?returnUrl={Uri.EscapeDataString(returnUrl)}";
60:     }
61: }
````

## File: Explore.Blazor.Client/Services/BffUnauthorizedHandler.cs
````csharp
  1: using System.Linq;
  2: using System.Net;
  3: using System.Net.Http;
  4: using System.Threading;
  5: using System.Threading.Tasks;
  6: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components;
  7: using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
  8: 
  9: namespace Explore.Blazor.Client.Services;
 10: 
 11: public sealed class BffUnauthorizedHandler : DelegatingHandler
 12: {
 13:     private static readonly string[] AnonymousApiPathPrefixes =
 14:     [
 15:         "/api/publicexperience/settings",
 16:         "/api/instanceonboarding/status"
 17:     ];
 18: 
 19:     private readonly NavigationManager _nav;
 20:     private readonly ILogger<BffUnauthorizedHandler> _logger;
 21: 
 22:     public BffUnauthorizedHandler(NavigationManager nav, ILogger<BffUnauthorizedHandler> logger)
 23:     {
 24:         _nav = nav;
 25:         _logger = logger;
 26:     }
 27: 
 28:     protected override async Task<HttpResponseMessage> SendAsync(HttpRequestMessage request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
 29:     {
 30:         HttpResponseMessage response;
 31:         try
 32:         {
 33:             response = await base.SendAsync(request, cancellationToken);
 34:         }
 35:         catch (Exception ex)
 36:         {
 37:             _logger.LogError(ex, "BFF handler: request failed for {Method} {Uri}", request.Method, request.RequestUri);
 38:             throw;
 39:         }
 40: 
 41:         if (response.StatusCode == HttpStatusCode.Unauthorized)
 42:         {
 43:             var path = request.RequestUri?.AbsolutePath ?? string.Empty;
 44:             var currentRelativePath = _nav.ToBaseRelativePath(_nav.Uri);
 45:             if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(currentRelativePath))
 46:             {
 47:                 currentRelativePath = "/";
 48:             }
 49:             else if (!currentRelativePath.StartsWith('/'))
 50:             {
 51:                 currentRelativePath = "/" + currentRelativePath;
 52:             }
 53:             else
 54:             {
 55:                 var queryIndex = currentRelativePath.IndexOf('?', System.StringComparison.Ordinal);
 56:                 if (queryIndex >= 0)
 57:                 {
 58:                     currentRelativePath = currentRelativePath[..queryIndex];
 59:                 }
 60:             }
 61: 
 62: 
 63:             if (path.StartsWith("/login", System.StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) ||
 64:                 path.StartsWith("/logout", System.StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) ||
 65:                 path.StartsWith("/auth", System.StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
 66:             {
 67:                 _logger.LogDebug("BFF handler: received 401 from auth endpoint {Method} {Uri}", request.Method, request.RequestUri);
 68:                 return response;
 69:             }
 70: 
 71: 
 72:             if (currentRelativePath.StartsWith("/login", System.StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) ||
 73:                 currentRelativePath.StartsWith("/logout", System.StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
 74:             {
 75:                 _logger.LogDebug("BFF handler: suppressing 401 redirect while on auth page {CurrentPath}", currentRelativePath);
 76:                 return response;
 77:             }
 78: 
 79: 
 80:             if (AnonymousApiPathPrefixes.Any(prefix => path.StartsWith(prefix, System.StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)))
 81:             {
 82:                 _logger.LogDebug("BFF handler: received 401 from anonymous endpoint {Method} {Uri}", request.Method, request.RequestUri);
 83:                 return response;
 84:             }
 85: 
 86:             _logger.LogWarning("BFF handler: received 401 for {Method} {Uri} - redirecting to /login", request.Method, request.RequestUri);
 87: 
 88:             var relativeCurrentPath = _nav.ToBaseRelativePath(_nav.Uri);
 89:             if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(relativeCurrentPath))
 90:             {
 91:                 relativeCurrentPath = "/";
 92:             }
 93:             else if (!relativeCurrentPath.StartsWith('/'))
 94:             {
 95:                 relativeCurrentPath = "/" + relativeCurrentPath;
 96:             }
 97: 
 98:             var returnUrl = Uri.EscapeDataString(relativeCurrentPath);
 99:             _nav.NavigateTo($"/login?returnUrl={returnUrl}", forceLoad: true);
100:         }
101: 
102:         return response;
103:     }
104: }
````

## File: .claude/skills/auth-patterns/SKILL.md
````markdown
  1: ---
  2: name: auth-patterns
  3: description: Guidelines for authentication and authorization patterns covering OIDC, JWT, and BFF security in .NET Clean Architecture projects.
  4: type: domain
  5: enforcement: suggest
  6: priority: critical
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: # Authentication & Authorization Patterns
 10: 
 11: > **Project-Agnostic Authentication & Authorization Guide**
 12: >
 13: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
 14: 
 15: ## Placeholder Substitutions
 16: 
 17: | Placeholder | Replace With | Example (ISLAMU Event) |
 18: |-------------|--------------|------------------------|
 19: | `{Project}` | Your solution name | `Explore` |
 20: | `{Project}.Blazor` | Blazor Server (BFF) project | `Explore.Blazor` |
 21: | `{Project}.Blazor.Client` | Blazor WASM project | `Explore.Blazor.Client` |
 22: | `{Project}.API` | API project | `Explore.API` |
 23: 
 24: ---
 25: 
 26: ## 🎯 Purpose
 27: 
 28: This skill provides the standard patterns for implementing security in .NET Clean Architecture projects. It covers the OIDC/JWT authentication flow, the Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) security model, and authorization conventions.
 29: 
 30: ## ⚡ When This Skill Activates
 31: 
 32: **Triggered by**:
 33: - Keywords: "auth", "security", "jwt", "oidc", "keycloak", "authorize", "claim"
 34: - File patterns: `*Controller.cs`, `*Program.cs` (for auth setup)
 35: 
 36: ## 📚 Resources
 37: 
 38: | Resource | Description |
 39: |----------|-------------|
 40: | [user-id-extraction.md](resources/user-id-extraction.md) | The critical fallback pattern for extracting user ID from JWT claims. |
 41: | [api-jwt-validation.md](resources/api-jwt-validation.md) | API-side JWT bearer validation, middleware order, and claim validation patterns. |
 42: 
 43: ## 1. Authentication Architecture: BFF with OIDC & JWT
 44: 
 45: The project uses a **Backend-for-Frontend (BFF)** pattern to handle authentication, which provides a strong security posture by never exposing tokens to the browser.
 46: 
 47: ```mermaid
 48: sequenceDiagram
 49:     participant Browser (Blazor WASM)
 50:     participant BFF (Blazor Server)
 51:     participant Keycloak
 52:     participant API (Backend)
 53: 
 54:     Browser->>+BFF: User clicks "Login"
 55:     BFF->>+Keycloak: Initiates OIDC Authorization Code Flow
 56:     Keycloak-->>-BFF: Redirects with Authorization Code
 57:     BFF->>+Keycloak: Exchanges Code for Tokens (Access + Refresh)
 58:     Keycloak-->>-BFF: Returns JWTs
 59:     BFF-->>-Browser: Stores tokens in secure, HttpOnly cookie & redirects
 60: 
 61:     Browser->>+BFF: Makes API call (/api/...)
 62:     BFF->>+API: YARP proxy reads token from cookie, attaches as "Authorization: Bearer" header
 63:     API->>API: Validates JWT signature & claims
 64:     API-->>-BFF: Returns data
 65:     BFF-->>-Browser: Returns data to client
 66: ```
 67: 
 68: *   **`{Project}.Blazor` (BFF)**: Is the OIDC client. It handles the redirect to the identity provider and manages the user's session via a cookie.
 69: *   **`{Project}.Blazor.Client` (WASM)**: Is not OIDC-aware. It simply includes credentials (the cookie) with every request to its backend (the BFF).
 70: *   **`{Project}.API`**: Is a stateless service that only trusts JWT Bearer tokens. It has no knowledge of the user's session cookie.
 71: 
 72: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
 73: - **`Explore.Blazor`**: BFF using Keycloak as the identity provider
 74: - **`Explore.Blazor.Client`**: Blazor WASM client
 75: - **`Explore.API`**: Stateless API validating Keycloak-issued JWTs
 76: 
 77: ## 2. Authorization Conventions
 78: 
 79: ### Controller Endpoint Authorization
 80: 
 81: A simple and strict convention is followed for API endpoints:
 82: *   **`GET` requests are public**: Decorated with `[AllowAnonymous]`.
 83: *   **`POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE` requests are protected**: Decorated with `[Authorize]`.
 84: *   **Admin-only operations**: Decorated with `[Authorize(Roles = "Admin")]`.
 85: *   **Resource ownership is enforced in handlers**: Controller attributes gate access, handlers enforce business-level ownership and permissions.
 86: 
 87: **Generic Template:**
 88: ```csharp
 89: // ✅ Public read access
 90: [HttpGet]
 91: [AllowAnonymous]
 92: public async Task<ActionResult<List<{Entity}ListDto>>> GetAll()
 93: {
 94:     var {entities} = await _mediator.Send(new Get{Entity}ListRequest());
 95:     return Ok({entities});
 96: }
 97: 
 98: // ✅ Authenticated write access
 99: [HttpPost]
100: [Authorize]
101: public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>> Create([FromBody] Create{Entity}Dto {entity})
102: {
103:     var command = new Create{Entity}Command { {Entity}Dto = {entity} };
104:     var response = await _mediator.Send(command);
105:     return Ok(response);
106: }
107: 
108: // ✅ Admin-only access
109: [HttpDelete("{id}")]
110: [Authorize(Roles = "Admin")]
111: public async Task<ActionResult> DeletePermanent({IdType} id)
112: {
113:     var result = await _mediator.Send(new Delete{Entity}PermanentlyCommand { Id = id });
114:     return result ? NoContent() : NotFound();
115: }
116: ```
117: 
118: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
119: ```csharp
120: [HttpGet]
121: [AllowAnonymous]
122: public async Task<ActionResult<List<EventListDto>>> GetAll()
123: {
124:     var events = await _mediator.Send(new GetEventListRequest());
125:     return Ok(events);
126: }
127: 
128: [HttpPost]
129: [Authorize]
130: public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<Guid>>> Create([FromBody] CreateEventDto @event)
131: {
132:     var command = new CreateEventCommand { EventDto = @event };
133:     var response = await _mediator.Send(command);
134:     return Ok(response);
135: }
136: ```
137: 
138: ### Resource-Level Authorization
139: 
140: Resource-level authorization (e.g., "can this user edit *this specific* event?") is the responsibility of the **MediatR handler** in the Application layer, not the controller.
141: 
142: ```csharp
143: // Example: DeleteEventCommandHandler
144: public async Task<bool> Handle(DeleteEventCommand request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
145: {
146:     // The handler receives the UserId from the controller
147:     var @event = await _eventRepository.GetById(request.Id);
148: 
149:     if (@event == null)
150:         return false; // Not found
151: 
152:     // ✅ Handler enforces ownership logic
153:     var actor = await _actorRepository.GetById(@event.ActorId);
154:     if (actor == null || actor.UserId.ToString() != request.UserId)
155:     {
156:         // User does not own the event, deny deletion
157:         return false;
158:     }
159: 
160:     await _eventRepository.Delete(@event);
161:     return true;
162: }
163: ```
164: 
165: ## 3. User ID Extraction from JWT Claims
166: 
167: For the **CRITICAL PATTERN** for safely and consistently extracting the user ID from JWT claims, including the fallback mechanism for `sub`, `nameidentifier`, and `sid`, refer to [user-id-extraction.md](resources/user-id-extraction.md).
168: 
169: ## 4. API JWT Validation and Middleware Order
170: 
171: For API-side JWT setup and common production safeguards, refer to [api-jwt-validation.md](resources/api-jwt-validation.md).
172: 
173: Key points:
174: - Configure JWT bearer auth with explicit issuer and audience validation.
175: - Use middleware in the correct order: exception handling, routing/cors, authentication, authorization, endpoint mapping.
176: - Normalize claim extraction through one shared helper/service instead of duplicating controller logic.
177: - Log auth failures with structured context, but never log raw tokens.
178: 
179: ---
180: **Related Skills**:
181: - `clean-architecture-rules`
182: - `blazor-bff-patterns`
````

 37: - File patterns: `**/*Blazor/Program.cs`, `**/*Blazor/Services/**/*.cs`, `**/*Blazor.Client/Services/**/*.cs`, `**/Extensions/**/*.cs`
