 73: 
 74: ## Environment Variables
 75: 
 76: | Variable | Description | Example |
 77: |----------|-------------|---------|
 78: | `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT` | Runtime environment | `Development`, `Staging`, `Production` |
 79: | `ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection` | PostgreSQL connection | `Host=...;Database=...` |
 80: | `Keycloak__ClientSecret` | Keycloak client secret | `...` |
 81: | `Infisical__ClientId` | Secrets manager client | `...` |
 82: | `Infisical__ClientSecret` | Secrets manager secret | `...` |
 83: 
 84: ## Secret Management
 85: 
 86: The application uses a unified secret management system (`Explore.Secrets`) that supports multiple providers:
 87: 
 88: ### Secret Providers
 89: 
 90: | Provider | Use Case | Configuration |
 91: |----------|----------|---------------|
 92: | `none` | Self-hosters, local dev | Use environment variables directly |
 93: | `infisical` | Production with Infisical | Connects to Infisical service |
 94: 
 95: ### Configuration Options
 96: 
 97: ```json
 98: {
 99:   "SecretProvider": {
100:     "Provider": "infisical",
101:     "FailFast": true
102:   },
103:   "Infisical": {
104:     "Url": "https://app.infisical.com",
105:     "ProjectId": "your-project-id",
106:     "ClientId": "your-client-id",
107:     "ClientSecret": "your-client-secret",
108:     "Environment": "dev"
109:   },
110:   "SecretRefresh": {
111:     "RefreshInterval": "00:05:00",
112:     "BaseBackoffDelay": "00:00:30",
113:     "MaxBackoffDelay": "00:05:00"
114:   }
115: }
116: ```
117: 
118: ### Environment Variables
119: 
120: | Variable | Description | Required |
121: |----------|-------------|----------|
122: | `SECRET_PROVIDER` | Provider type: `none` or `infisical` | No (default: `none`) |
123: | `Infisical__Url` | Infisical server URL | Only if using Infisical |
124: | `Infisical__ProjectId` | Infisical project ID | Only if using Infisical |
125: | `Infisical__ClientId` | Universal Auth client ID | Only if using Infisical |
126: | `Infisical__ClientSecret` | Universal Auth client secret | Only if using Infisical |
127: | `Infisical__Environment` | Environment slug (dev, staging, prod) | No (default: `dev`) |
128: 
129: ### Self-Hosted Deployment (No Secret Manager)
130: 
131: For self-hosters who don't want to use Infisical, set `SECRET_PROVIDER=none` and provide all secrets via environment variables:
132: 
133: ```bash
134: # Required environment variables for self-hosted deployment
135: SECRET_PROVIDER=none
136: ConnectionStrings__DefaultConnection=Host=...;Database=...;Username=...;Password=...
137: Keycloak__Authority=https://your-keycloak/realms/your-realm
138: Keycloak__ClientId=explore-api
139: Keycloak__ClientSecret=your-secret
140: S3Settings__AccessKeyId=your-access-key
141: S3Settings__SecretAccessKey=your-secret-key
142: ```
143: 
144: ### Infisical Deployment
145: 
146: For production with Infisical:
147: 
148: ```bash
149: SECRET_PROVIDER=infisical
150: Infisical__Url=https://app.infisical.com
151: Infisical__ProjectId=your-project-id
152: Infisical__ClientId=your-client-id
153: Infisical__ClientSecret=your-client-secret
154: Infisical__Environment=prod
155: ```
156: 
157: Secrets are automatically loaded from Infisical paths:
158: - `/keycloak` - Keycloak configuration
159: - `/postgresql` - Database credentials
160: - `/api` - API-specific secrets (S3, etc.)
161: - `/blazor` - Blazor-specific configuration
162: 
163: ### Features
164: 
165: - **Automatic Refresh**: Secrets are refreshed periodically (configurable interval)
166: - **Health Checks**: Secret provider health is exposed at `/health`
167: - **Metrics**: Prometheus-compatible metrics for monitoring
168: - **Audit Logging**: All secret access is logged with redaction
169: - **Graceful Fallback**: Falls back to environment variables if Infisical unavailable
170: 
171: ## Cerbos (Planned - Not Currently Integrated)
172: 
173: Some older docs/templates mention a `Cerbos` configuration section.
174: 
175: Cerbos is **not currently integrated** into `{Project}.API`. All authorization logic is currently implemented within the application code. There is no active Cerbos configuration required for the running system.
176: 
177: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
178: Cerbos is not currently integrated into `Explore.API`. Authorization is handled by MediatR handlers and endpoint-level `[Authorize]` attributes.
179: 
180: ---
181: 
182: ## Instance-Level Settings
183: 
184: The system supports **instance-level configuration** that controls deployment modes, feature toggles, and system-wide settings through the `SystemSetting` table.
185: 
186: ### SystemSetting Table
187: 
188: Instance administrators can configure system behavior through database-stored settings:
189: 
190: **Generic Pattern:**
191: ```csharp
192: public class SystemSetting
193: {
194:     public Guid Id { get; set; }
195:     public string Key { get; set; } = string.Empty;
196:     public string Value { get; set; } = string.Empty;
197:     public string? Description { get; set; }
198: 
199:     // Auditing
200:     public DateTime CreatedAt { get; set; }
201:     public Guid? CreatedBy { get; set; }
202:     public DateTime? UpdatedAt { get; set; }
203:     public Guid? UpdatedBy { get; set; }
204: }
205: ```
206: 
207: ### Governance Setting Keys
208: 
209: System settings are defined as constants in `GovernanceSettingKeys`:
210: 
211: ```csharp
212: public static class GovernanceSettingKeys
213: {
214:     // Deployment Mode
215:     public const string DeploymentMode = "System.DeploymentMode";  // "SingleTenant" or "MultiTenant"
216: 
217:     // Feature Flags
218:     public const string FederationEnabled = "System.Federation.Enabled";
219:     public const string RegistrationOpen = "System.Registration.Open";
220:     public const string MaintenanceMode = "System.MaintenanceMode";
221: 
222:     // Module Governance (see Module-Specific Configuration section)
223:     public const string IslamicModuleEnabled = "System.Modules.Islamic.Enabled";
224:     public const string TechModuleEnabled = "System.Modules.Tech.Enabled";
225: 
226:     // Instance Metadata
227:     public const string InstanceName = "System.Instance.Name";
228:     public const string InstanceDomain = "System.Instance.Domain";
229: }
230: ```
231: 
232: ### Deployment Mode Switching
233: 
234: The `DeploymentMode` setting controls multi-tenant vs single-tenant behavior:
235: 
236: **Generic Pattern:**
237: ```csharp
238: // Retrieve deployment mode
239: var deploymentMode = await _systemSettingService.GetAsync(
240:     GovernanceSettingKeys.DeploymentMode);
241: 
242: if (deploymentMode == "SingleTenant")
243: {
244:     // Single tenant: All users belong to default tenant
245:     // No tenant selection UI shown
246: }
247: else if (deploymentMode == "MultiTenant")
248: {
249:     // Multi-tenant: Users can belong to multiple tenants
250:     // Tenant selection UI shown
251:     // Tenant context required for all operations
252: }
253: ```
254: 
255: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
256: 
257: ```csharp
258: // Explore.Domain/Constants/GovernanceSettingKeys.cs
259: public static class GovernanceSettingKeys
260: {
261:     public const string DeploymentMode = "System.DeploymentMode";
262:     public const string FederationEnabled = "System.Federation.Enabled";
263:     public const string IslamicModuleEnabled = "System.Modules.Islamic.Enabled";
264:     // ... more keys
265: }
266: 
267: // Usage in services
268: var federationEnabled = await _systemSettingService.GetBoolAsync(
269:     GovernanceSettingKeys.FederationEnabled);
270: 
271: if (federationEnabled)
272: {
273:     // Enable federation endpoints
274: }
275: ```
276: 
277: **See Also**: [OPERATIONS.md](OPERATIONS.md) for deployment mode details.
278: 
279: ---
280: 
281: ## Module-Specific Configuration
282: 
283: The system supports **modular event types** through per-tenant capability configuration. Different tenants can enable different event modules (e.g., Islamic events, Tech events).
284: 
285: ### TenantCapability Table
286: 
287: Modules are enabled per-tenant through the `TenantCapability` table:
288: 
289: **Generic Pattern:**
290: ```csharp
291: public class TenantCapability
292: {
293:     public Guid Id { get; set; }
294:     public Guid TenantId { get; set; }
295:     public string ModuleName { get; set; } = string.Empty;  // "Islamic", "Tech", etc.
296:     public bool Enabled { get; set; }
297:     public Dictionary<string, string>? Configuration { get; set; }  // Module-specific settings
298: 
299:     // Relationships
300:     public Tenant? Tenant { get; set; }
301: }
302: ```
303: 
304: ### Module Governance Settings
305: 
306: Modules can be enabled/disabled at two levels:
307: 
308: 1. **System Level** (via `SystemSetting` table):
309:    - Controls if a module is available at all
310:    - Instance admin configures
311: 
312: 2. **Tenant Level** (via `TenantCapability` table):
313:    - Controls if a specific tenant can use a module
314:    - Tenant admin configures
315: 
316: **Hierarchy**:
317: ```
318: System.Modules.Islamic.Enabled = true   (System-wide toggle)
319:   └── TenantCapability: TenantId=abc, ModuleName="Islamic", Enabled=true   (Tenant-specific)
320: ```
321: 
322: If system-level setting is `false`, the module is unavailable to ALL tenants, regardless of `TenantCapability` settings.
323: 
324: ### Module Resolution Example
325: 
326: **Generic Pattern:**
327: ```csharp
328: // Check if module is available for tenant
329: public async Task<bool> IsModuleAvailableAsync(Guid tenantId, string moduleName)
330: {
331:     // 1. Check system-level setting
332:     var systemKey = $"System.Modules.{moduleName}.Enabled";
333:     var systemEnabled = await _systemSettingService.GetBoolAsync(systemKey);
334:     if (!systemEnabled) return false;
335: 
336:     // 2. Check tenant-level capability
337:     var capability = await _tenantCapabilityRepository.GetByTenantAndModule(
338:         tenantId, moduleName);
339: 
340:     return capability?.Enabled ?? false;
341: }
342: 
343: // Usage in handlers
344: if (await _moduleService.IsModuleAvailableAsync(tenantId, "Islamic"))
345: {
346:     // Load EventIslamicAspect
347:     var aspect = await _islamicAspectRepository.GetByEventId(eventId);
348: }
349: ```
350: 
351: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
352: 
353: ```csharp
354: // Module availability check in Create Event handler
355: public async Task<BaseCommandResponse<Guid>> Handle(...)
356: {
357:     // ... create base event ...
358: 
359:     // If Islamic module enabled for this tenant, create Islamic aspect
360:     if (await _moduleService.IsModuleAvailableAsync(tenantId, "Islamic"))
361:     {
362:         if (request.EventDto.IslamicAspect != null)
363:         {
364:             var islamicAspect = new EventIslamicAspect
365:             {
366:                 EventId = newEvent.Id,
367:                 PrayerTimesAvailable = request.EventDto.IslamicAspect.PrayerTimesAvailable,
368:                 // ... map other fields
369:             };
370:             await _islamicAspectRepository.Create(islamicAspect);
371:         }
372:     }
373: 
374:     return response;
375: }
376: ```
377: 
378: **See Also**: [CODEBASE_INSIGHTS.md](CODEBASE_INSIGHTS.md) Section 7 for module governance implementation.
379: 
380: ---
381: 
382: ## Monitoring & Observability
383: 
384: The system uses **Prometheus** for metrics and **Loki** for centralized logging.
385: 
386: ### Prometheus (Metrics)
387: 
388: Application metrics are exposed at `/metrics` endpoint using Prometheus format:
389: 
390: **Generic Configuration:**
391: ```json
392: {
393:   "Prometheus": {
394:     "Enabled": true,
395:     "MetricsPath": "/metrics",
396:     "Port": 9090
397:   }
398: }
399: ```
400: 
401: **Metrics Exposed**:
402: - HTTP request duration histograms
403: - Database query performance
404: - Command/Query execution times (MediatR pipeline)
405: - Repository operation counters
406: - Exception counts by type
407: 
408: **Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event**
409: ```csharp
410: // Explore.API/Program.cs
411: builder.Services.AddOpenTelemetry()
412:     .WithMetrics(metrics =>
413:     {
414:         metrics.AddPrometheusExporter();
415:         metrics.AddMeter("Explore.API");
416:         metrics.AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation();
417:         metrics.AddHttpClientInstrumentation();
418:     });
419: 
420: app.MapPrometheusScrapingEndpoint();  // Exposes /metrics
421: ```
422: 
423: ### Loki (Centralized Logging)
424: 
425: Logs are shipped to Loki via Serilog:
426: 
427: **Generic Configuration:**
428: ```json
429: {
430:   "Serilog": {
431:     "WriteTo": [
432:       {
433:         "Name": "GrafanaLoki",
434:         "Args": {
435:           "uri": "http://loki:3100",
436:           "labels": [
437:             { "key": "app", "value": "{project}-api" },
438:             { "key": "environment", "value": "production" }
439:           ]
440:         }
441:       }
442:     ]
443:   }
444: }
445: ```
446: 
447: **Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event**
448: ```csharp
449: // Explore.API/Program.cs
450: builder.Host.UseSerilog((context, configuration) =>
451: {
452:     configuration
453:         .ReadFrom.Configuration(context.Configuration)
454:         .Enrich.FromLogContext()
455:         .Enrich.WithProperty("Application", "Explore.API")
456:         .WriteTo.Console()
457:         .WriteTo.GrafanaLoki(
458:             context.Configuration["Loki:Uri"]!,
459:             labels: new List<LokiLabel>
460:             {
461:                 new() { Key = "app", Value = "explore-api" },
462:                 new() { Key = "env", Value = context.HostingEnvironment.EnvironmentName }
463:             });
464: });
465: ```
466: 
467: ### Observability Stack
468: 
469: **Recommended Stack**:
470: - **Prometheus**: Metrics collection and storage
471: - **Loki**: Log aggregation and querying
472: - **Grafana**: Unified dashboards for metrics + logs
473: - **Aspire Dashboard** (Development): Local observability during development
474: 
475: **Key Benefits**:
476: - Unified observability (metrics + logs in Grafana)
477: - Label-based log filtering (tenant, user, request ID)
478: - Performance monitoring (P50, P95, P99 latencies)
479: - Error tracking with stack traces
480: - Correlation between logs and metrics
481: 
482: **See Also**: [TROUBLESHOOTING.md](TROUBLESHOOTING.md) for debugging with Prometheus/Loki.
````

## File: docs/PROJECT.md
````markdown
  1: ## 1. Project Overview
  2: 
  3: ## What is ISLAMU Event?
  4: 
  5: **ISLAMU Event** (also known as ISLAMU Explore or Event Explorer) is an **open-source event discovery platform**.
  6: 
  7: The long-term vision includes **ATProto-first federation** with an **ActivityPub gateway**, but HTTP federation endpoints are **not currently implemented** in `Explore.API`.
  8: 
  9: ## Core Value Proposition
 10: 
 11: | Component | Value |
 12:   |-----------|-------|
 13: | **Software** | Multi-tenant federated event platform (AGPL) |
 14: | **Primary Instance** | Trusted Islamic event directory with verification |
 15: | **Filtering System** | Culturally-appropriate discovery (age, gender, madhab) |
 16: 
 17: ## Organizational Context
 18: 
 19: - **Organization**: ISLAMU Non Profit Organization (Islamic Software Lighthouse Alliance of the Muslim Ummah)
 20: - **Legal Entity**: Belgian non-profit organization ASBL (Association sans but lucratif)
 21: - **GitHub Organization**: `islamu-ngo`
 22: - **Repository**: `https://github.com/islamu-ngo/explore`
 23: - **License**: AGPL-3.0
 24: 
 25: ---
 26: 
 27: # Strategic Context
 28: 
 29: ## Ecosystem Architecture
 30: 
 31: ```
 32: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 33: │                      ISLAMU Event Ecosystem                         │
 34: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 35: │                                                                     │
 36: │  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
 37: │  │           ISLAMU-Hosted Instance (Primary Focus)            │   │
 38: │  │  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────  │   │
 39: │  │  • Islamic events globally                                  │   │
 40: │  │  • Verified actors (fact-checked)                           │   │
 41: │  │  • User-submitted events (flagged as unverified)            │   │
 42: │  │  • Strike/ban system for policy violations                  │   │
 43: │  │  • Advanced filtering (age, gender, location, language, and more)│   │
 44: │  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
 45: │                              │                                      │
 46: │                    ActivityPub Federation                           │
 47: │                              │                                      │
 48: │  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐              │
 49: │  │ Community A  │  │ Community B  │  │ Organization │  ...         │
 50: │  │ Instance     │  │ Instance     │  │ Instance     │              │
 51: │  │ (3rd party)  │  │ (3rd party)  │  │ (3rd party)  │              │
 52: │  └──────────────┘  └──────────────┘  └──────────────┘              │
 53: │         │                  │                  │                     │
 54: │         └──────────────────┴──────────────────┘                     │
 55: │                    Managed Hosting Partners                         │
 56: │                    (Revenue share with ISLAMU)                      │
 57: │                                                                     │
 58: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 59: ```
 60: 
 61: ## Architecture Philosophy
 62: 
 63: ```
 64: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 65: │                           ISLAMU Event Architecture                          │
 66: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 67: │                                                                             │
 68: │   ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────────────────────┐   │
 69: │   │   Users     │────▶│    PDS      │────▶│    ATProto Network          │   │
 70: │   │  (DIDs)     │     │  (Hosting)  │     │  (Relay/Firehose/AppView)   │   │
 71: │   └─────────────┘     └─────────────┘     └─────────────────────────────┘   │
 72: │         │                                              │                    │
 73: │         │                                              │                    │
 74: │         ▼                                              ▼                    │
 75: │   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
 76: │   │                    ISLAMU Event AppView                              │   │
 77: │   │  • Indexes ngo.islamu.event.* records                               │   │
 78: │   │  • Provides search/discovery APIs                                    │   │
 79: │   │  • Manages cultural/audience filtering                               │   │
 80: │   │  • Hosts ActivityPub Gateway (planned)                                │   │
 81: │   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
 82: │                                        │                                    │
 83: │                                        ▼                                    │
 84: │   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
 85: │   │               ActivityPub Gateway (Bridge, planned)                  │   │
 86: │   │  • Exposes ATProto events as ActivityPub Event objects              │   │
 87: │   │  • Translates ActivityPub Follow → ATProto follow records           │   │
 88: │   │  • Translates ActivityPub RSVP → ATProto participation records      │   │
 89: │   │  • Would provide WebFinger, Actor endpoints, Inbox/Outbox (planned) │   │
 90: │   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
 91: │                                        │                                    │
 92: │                                        ▼                                    │
 93: │   ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
 94: │   │                      Fediverse                                       │   │
 95: │   │              (Mastodon, Mobilizon, Pleroma, etc.)                   │   │
 96: │   └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
 97: │                                                                             │
 98: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 99: ```
100: 
101: # Core Features
102: 
103: ## Two-Tier Verification System
104: 
105: ```
106: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
107: │                    VERIFICATION SYSTEM                              │
108: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
109: │                                                                     │
110: │  TIER 1: User-Submitted Events                                      │
111: │  ├── Anyone can create account                                      │
112: │  ├── Can post events immediately                                    │
113: │  ├── Events marked as "User Reported"                               │
114: │  ├── Subject to community moderation                                │
115: │  └── Strike/ban system for violations                               │
116: │                                                                     │
117: │  TIER 2: Verified Organizations                                     │
118: │  ├── Application required                                           │
119: │  └── Fact-checking process:                                         │
120: │      └── Organization exists? (registration check)                  │
121: │                                                                     │
122: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
123: ```
124: 
125: ## Advanced Filtering System
126: 
127: | Filter | Options | Description |
128: |--------|---------|-------------|
129: | **Audience Age** | Children, Youth, Adults, Seniors, All Ages | Target demographic |
130: | **Gender** | Men-only, Women-only, Mixed, Family | Audience type |
131: | **Location** | Country, Region, City, Radius | Geographic filtering with PostGIS |
132: | **Language** | Arabic, English, French, etc. | Event language |
133: | **Event Type** | Webinar, Conference | Event Type |
134: | **Madhab** | Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali | Islamic jurisprudence school |
135: | **Category** | Aqidah, Fiqh, Tafsir, Hadith, etc. | Event classification |
136: | **Tag** | Mohammed Hijab, Mufti Menk etc... | Event tags |
137: | **TagType** | Person, Channel, oeuvres | Tag classification |
138: | **TagTypeTags** | Specific tags within TagType | e.g., Person → Mohammed Hijab |
139: | **Event Format** | In-person Local (physical), Digital (online), Hybrid | Event format |
140: | **Date/Time** | Upcoming, This Week, This Month, Custom | Temporal filtering |
141: | **Verification** | Verified only, All | Trust level |
142: 
143: ## Liturgical Temporal Engine
144: 
145: **Dynamic Prayer-Relative Scheduling**:
146: 
147: - Events can be scheduled relative to prayer times (e.g., "15 minutes after Maghrib")
148: - exact times based on event geolocation using Third-party API
149: 
150: ## Moderation System
151: 
152: Still todo
153: 
154: ## Data Portability
155: 
156: Export formats supported:
157: - **iCal/ICS**: Standard calendar format for events
158: - **CSV**: Attendee lists, organizations, bulk data
159: - **ActivityPub-native** (planned): Federation-compatible JSON-LD
160: - **Full database dump**: Complete data export for self-hosters
161: 
162: ---
````

## File: docs/SECURITY.md
````markdown
  1: # Security Architecture
  2: 
  3: This document provides a high-level overview of the security architecture for the ISLAMU Event platform.
  4: 
  5: For detailed implementation patterns, code examples, and specific conventions, refer to the **`auth-patterns` skill**.
  6: 
  7: ## 1. Authentication Strategy: Backend-for-Frontend (BFF)
  8: 
  9: The project employs a **Backend-for-Frontend (BFF)** security model to provide a high level of security by ensuring that no tokens are ever exposed to the end-user's browser.
 10: 
 11: **Protocol**: OpenID Connect (OIDC) / OAuth 2.0  
 12: **Provider**: Keycloak
 13: 
 14: ### Conceptual Flow
 15: 
 16: The authentication flow is designed to separate the concerns of browser session management from backend API authorization.
 17: 
 18: ```mermaid
 19: sequenceDiagram
 20:     participant Browser (Blazor WASM)
 21:     participant BFF (Blazor Server)
 22:     participant Keycloak
 23:     participant API (Backend)
 24: 
 25:     Browser->>+BFF: User clicks "Login"
 26:     BFF->>+Keycloak: Initiates OIDC Authorization Code Flow
 27:     Keycloak-->>-BFF: Redirects with Authorization Code
 28:     BFF->>+Keycloak: Exchanges Code for Tokens (Access + Refresh)
 29:     Keycloak-->>-BFF: Returns JWTs
 30:     BFF-->>-Browser: Stores tokens in a secure, HttpOnly cookie & redirects
 31: 
 32:     Browser->>+BFF: Makes API call
 33:     BFF->>+API: YARP proxy attaches JWT Bearer token
 34:     API->>API: Validates JWT
 35:     API-->>-BFF: Returns data
 36:     BFF-->>-Browser: Returns data
 37: ```
 38: 
 39: ### Key Architectural Principles
 40: 
 41: *   **`Explore.Blazor` (The BFF)** is the only component that communicates directly with Keycloak. It manages the user's session using a secure, server-side, `HttpOnly` cookie.
 42: *   **`Explore.Blazor.Client` (The Frontend)** is completely unaware of OIDC or JWTs. It operates like a traditional web application, automatically sending the session cookie with every request to its backend (the BFF).
 43: *   **`Explore.API` (The Backend Resource)** is a stateless service. It only accepts JWT Bearer tokens for authorization and has no knowledge of the user's session cookie. This allows the API to be used by other clients (e.g., mobile apps, other services) in the future.
 44: 
 45: ## 2. Authorization Strategy
 46: 
 47: ### Endpoint-Level Authorization
 48: 
 49: A simple and strict convention is followed for securing API endpoints:
 50: *   **Read operations (`GET`)** are generally public and decorated with `[AllowAnonymous]`.
 51: *   **Write operations (`POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`)** are protected and require a valid token, enforced with `[Authorize]`.
 52: 
 53: ### Resource-Level Authorization
 54: 
 55: Fine-grained, resource-level authorization (e.g., "can this user edit *this specific* event?") is the responsibility of the **Application Layer**, typically within the MediatR handlers. This logic is not handled at the controller level.
 56: 
 57: ### Policy-Based Authorization (Cerbos)
 58: 
 59: Cerbos is actively integrated as the policy decision point (PDP) for fine-grained authorization.
 60: 
 61: Current implementation overview:
 62: 
 63: *   **Application Layer** enforces resource/action checks via MediatR `AuthorizationBehavior` before command handlers execute.
 64: *   **Infrastructure Layer** delegates policy decisions to Cerbos via HTTP in `CerbosAuthorizationService` (implements `IAuthorizationProvider`).
 65: *   **Fallback Path** exists via `FallbackAuthorizationService` (also implements `IAuthorizationProvider`) when Cerbos is disabled by configuration. A `RuntimeAuthorizationProvider` wrapper selects the active provider based on the `AuthorizationProvider` system setting.
 66: *   **API HATEOAS Layer** filters links using Cerbos batch checks so clients only receive authorized actions.
 67: *   **Blazor UI** uses DB-backed admin claims for UX gating; server-side authorization remains the hard security boundary.
 68: 
 69: This keeps endpoint authorization simple (`[AllowAnonymous]` for public reads, `[Authorize]` for writes) while enforcing fine-grained resource policies centrally.
 70: 
 71: ## 3. Fine-Grained Authorization (Cerbos)
 72: 
 73: We use **Cerbos** as an external Policy Decision Point (PDP). This decouples authorization logic from application code.
 74: 
 75: ### 3.1. Implementation Pattern
 76: 
 77: 1.  **Define Policy**: Authorization rules are defined in YAML files in the `cerbos/policies` directory.
 78: 2.  **Decorate Command**: Use `[AuthorizeResource]` on MediatR commands (optionally with `ISecureRequest` for dynamic resource IDs).
 79: 
 80: ```csharp
 81: [AuthorizeResource("event", PermissionAction.Update)]
 82: public class UpdateEventCommand : IRequest<BaseCommandResponse>
 83: {
 84:     public Guid Id { get; set; }
 85: }
 86: ```
 87: 
 88: 3.  **Pipeline Enforcement**: The `AuthorizationBehavior` pipeline detects this attribute:
 89:     *   Extracts the User (Principal) from `IUserContext`.
 90:     *   Constructs the Resource (Kind: "event", ID: `command.Id`).
 91:     *   Calls Cerbos: `Check(principal, resource, "update")`.
 92:     *   If denied, throws `ForbiddenException`.
 93: 
 94: ### 3.2. Policy Structure
 95: 
 96: Cerbos policies follow a standard hierarchy:
 97: 
 98: *   **Resource Policy**: Rules for a specific resource type (e.g., `event.yaml`).
 99: *   **Principal Policy**: Rules for specific users/roles (rarely used, prefer roles in resource policies).
100: *   **Derived Roles**: Logic to map dynamic conditions to simple roles (e.g., `owner` if `request.auth.id == resource.attr.ownerId`).
101: 
102: ---
103: 
104: ## 4. Multi-Tenancy & Keycloak
105: 
106: ### 4.1. Tenant Isolation
107: 
108: *   **Data Layer**: Enforced via Global Query Filters (`TenantId`).
109: *   **Auth Layer**: Keycloak manages identity.
110: 
111: ### 4.2. Keycloak Configuration Models
112: 
113: The system supports two multi-tenancy models in Keycloak:
114: 
115: 1.  **Shared Realm (Default)**:
116:     *   All tenants live in one Keycloak Realm.
117:     *   `TenantId` is stored as a custom attribute on the User or Group.
118:     *   Pros: Simpler management, Single Sign-On (SSO) across tenants.
119:     *   Cons: Less isolation between tenant user directories.
120: 
121: 2.  **Realm-per-Tenant**:
122:     *   Each tenant has its own Keycloak Realm.
123:     *   Pros: Total isolation, tenant-specific login pages/policies.
124:     *   Cons: No SSO, higher management overhead.
125: 
126: *Current Implementation assumes **Shared Realm** with Group-based tenancy.*
127: 
128: ---
129: 
130: ## 5. Secret Management (Infisical)
131: 
132: We use **Infisical** to manage secrets (DB connection strings, API keys, Client Secrets) at runtime.
133: 
134: *   **No Hardcoded Secrets**: `appsettings.json` contains only placeholders or non-sensitive config.
135: *   **Runtime Injection**: `AddInfisicalBlazorCompatibility()` loads secrets into the `.NET Configuration` provider at startup.
136: *   **Rotation**: Secrets can be rotated in Infisical without code changes (requires app restart).
137: 
138: ---
139: 
140: ## 6. Client-Side Authorization (UX-Only)
141: 
142: Blazor WASM receives user claims via the BFF pattern — the server serializes admin authority claims into the authentication cookie, and `AddAuthenticationStateSerialization` makes them available to the client.
143: 
144: ### What Client-Side Auth Does
145: 
146: - **Route guards** (`AdminRouteGuard`): Redirect unauthorized users away from admin pages
147: - **UI visibility**: Hide buttons, menu items, and actions the user cannot perform
148: - **Form validation**: Disable fields the user shouldn't edit
149: 
150: ### What Client-Side Auth Does NOT Do
151: 
152: Client-side authorization checks are **UX conveniences only**. They:
153: 
154: - **Cannot prevent unauthorized access** — a user can bypass Blazor WASM checks trivially
155: - **Cannot enforce security policies** — all enforcement happens server-side
156: - **Cannot be trusted** for any security decision
157: 
158: ### The Hard Security Boundary
159: 
160: ```
161: Blazor WASM (client)          →  UX gating only (hide/show)
162:      │
163:      ▼
164: Blazor Server BFF (server)    →  Cookie auth, YARP proxy
165:      │
166:      ▼
167: API Controller (server)       →  [Authorize] + JWT validation
168:      │
169:      ▼
170: AuthorizationBehavior (server) →  THE ENFORCEMENT POINT
171:      │                            Calls IAuthorizationProvider
172:      │                            Throws ForbiddenException if denied
173:      ▼
174: Handler (server)              →  Business logic (only runs if authorized)
175: ```
176: 
177: `AuthorizationBehavior` in the MediatR pipeline is the **only** authorization enforcement point. Every write operation passes through it before reaching the handler.
178: 
179: For pattern details, see [AUTHORIZATION_PATTERNS.md](AUTHORIZATION_PATTERNS.md).
180: 
181: ---
182: For implementation details, see the `auth-patterns` skill.
````

 74:     private static PaginatedResult<EventListDto> CreateResult(int pageNumber, int pageSize, List<EventListDto> items)
 75:     {
 76:         return new PaginatedResult<EventListDto>
 77:         {
 78:             Items = items,
 79:             PageNumber = pageNumber,
 80:             PageSize = pageSize,
 81:             TotalCount = items.Count
 82:         };
 83:     }

 85:     private void SetupPagedResult(Task<PaginatedResult<EventListDto>> resultTask)
 86:     {
 87:         _eventService.GetEventsPagedAsync(
 88:             Arg.Any<int>(),
 89:             Arg.Any<int>(),
 90:             Arg.Any<string?>(),
 91:             Arg.Any<Guid?>(),
 92:             Arg.Any<Guid?>(),
 93:             Arg.Any<int?>(),
 94:             Arg.Any<int?>(),
 95:             Arg.Any<Guid?>(),
 96:             Arg.Any<int?>(),
 97:             Arg.Any<int?>(),
 98:             Arg.Any<DateTimeOffset?>(),
 99:             Arg.Any<DateTimeOffset?>(),
100:             Arg.Any<string?>(),
101:             Arg.Any<bool?>(),
102:             Arg.Any<int?>(),
103:             Arg.Any<int?>(),
104:             Arg.Any<int?>(),
105:             Arg.Any<int?>(),
106:             Arg.Any<int?>(),
107:             Arg.Any<bool?>(),
108:             Arg.Any<int?>(),
109:             Arg.Any<int?>(),
110:             Arg.Any<bool?>(),
111:             Arg.Any<int?>(),
112:             Arg.Any<bool?>(),
113:             Arg.Any<bool?>(),
114:             Arg.Any<bool?>(),
115:             Arg.Any<string?>(),
116:             Arg.Any<bool?>(),
117:             Arg.Any<CancellationToken>())
118:             .Returns(resultTask);
119:     }
120: 
121:     private static async Task InvokeLoadEventsAsync(IRenderedComponent<EventList> cut)
122:     {
123:         var loadEventsMethod = typeof(EventList).GetMethod("LoadEventsAsync", System.Reflection.BindingFlags.Instance | System.Reflection.BindingFlags.NonPublic);
124:         if (loadEventsMethod is null)
125:         {
126:             throw new InvalidOperationException("LoadEventsAsync method was not found on EventList.");
127:         }
128: 
129:         var request = new ItemsProviderRequest(startIndex: 0, count: 20, cancellationToken: CancellationToken.None);
130:         await cut.InvokeAsync(async () =>
131:         {
132:             var valueTask = (ValueTask<ItemsProviderResult<EventListDto>>)loadEventsMethod.Invoke(cut.Instance, [request])!;
133:             await valueTask;
134:         });
135:     }
136: 
137:     [Test]
138:     public async Task EventList_DoesNotShowEmptyState_BeforeFirstEventsLoadCompletes()
139:     {
140: 
141:         var pendingResult = new TaskCompletionSource<PaginatedResult<EventListDto>>();
142:         SetupPagedResult(pendingResult.Task);
143: 
144: 
145:         var cut = _ctx.RenderMudComponent<EventList>();
146: 
147: 
148:         if (cut.Markup.Contains("No events found"))
149:         {
150:             throw new InvalidOperationException("Empty state should not be displayed before first events load completes.");
151:         }
152: 
153: 
154:         pendingResult.TrySetResult(CreateResult(1, 20, []));
155:         await Task.CompletedTask;
156:     }
157: 
158:     [Test]
159:     public async Task EventList_ShowsNoEventsState_OnlyAfterInitialLoadCompletesWithEmptyResult()
160:     {
161: 
162:         var pendingResult = new TaskCompletionSource<PaginatedResult<EventListDto>>();
163:         SetupPagedResult(pendingResult.Task);
164: 
165: 
166:         var cut = _ctx.RenderMudComponent<EventList>();
167: 
168: 
169:         cut.WaitForAssertion(() =>
170:         {
171:             if (cut.Markup.Contains("No events found"))
172:             {
173:                 throw new InvalidOperationException("Empty state should not be visible before first event load completes.");
174:             }
175:         });
176: 
177: 
178:         pendingResult.SetResult(CreateResult(1, 20, []));
179:         await InvokeLoadEventsAsync(cut);
180: 
181:         if (!cut.Markup.Contains("No events found"))
182:         {
183:             throw new InvalidOperationException("Expected empty-state message after completed empty load.");
184:         }
185: 
186:         await Task.CompletedTask;
187:     }
188: 
189:     [Test]
190:     public async Task EventList_HidesNoEventsState_WhenResultsExist()
191:     {
192: 
193:         var events = new List<EventListDto>
194:         {
195:             new() { Id = Guid.NewGuid(), Title = "Blazor Summit", Description = "Event description" }
196:         };
197:         SetupPagedResult(Task.FromResult(CreateResult(1, 20, events)));
198: 
199: 
200:         var cut = _ctx.RenderMudComponent<EventList>();
201: 
202: 
203:         await InvokeLoadEventsAsync(cut);
204: 
205:         if (!cut.Markup.Contains("Blazor Summit"))
206:         {
207:             throw new InvalidOperationException("Expected event title in rendered markup.");
208:         }
209: 
210:         if (cut.Markup.Contains("No events found"))
211:         {
212:             throw new InvalidOperationException("Empty-state message should not be visible when events exist.");
213:         }
214: 
215:         if (!cut.Markup.Contains("1 events found"))
216:         {
217:             throw new InvalidOperationException("Expected total count text for non-empty result.");
218:         }
219: 
220:         await Task.CompletedTask;
221:     }
222: }

## File: Explore.Blazor.Client/Components/Event/EventSessionManager.razor
````razor
  1: @using Explore.Blazor.Client.Clients
  2: @using MudBlazor
  3: @inject IDialogService DialogService
  4: @inject IEventService EventService
  5: @inject ISnackbar Snackbar
  6: 
  7: <div class="event-session-manager">
  8:     @if (_isLoading)
  9:     {
 10:         <div class="d-flex justify-center pa-4">
 11:             <MudProgressCircular Color="Color.Primary" Indeterminate="true" />
 12:         </div>
 13:     }
 14:     else if (Sessions.Count > 1)
 15:     {
 16:         <MudStack Spacing="3">
 17:             @foreach (var session in Sessions)
 18:             {
 19:                 <MudPaper Elevation="0" Class="pa-4 border-solid border-1 mud-border-lines-default rounded-lg">
 20:                     <div class="d-flex flex-wrap gap-4 justify-space-between align-center">
 21:                         <div>
 22:                             <MudText Typo="Typo.h6">@session.Title</MudText>
 23:                             <div class="d-flex align-center gap-4 mt-1">
 24:                                 <div class="d-flex align-center gap-1">
 25:                                     <MudIcon Icon="@Icons.Material.Filled.CalendarToday" Size="Size.Small" Color="Color.Secondary" />
 26:                                     <MudText Typo="Typo.body2" Color="Color.Secondary">
 27:                                         @(session.StartTime?.ToString("f") ?? "")
 28:                                     </MudText>
 29:                                 </div>
 30:                                 <div class="d-flex align-center gap-1">
 31:                                     <MudIcon Icon="@Icons.Material.Filled.LocationOn" Size="Size.Small" Color="Color.Secondary" />
 32:                                     <MudText Typo="Typo.body2" Color="Color.Secondary">
 33:                                         @session.LocationFullName
 34:                                     </MudText>
 35:                                 </div>
 36:                             </div>
 37:                         </div>
 38:                         
 39:                         <div>
 40:                             @if (ShowRegisterButton)
 41:                             {
 42:                                 <MudButton Variant="Variant.Outlined" 
 43:                                            Color="Color.Primary" 
 44:                                            OnClick="@(() => OnRegisterClick.InvokeAsync(session))">
 45:                                     Register
 46:                                 </MudButton>
 47:                             }
 48:                         </div>
 49:                     </div>
 50:                 </MudPaper>
 51:             }
 52:         </MudStack>
 53:     }
 54:     else if (Sessions.Count == 0)
 55:     {
 56:         <MudAlert Severity="Severity.Info">No sessions available.</MudAlert>
 57:     }
 58:     else
 59:     {
 60:         // Single session case - intentionally empty or minimal if desired
 61:         // The parent component handles the display for single session
 62:     }
 63: </div>
 64: 
 65: @code {
 66:     [Parameter] public Guid EventId { get; set; }
 67:     [Parameter] public bool ShowRegisterButton { get; set; } = false;
 68:     [Parameter] public EventCallback<EventSessionListDto> OnRegisterClick { get; set; }
 69: 
 70:     public List<EventSessionListDto> Sessions { get; private set; } = new();
 71:     
 72:     private Guid _previousEventId;
 73:     private bool _isLoading = true;
 74: 
 75:     protected override async Task OnParametersSetAsync()
 76:     {
 77:         if (EventId != Guid.Empty && EventId != _previousEventId)
 78:         {
 79:             _previousEventId = EventId;
 80:             await LoadSessions();
 81:         }
 82:     }
 83: 
 84:     public async Task LoadSessions()
 85:     {
 86:         _isLoading = true;
 87:         try
 88:         {
 89:             var result = await EventService.GetSessionsByEventAsync(EventId);
 90:             Sessions = result.OrderBy(s => s.StartTime).ToList();
 91:         }
 92:         catch (Exception ex)
 93:         {
 94:             Snackbar.Add($"Error loading sessions: {ex.Message}", Severity.Error);
 95:             Sessions = new List<EventSessionListDto>();
 96:         }
 97:         finally
 98:         {
 99:             _isLoading = false;
100:             StateHasChanged();
101:         }
102:     }
103: }

  1: using System.Net.Http;

  7: using MudBlazor;
  8: 
  9: namespace Explore.Blazor.Client.Layout;
 10: 
 11: public partial class MainLayout : LayoutComponentBase, IDisposable
 12: {
 13:     private bool _isDarkMode = false;
 14:     private bool _isInitialized = false;
 15:     private MudTheme? _theme;
 16:     private MudThemeProvider _mudThemeProvider = null!;
 17:     private bool _hideChrome;
 18: 
 19:     [Inject]
 20:     protected IUserService UserService { get; set; } = null!;
 21: 
 22:     [Inject]
 23:     protected AuthenticationStateProvider AuthenticationStateProvider { get; set; } = null!;
 24: 
 25:     [Inject]
 26:     protected ILogger<MainLayout> Logger { get; set; } = null!;
 27: 
 28:     [Inject]
 29:     protected HttpClient HttpClient { get; set; } = null!;
 30: 
 31:     [Inject]
 32:     protected NavigationManager NavigationManager { get; set; } = null!;
 33: 
 34:     [CascadingParameter(Name = "InitialTheme")]
 35:     public bool? InitialTheme { get; set; }
 36: 
 37:     public string DarkLightModeButtonIcon => _isDarkMode switch
 38:     {
 39:         true => Icons.Material.Rounded.AutoMode,
 40:         false => Icons.Material.Outlined.DarkMode,
 41:     };
 42: 
 43:     protected override void OnInitialized()
 44:     {
 45:         base.OnInitialized();
 46: 
 47: 
 48:         if (InitialTheme.HasValue)
 49:         {
 50:             _isDarkMode = InitialTheme.Value;
 51:         }
 52: 
 53:         _theme = new()
 54:         {
 55:             PaletteLight = _lightPalette,
 56:             PaletteDark = _darkPalette,
 57:             LayoutProperties = new LayoutProperties()
 58:         };
 59: 
 60:         UpdateChromeVisibility();
 61:         NavigationManager.LocationChanged += OnLocationChanged;
 62:     }
 63: 
 64:     protected override async Task OnAfterRenderAsync(bool firstRender)
 65:     {
 66:         if (firstRender)
 67:         {
 68: 
 69:             try
 70:             {
 71:                 var authState = await AuthenticationStateProvider.GetAuthenticationStateAsync();
 72:                 if (authState.User.Identity?.IsAuthenticated == true)
 73:                 {
 74:                     await UserService.SyncUserAsync();
 75:                 }
 76:             }
 77:             catch (Exception ex)
 78:             {
 79:                 Logger.LogWarning(ex, "Error syncing user");
 80:             }
 81: 
 82: 
 83:             if (!InitialTheme.HasValue)
 84:             {
 85:                 try
 86:                 {
 87: 
 88:                     _isDarkMode = false;
 89: 
 90: 
 91:                     var systemDark = await _mudThemeProvider.GetSystemDarkModeAsync();
 92:                     if (systemDark)
 93:                     {
 94:                         _isDarkMode = true;
 95:                         await InvokeAsync(StateHasChanged);
 96:                     }
 97:                 }
 98:                 catch (Exception ex)
 99:                 {
100:                     Logger.LogWarning(ex, "Error initializing theme");
101:                 }
102:             }
103: 
104:             _isInitialized = true;
105:         }
106:     }
107: 
108:     private async Task DarkModeToggle()
109:     {
110:         _isDarkMode = !_isDarkMode;
111:         var themeValue = _isDarkMode ? "dark" : "light";
112: 
113:         try
114:         {
115: 
116:             await HttpClient.PostAsync($"/bff/theme?theme={Uri.EscapeDataString(themeValue)}", null);
117:         }
118:         catch (Exception ex)
119:         {
120:             Logger.LogWarning(ex, "Error saving theme preference");
121:         }
122:     }
123:

172:         Warning = "#FFC107",

174:         LinesDefault = "#333333",
175:         TableLines = "#333333",

179: 
180:     private void OnLocationChanged(object? sender, LocationChangedEventArgs e)
181:     {
182:         UpdateChromeVisibility();
183:         _ = InvokeAsync(StateHasChanged);
184:     }
185: 
186:     private void UpdateChromeVisibility()
187:     {
188:         var relative = NavigationManager.ToBaseRelativePath(NavigationManager.Uri);
189:         var path = relative.Split('?', '#')[0];
190: 
191:         if (!path.StartsWith('/'))
192:         {
193:             path = "/" + path;
194:         }
195: 
196:         if (path.Length > 1)
197:         {
198:             path = path.TrimEnd('/');
199:         }
200: 
201:         _hideChrome = path.Equals("/setup", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
202:             || path.StartsWith("/onboarding/", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase)
203:             || path.Equals("/startup", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
204:     }
205: 
206:     public void Dispose()
207:     {
208:         NavigationManager.LocationChanged -= OnLocationChanged;
209:     }
210: }

227:                         @if (IsSingleTenantMode)
228:                         {
229:                             <MudText Typo="Typo.body2"><strong>First Host Choice:</strong> @GetFirstHostChoiceLabel()</MudText>
230:                         }
231: 
232:                         <MudAlert Severity="Severity.Info" Variant="Variant.Outlined">
233:                             @GetCompletionRedirectHint()
234:                         </MudAlert>
235:                     </MudStack>
236:                     </MudStep>
237:                 </ChildContent>
238: 
239:                 <ActionContent Context="stepper">
240:                     <MudButton Variant="Variant.Text"
241:                                Color="Color.Default"
242:                                Disabled="@(_activeStep == 0 || _isSaving)"
243:                                OnClick="@(() => stepper.PreviousStepAsync())">
244:                         Back
245:                     </MudButton>
246:                     <MudSpacer />
247: 
248:                     @if (_activeStep < LastStepIndex)
249:                     {
250:                         <MudButton Variant="Variant.Filled"
251:                                    Color="Color.Primary"
252:                                    OnClick="@(() => GoToNextStepAsync(stepper))"
253:                                    Disabled="@(_isSaving || IsNextDisabled)">
254:                             Next
255:                         </MudButton>
256:                     }
257:                     else
258:                     {
259:                         <MudButton Variant="Variant.Filled"
260:                                    Color="Color.Primary"
261:                                    OnClick="CompleteOnboardingAsync"
262:                                    Disabled="@(_isSaving || IsCompleteDisabled)">
263:                             @_completeButtonLabel
264:                         </MudButton>
265:                     }
266:                 </ActionContent>
267:             </MudStepper>
268:         }
269:     </MudPaper>
270: </MudContainer>
271: 
272: @code {
273:     private enum FirstHostSetupChoice
274:     {
275:         None = 0,
276:         Personal = 1,
277:         GroupQuickSetup = 2,
278:         Organization = 3,
279:         DoLater = 4
280:     }
281: 
282:     private const int FirstHostStepIndex = 2;
283:     private InstanceGovernanceSettingsModel _model = new();
284:     private bool _isLoading = true;
285:     private bool _isSaving;
286:     private string? _errorMessage;
287:     private bool _setupSecretSynced;
288:     private int _activeStep;
289:     private UserDto? _currentUser;
290:     private FirstHostSetupChoice _firstHostSetupChoice = FirstHostSetupChoice.None;
291:     private string _completeButtonLabel = "Complete Instance Onboarding";
292: 
293:     private bool IsSingleTenantMode => _model.DeploymentMode.Equals("SingleTenant", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
294:     private bool IsMultiTenantMode => _model.DeploymentMode.Equals("MultiTenant", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
295:     private int LastStepIndex => IsSingleTenantMode ? 3 : 2;
296:     private bool IsFirstHostSelectionMissing => IsSingleTenantMode && _firstHostSetupChoice == FirstHostSetupChoice.None;
297:     private bool IsNextDisabled => _activeStep == FirstHostStepIndex && IsFirstHostSelectionMissing;
298:     private bool IsCompleteDisabled => IsFirstHostSelectionMissing;
299: 
300:     protected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()
301:     {
302:         try
303:         {
304:             await UserService.SyncUserAsync();
305:             _currentUser = await UserService.GetCurrentUserAsync();
306:         }
307:         catch (Exception ex)
308:         {
309:             Logger.LogWarning(ex, "Could not fully hydrate user context during instance onboarding.");
310:         }
311: 
312:         var status = await InstanceOnboardingService.GetStatusAsync();
313:         if (status?.IsCompleted == true)
314:         {
315:             Navigation.NavigateTo("/startup");
316:             return;
317:         }
318: 
319:         _model = await InstanceOnboardingService.GetSettingsAsync();
320:         if (!IsMultiTenantMode)
321:         {
322:             _model.AllowTenantWhiteLabeling = false;
323:         }
324: 
325:         _isLoading = false;
326:     }
327: 
328:     protected override async Task OnAfterRenderAsync(bool firstRender)
329:     {
330:         if (!firstRender || _setupSecretSynced)
331:         {
332:             return;
333:         }
334: 
335:         var secret = (await JSRuntime.InvokeAsync<string?>("sessionStorage.getItem", "setup-secret"))?.Trim();
336:         if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(secret))
337:         {
338:             return;
339:         }
340: 
341:         var syncResponse = await Http.PostAsJsonAsync("/bff/setup-secret/sync", new { Secret = secret });
342:         if (syncResponse.IsSuccessStatusCode)
343:         {
344:             _setupSecretSynced = true;
345:         }
346:     }
347: 
348:     private void OnDeploymentModeChanged(string deploymentMode)
349:     {
350:         _model.DeploymentMode = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(deploymentMode) ? "SingleTenant" : deploymentMode.Trim();
351:         if (!IsMultiTenantMode)
352:         {
353:             _model.AllowTenantWhiteLabeling = false;
354:         }
355: 
356:         if (_activeStep > LastStepIndex)
357:         {
358:             _activeStep = LastStepIndex;
359:         }
360: 
361:         _errorMessage = null;
362:     }
363: 
364:     private async Task GoToNextStepAsync(MudStepper stepper)
365:     {
366:         _errorMessage = null;
367: 
368:         if (IsNextDisabled)
369:         {
370:             _errorMessage = "Please choose how you want to set up your first host before continuing.";
371:             return;
372:         }
373: 
374:         await stepper.NextStepAsync();
375:     }
376: 
377:     private void SelectFirstHost(FirstHostSetupChoice choice)
378:     {
379:         _firstHostSetupChoice = choice;
380:         _errorMessage = null;
381:     }
382: 
383:     private Variant GetFirstHostButtonVariant(FirstHostSetupChoice choice) =>
384:         _firstHostSetupChoice == choice ? Variant.Filled : Variant.Outlined;
385: 
386:     private Color GetFirstHostButtonColor(FirstHostSetupChoice choice) =>
387:         _firstHostSetupChoice == choice ? Color.Primary : Color.Default;
388: 
389:     private string GetFirstHostChoiceLabel()
390:     {
391:         return _firstHostSetupChoice switch
392:         {
393:             FirstHostSetupChoice.Personal => "Publish under my account",
394:             FirstHostSetupChoice.GroupQuickSetup => "Group (informal quick setup)",
395:             FirstHostSetupChoice.Organization => "Organization (formal setup)",
396:             FirstHostSetupChoice.DoLater => "I will do this later",
397:             _ => "Not selected"
398:         };
399:     }
400: 
401:     private string GetCompletionRedirectHint()
402:     {
403:         if (IsMultiTenantMode)
404:         {
405:             return "After completion, you will be redirected to instance administration pages.";
406:         }
407: 
408:         return _firstHostSetupChoice switch
409:         {
410:             FirstHostSetupChoice.Organization => "After completion, you will be redirected to create your organization profile first.",
411:             _ => "After completion, you will be redirected to the event list."
412:         };
413:     }
414: 
415:     private async Task CompleteOnboardingAsync()
416:     {
417:         if (IsCompleteDisabled)
418:         {
419:             _errorMessage = "Please choose how you want to set up your first host before completing onboarding.";
420:             return;
421:         }
422: 
423:         _isSaving = true;
424:         _completeButtonLabel = "Saving...";
425:         _errorMessage = null;
426: 
427:         if (!IsMultiTenantMode)
428:         {
429:             _model.AllowTenantWhiteLabeling = false;
430:         }
431: 
432:         var response = await InstanceOnboardingService.CompleteAsync(_model);
433:         _isSaving = false;
434:         _completeButtonLabel = "Complete Instance Onboarding";
435: 
436:         if (response.Success)
437:         {
438:             Snackbar.Add("Instance onboarding completed.", Severity.Success);
439:             await NavigatePostCompletionAsync();
440:             return;
441:         }
442: 
443:         _errorMessage = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(response.Message)
444:             ? "Failed to complete onboarding."
445:             : response.Message;
446:     }
447: 
448:     private async Task NavigatePostCompletionAsync()
449:     {
450:         if (IsMultiTenantMode)
451:         {
452:             Navigation.NavigateTo("/admin/instance/settings");
453:             return;
454:         }
455: 
456:         switch (_firstHostSetupChoice)
457:         {
458:             case FirstHostSetupChoice.Organization:
459:                 Snackbar.Add("Complete your organization profile now to publish events as an organization.", Severity.Info);
460:                 Navigation.NavigateTo("/organization/create");
461:                 return;
462: 
463:             case FirstHostSetupChoice.GroupQuickSetup:
464:             {
465:                 var created = await TryCreateQuickGroupAsync();
466:                 if (created)
467:                 {
468:                     Snackbar.Add("Starter group created. You can now publish events under your group.", Severity.Success);
469:                 }
470:                 else
471:                 {
472:                     Snackbar.Add("Could not create the starter group automatically. You can set up a group later.", Severity.Warning);
473:                 }
474: 
475:                 Navigation.NavigateTo("/events");
476:                 return;
477:             }
478: 
479:             case FirstHostSetupChoice.Personal:
480:                 Snackbar.Add("You can publish events under your account immediately.", Severity.Info);
481:                 Navigation.NavigateTo("/events");
482:                 return;
483: 
484:             case FirstHostSetupChoice.DoLater:
485:             default:
486:                 Snackbar.Add("You can set up a group or organization later from your account area.", Severity.Info);
487:                 Navigation.NavigateTo("/events");
488:                 return;
489:         }
490:     }
491: 
492:     private async Task<bool> TryCreateQuickGroupAsync()
493:     {
494:         var groupName = BuildDefaultGroupName();
495:         return await GroupService.CreateGroupAsync(groupName, "Starter group created during instance onboarding.");
496:     }
497: 
498:     private string BuildDefaultGroupName()
499:     {
500:         var fullName = string.Join(" ", new[] { _currentUser?.FirstName, _currentUser?.LastName }
501:             .Where(s => !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(s))
502:             .Select(s => s!.Trim()));
503: 
504:         if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(fullName))
505:         {
506:             return $"{fullName}'s Group";
507:         }
508: 
509:         if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(_currentUser?.Username))
510:         {
511:             return $"{_currentUser.Username!.Trim()}'s Group";
512:         }
513: 
514:         return "My Group";
515:     }
516: }

  9: public interface ICategoryService
 10: {
 11:     Task<ICollection<CategoryListDto>> GetCategoriesAsync();
 12:     Task<ICollection<CategoryListDto>> GetAllCategoriesAsync();
 13:     Task<PaginatedResult<CategoryListDto>> GetCategoriesPagedAsync(int pageNumber, int pageSize);
 14:     Task<CategoryDto?> GetCategoryByIdAsync(Guid categoryId);
 15:     Task<BaseCommandResponseOfGuid?> CreateCategoryAsync(CreateCategoryDto dto);
 16:     Task<BaseCommandResponseOfGuid?> UpdateCategoryAsync(Guid id, UpdateCategoryDto dto);
 17:     Task<bool> DeleteCategoryAsync(Guid categoryId);
 18:     Task<ICollection<object>> GetCategoriesByEventAsync(Guid eventId);
 19:     Task<ICollection<object>> GetEventsByCategoryAsync(Guid categoryId);
 20:     Task<BaseCommandResponseOfGuid?> AssignCategoryToEventAsync(object dto);
 21:     Task<bool> RemoveCategoryFromEventAsync(Guid eventCategoryId);
 22: }
 23: 
 24: public class CategoryService : ICategoryService
 25: {
 26:     private readonly IEventApiClient _apiClient;
 27:     private readonly ILogger<CategoryService> _logger;
 28: 
 29:     public CategoryService(IEventApiClient apiClient, ILogger<CategoryService> logger)
 30:     {
 31:         _apiClient = apiClient ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(apiClient));
 32:         _logger = logger ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(logger));
 33:     }
 34: 
 35:     public async Task<ICollection<CategoryListDto>> GetCategoriesAsync()
 36:     {
 37:         try
 38:         {
 39:             var result = await _apiClient.GetCategoriesAsync(pageNumber: ApiConstants.FirstPage, pageSize: ApiConstants.DefaultPageSize);
 40:             return result?.GetItems() ?? new List<CategoryListDto>();
 41:         }
 42:         catch (ApiException ex)
 43:         {
 44:             _logger.LogError(ex, "[CATEGORY SERVICE] API error fetching categories: {StatusCode}", ex.StatusCode);
 45:             return new List<CategoryListDto>();
 46:         }
 47:     }
 48: 
 49:     public Task<ICollection<CategoryListDto>> GetAllCategoriesAsync() => GetCategoriesAsync();
 50: 
 51:     public async Task<PaginatedResult<CategoryListDto>> GetCategoriesPagedAsync(int pageNumber, int pageSize)
 52:     {
 53:         try

  5: # ISLAMU Event
  6: 
  7: # Event Platform & Management System — v0.1.0 Beta
  8: 
  9: ⚠️ **Beta Release**: Currently at v0.1.0 — First public release ready for beta testing and early adopters. API may change before 1.0.0 stable release.
 10: 
 11: ISLAMU Event is a self-hostable, decentralized, multi-tenant event platform for any community or industry.
 12: The ISLAMU organization hosts a public instance focused on Islamic events, but the software itself is purpose-agnostic, fully white-label, and designed to be rebranded for any use case.

 30: ## ℹ About ISLAMU Event
 31: 
 32: ISLAMU Event is a **self-hostable event discovery and management platform** that helps communities find, organize, and promote events. Built with advanced filtering, verification workflows, and cultural intelligence to serve diverse communities worldwide.
 33: 
 34: > **v0.1.0 Beta** — First public release ready for beta testing. [See what's included →](docs/semantic_versioning/v0.1.0.md)
 35: 
 36: > Give us a Star ⭐️
 37: 
 38: ### Platform Flexibility
 39: - **The software is general-purpose**: Adaptable for any kind of events, communities, and organizations (tech meetups, conferences, workshops, community gatherings)
 40: - **The ISLAMU-hosted instance is Islamic-focused**: Our public instance at [event.openislamu.org](https://event.openislamu.org) is curated for Islamic events and community needs
 41: - **White-label ready**: Rebrand and customize the platform for your specific use case with full control over branding, policies, and features
 42: 
 43: ## ✨ Why ISLAMU Event
 44: 
 45: ### Key Differentiators
 46: 
 47: - **🔐 Security-First:** BFF pattern (no tokens in browser), Cerbos fine-grained authorization, Infisical secrets management
 48: - **🛡️ Verified Organizations:** Two-tier verification system for trust and quality
 49: - **⚡ Multi-Tenancy:** Runtime mode switching (Single-tenant ↔ Multi-tenant) without code changes
 50: - **🔧 Modular Events:** Plugin-style aspects (Islamic, Tech) with per-tenant enablement
 51: - **🎯 Cultural Intelligence:** Advanced filtering based on enabled modules. filter by madhab, gender, age, prayer times, skill level...
 52: - **🏗️ Enterprise Architecture:** Clean Architecture + CQRS with MediatR, REST Level 3 (HATEOAS)
 53: - **🌍 Federation-Ready:** ATProto/ActivityPub data models complete (Phase 1), protocol endpoints planned for 1.0.0
 54: - **🧪 Test Coverage:** 7 test projects (TUnit, bUnit, architecture tests)
 55: - **📖 Open Source:** AGPL-3.0 licensed for transparency and community ownership
 56: 
 57: ---
 58: 
 59: ## 🎯 Core Features (v0.1.0)
 60: 
 61: ### For Event Seekers
 62: 
 63: - **🔍 Advanced Discovery:** 33 query parameters including title search, date range, location radius, categories, tags, and more
 64: - **👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Culturally-Aware Filters:** Age ranges, gender segregation modes, madhab targeting, prayer-relative timing (for instances that enable these modules)
 65: - **🌐 Multi-Language Support:** Event sessions with multiple language options
 66: - **📱 Responsive Design:** Mobile-friendly Blazor UI with MudBlazor components
 67: - **✅ RSVP & Registration:** Waitlists, approval workflows, registration limits per session
 68: 
 69: ### For Event Organizers
 70: 
 71: - **📅 Multi-Session Events:** Conferences, seminars, recurring programs with speakers, agendas, and language variants
 72: - **🛡️ Organization Verification:** Two-tier system (user-submitted vs. verified organizations)
 73: - **👥 Member Management:** Invite members, assign roles (Owner, Admin, Editor, Viewer), track permissions
 74: - **⭐ Reviews & Ratings:** Users can review verified organizations to build trust
 75: - **🎯 Modular Event Types:** Enable Islamic or Tech aspects per event based on tenant configuration
 76: - **📊 Flexible Publishing:** Open registration, approval-required, or invite-only policies
 77: 
 78: ### For Platform Owners
 79: 
 80: - **🐳 Docker-Ready:** One-command deployment with `docker-compose up -d`
 81: - **💼 Multi-Tenancy:** Switch between single-tenant and SaaS modes at runtime without code changes
 82: - **🛠️ White-Label Control:** Custom branding, domains, logos, navigation links, policies per tenant
 83: - **🔧 Admin Hierarchy:** Instance admins, tenant admins, and organization admins with cascading settings
 84: - **🌍 Federation Foundation:** ATProto/ActivityPub data models complete (Phase 1), protocol endpoints planned for 1.0.0
 85: - **📚 Comprehensive Docs:** Architecture, deployment, configuration, troubleshooting, and API reference
 86: - **🔐 Enterprise Security:** BFF pattern, Cerbos authorization, Infisical secrets, HATEOAS REST API
 87: 
 88: ##  Deployment & Hosting Options
 89: 
 90: This platform is designed to be flexible and self-hostable for any organization.
 91: 
 92: - **Single-Instance Mode**: One organization or community per deployment
 93: - **Multi-Tenant SaaS Mode**: Multiple isolated tenants with custom domains and branding
 94: 
 95: See [Operations Guide][operations-doc] for full deployment details and examples.
 96: 
 97: ## 🎨 Branding & Customization
 98: 
 99: ISLAMU Event is built for white-label use:
100: 
101: - **Change instance name and domain**
102: - **Customize logos, colors, and UI**
103: - **Define your own categories, tags, and policies**
104: - **Decide who can publish events and how verification works**
105: 
106: See [Configuration Guide][configuration-doc] for full customization options.
107: 
108: ## 🛡️ Enterprise Security & Compliance
109: 
110: We treat security as a first-class citizen, not an afterthought.
111: 
112: * **Identity & Access:** Managed via **Keycloak**, supporting MFA, Social Login, and SAML/LDAP integration.
113: * **Authorization:** Fine-grained access control (FGAC) powered by **Cerbos**: Policy Decision Point that coordinates unified policy-based authorization, allowing for complex "Who can do what" logic with human readable yaml for non technical users.
114: * **Data Integrity:** All database interactions use **Parameterized EF Core queries** to eliminate SQL injection.
115: * **Secret Management:** Zero hardcoded credentials; all secrets are injected at runtime via **Infisical**.
116: * **Observability:** Integrated **OpenTelemetry** for distributed tracing and real-time security monitoring.
117: 
118: ### Security Features
119: 
120: - **🔒 HTTPS Enforcement:** All traffic encrypted with HSTS
121: - **🔐 Modern Authentication:** OAuth 2.0/OIDC via Keycloak
122: - **🗝️ Secret Management:** Infisical vault for credentials
123: - **🛡️ Authorization:** Policy-based access control via Cerbos
124: - **🔍 Input Validation:** FluentValidation + ASP.NET Core model binding
125: - **🚫 SQL Injection Prevention:** Parameterized queries (EF Core)
126: - **🌐 CORS:** Configurable origin whitelist
127: - **⏱️ Rate Limiting:** ASP.NET Core middleware
128: 
129: ### Extensibility Model
130: 
131: Events use **composition over inheritance**:
132: 
133: ```
134: Event (Core)
135:   ├── IslamicDetails (optional aspect)
136:   ├── TechDetails (optional aspect)
137:   └── EducationalDetails (optional aspect)
138: ```
139: 
140: A "Ramadan Tech Workshop" has both Islamic and Tech aspects. No class explosion.
141: 
142: See [EXTENSIBILITY.md](docs/EXTENSIBILITY.md) and [MODULAR_EVENTS.md](docs/MODULAR_EVENTS.md).
143:

261: ## 🏗️ Technical Overview
262: 
263: ISLAMU Event is built on **Clean Architecture + CQRS** with a **BFF (Backend-for-Frontend)** pattern.
264: 
265: ### Technology Stack (v0.1.0)
266: 
267: | Component | Technology | Purpose |
268: |-----------|------------|---------|
269: | **Runtime** | .NET 10.0 | Latest LTS framework |
270: | **Architecture** | Clean Architecture + CQRS | Layer separation with MediatR |
271: | **Frontend** | Blazor Server + WASM | Hybrid rendering (InteractiveAuto) |
272: | **UI Components** | MudBlazor | Material Design components |
273: | **Database** | PostgreSQL + PostGIS | Relational + spatial queries |
274: | **ORM** | Entity Framework Core 10 | Data access with named query filters |
275: | **Authentication** | Keycloak (OIDC/OAuth 2.0) | Identity provider with BFF pattern |
276: | **Authorization** | Cerbos | Policy Decision Point (PDP) for FGAC |
277: | **Secrets** | Infisical | Vault with auto-refresh + health checks |
278: | **API Docs** | Scalar + Swagger/NSwag | OpenAPI 3.0 with HAL+JSON |
279: | **Logging** | Serilog | Structured logging to Loki |
280: | **Telemetry** | OpenTelemetry | Distributed tracing + Prometheus metrics |
281: | **Orchestration** | .NET Aspire (dev), Docker (prod) | Service orchestration |
282: | **Test Framework** | TUnit + bUnit | Unit + integration + component tests |
283: 
284: ### The Request Lifecycle (CQRS)
285: We utilize **MediatR** for a decoupled command/query pipeline. This ensures that our business logic is isolated from transport layers (API/Blazor).
286: 
287: ```mermaid
288: graph TD
289:     subgraph Client_Layer [Presentation]
290:         A[Blazor WASM / Mobile] -->|HTTPS/REST| B[ASP.NET Core API]
291:     end
292: 
293:     subgraph Application_Layer [Business Logic]
294:         B -->|Command/Query| C[MediatR Pipeline]
295:         C -->|Validation| D[FluentValidation]
296:         D -->|Execution| E[Domain Handler]
297:     end
298: 
299:     subgraph Infrastructure_Layer [Data & Services]
300:         E -->|EF Core| F[(PostgreSQL + PostGIS)]
301:         E -->|OIDC| G[Keycloak]
302:         E -->|Events| H[Svix Webhooks]
303:     end
304: 
305:     E -.->|Future| I[ATProto / ActivityPub Gateway]
306: ```
307: 
308: ```mermaid
309: graph LR
310:     A[Request] --> B[Controller]
311:     B --> C[MediatR]
312:     C --> D[Handler]
313:     D --> E[Repository]
314:     E --> F[(PostgreSQL)]
315:     D --> G[Response]
316: ```
317:

## File: .claude/agents/README.md
````markdown
  1: ---
  2: name: Agents Documentation
  3: description: Documentation file - not an executable agent
  4: disabled: true
  5: ---
  6: 
  7: # Project Agents
  8: 
  9: > **Project-Agnostic Autonomous Agents for Complex Tasks**
 10: >
 11: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
 12: 
 13: Specialized autonomous agents for complex, multi-step tasks in Clean Architecture .NET projects.
 14: 
 15: ---
 16: 
 17: ## Overview
 18: 
 19: Agents are autonomous Claude instances that handle specific complex tasks. Unlike skills (which provide inline guidance), agents:
 20: 
 21: - Run as separate sub-tasks with focused objectives
 22: - Work autonomously with minimal supervision
 23: - Have specialized tool access for their domain
 24: - Return comprehensive reports upon completion
 25: 
 26: **Key Advantage**: Agents are standalone—just reference the agent name and Claude Code handles the rest.
 27: 
 28: ---
 29: 
 30: ## Available Agents
 31: 
 32: | Agent | Purpose | When to Use |
 33: |-------|---------|-------------|
 34: | [blazor-component-architect](#blazor-component-architect) | Design and review Blazor components | Component architecture, MudBlazor patterns, BFF compliance |
 35: | [code-architecture-reviewer](#code-architecture-reviewer) | Review code for architectural consistency | After implementing features, before merging changes |
 36: | [code-refactor-master](#code-refactor-master) | Enforce Clean Architecture with CQRS | Architecture violations, pattern compliance |
 37: | [documentation-architect](#documentation-architect) | Create comprehensive documentation | API docs, developer guides, architectural overviews |
 38: | [frontend-error-fixer](#frontend-error-fixer) | Debug Blazor frontend errors | Compilation errors, MudBlazor issues, render mode problems |
 39: | [plan-reviewer](#plan-reviewer) | Review development plans | Before starting complex features, validating approaches |
 40: | [refactor-planner](#refactor-planner) | Create refactoring strategies | Code reorganization, modernizing legacy code |
 41: | [web-research-specialist](#web-research-specialist) | Research technical issues | Debugging obscure errors, finding best practices |
 42: | [auth-route-tester](#auth-route-tester) | Test authenticated API endpoints | Validating endpoint functionality, debugging auth |
 43: | [auth-route-debugger](#auth-route-debugger) | Debug authentication issues | Token issues, cookie problems, permission errors |
 44: | [auto-error-resolver](#auto-error-resolver) | Automatically fix C#/.NET errors | Build failures, systematic error resolution |
