460: ---
461: 
462: ## 2. Get Entity List - Full Query Flow
463: 
464: ### List DTO (Optimized for Display)
465: 
466: **File**: `{Project}.Application/DTOs/{Entity}/{Entity}ListDto.cs`
467: 
468: ```csharp
469: using System;
470: 
471: namespace {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity};
472: 
473: public class {Entity}ListDto
474: {
475:     public {IdType} Id { get; set; }
476:     public string Title { get; set; }
477:     public string? Description { get; set; }
478:     public string? Slug { get; set; }
479: 
480:     // Lookup entity
481:     public {LookupIdType} {LookupEntity}Id { get; set; }
482:     public string {LookupEntity}FullName { get; set; }
483: 
484:     // Related entities
485:     public {LookupIdType} {RelatedEntity1}Id { get; set; }
486:     public string {RelatedEntity1}FullName { get; set; }
487:     public {LookupIdType} {RelatedEntity2}Id { get; set; }
488:     public string {RelatedEntity2}FullName { get; set; }
489: 
490:     // Parent entity (Owner)
491:     public {IdType} {ParentEntity}Id { get; set; }
492:     public string {ParentEntity}DisplayName { get; set; }
493: 
494:     // Pricing
495:     public decimal? Price { get; set; }
496:     public string? CurrencyCode { get; set; }
497: 
498:     // Featured Image
499:     public {IdType} FeaturedImageId { get; set; }
500:     public string? FeaturedImageUri { get; set; }
501: 
502:     // Configuration
503:     public bool IsActive { get; set; }
504:     public string? ExternalUrl { get; set; }
505: 
506:     // Status & Visibility
507:     public {LookupIdType} StatusId { get; set; }
508:     public string StatusFullName { get; set; }
509:     public {LookupIdType} VisibilityId { get; set; }
510:     public string VisibilityFullName { get; set; }
511: 
512:     // Date range
513:     public DateOnly? StartDate { get; set; }
514:     public DateOnly? EndDate { get; set; }
515:     public string? Timezone { get; set; }
516: 
517:     // Metadata
518:     public int ViewCount { get; set; }
519: 
520:     // Tenant
521:     public {IdType} TenantId { get; set; }
522: }
523: ```
524: 
525: ### Query Request
526: 
527: **File**: `{Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Requests/Queries/Get{Entity}ListRequest.cs`
528: 
529: ```csharp
530: using System.Collections.Generic;
531: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity};
532: using MediatR;
533: 
534: namespace {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Requests.Queries;
535: 
536: public class Get{Entity}ListRequest : IRequest<List<{Entity}ListDto>>
537: {
538:     // No parameters - returns all entities
539: }
540: ```
541: 
542: ### Query Handler (Shows Repository → DTO Mapping)
543: 
544: **File**: `{Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Handlers/Queries/Get{Entity}ListRequestHandler.cs`
545: 
546: ```csharp
547: using System.Collections.Generic;
548: using System.Threading;
549: using System.Threading.Tasks;
550: using AutoMapper;
551: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
552: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity};
553: using {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Requests.Queries;
554: using MediatR;
555: 
556: namespace {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Handlers.Queries;
557: 
558: public class Get{Entity}ListRequestHandler : IRequestHandler<Get{Entity}ListRequest, List<{Entity}ListDto>>
559: {
560:     private readonly I{Entity}Repository _{entity}Repository;
561:     private readonly IMapper _mapper;
562: 
563:     public Get{Entity}ListRequestHandler(I{Entity}Repository {entity}Repository, IMapper mapper)
564:     {
565:         _{entity}Repository = {entity}Repository;
566:         _mapper = mapper;
567:     }
568: 
569:     public async Task<List<{Entity}ListDto>> Handle(Get{Entity}ListRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
570:     {
571:         // CRITICAL: Repository returns ENTITIES (not DTOs)
572:         var {entities} = await _{entity}Repository.Get{Entities}WithDetails();
573: 
574:         // CRITICAL: AutoMapper maps entities to DTOs
575:         return _mapper.Map<List<{Entity}ListDto>>({entities});
576:     }
577: }
578: ```
579: 
580: ### Repository Interface
581: 
582: **File**: `{Project}.Application/Contracts/Persistence/I{Entity}Repository.cs`
583: 
584: ```csharp
585: using System;
586: using System.Collections.Generic;
587: using System.Threading.Tasks;
588: using {Project}.Domain;
589: 
590: namespace {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
591: 
592: public interface I{Entity}Repository : IGenericRepository<{Entity}, {IdType}>
593: {
594:     Task<{Entity}?> Get{Entity}WithDetails({IdType} id);
595:     Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}WithDetails();
596:     Task<List<{Entity}>> GetMy{Entities}WithDetails(string userId);
597: }
598: ```
599: 
600: ### Repository Implementation (Complex Include Chains)
601: 
602: **File**: `{Project}.Persistence/Repositories/{Entity}Repository.cs`
603: 
604: ```csharp
605: using System;
606: using System.Collections.Generic;
607: using System.Linq;
608: using System.Threading.Tasks;
609: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
610: using {Project}.Domain;
611: using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
612: 
613: namespace {Project}.Persistence.Repositories;
614: 
615: public class {Entity}Repository : GenericRepository<{Entity}, {IdType}>, I{Entity}Repository
616: {
617:     private readonly {DbContext} _dbContext;
618: 
619:     public {Entity}Repository({DbContext} dbContext) : base(dbContext)
620:     {
621:         _dbContext = dbContext;
622:     }
623: 
624:     public async Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}WithDetails()
625:     {
626:         return await _dbContext.{Entities}
627:             .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
628:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity1})
629:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity2})
630:             .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
631:             .Include(e => e.Status)
632:             .Include(e => e.Visibility)
633:             .Include(e => e.FeaturedImage)
634:             .ToListAsync();
635:     }
636: 
637:     public async Task<{Entity}?> Get{Entity}WithDetails({IdType} id)
638:     {
639:         return await _dbContext.{Entities}
640:             .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
641:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity1})
642:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity2})
643:             .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
644:             .Include(e => e.Status)
645:             .Include(e => e.Visibility)
646:             .Include(e => e.FeaturedImage)
647:             .FirstOrDefaultAsync(e => e.Id == id);
648:     }
649: 
650:     public async Task<List<{Entity}>> GetMy{Entities}WithDetails(string userId)
651:     {
652:         {IdType} userIdParsed;
653:         var isValid = {IdType}.TryParse(userId, out userIdParsed);
654: 
655:         var query = _dbContext.{Entities}
656:             .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
657:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity1})
658:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity2})
659:             .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
660:             .Include(e => e.Status)
661:             .Include(e => e.Visibility)
662:             .Include(e => e.FeaturedImage)
663:             .AsQueryable();
664: 
665:         if (isValid)
666:         {
667:             query = query.Where(e =>
668:                 _dbContext.Users.Any(u => u.Id == userIdParsed && u.{ParentEntity}Id == e.{ParentEntity}Id));
669:         }
670: 
671:         return await query.ToListAsync();
672:     }
673: }
674: ```
675: 
676: ### AutoMapper Profile
677: 
678: **File**: `{Project}.Application/Profiles/MappingProfile.cs` (excerpt)
679: 
680: ```csharp
681: using AutoMapper;
682: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity};
683: using {Project}.Domain;
684: 
685: namespace {Project}.Application.Profiles;
686: 
687: public class MappingProfile : Profile
688: {
689:     public MappingProfile()
690:     {
691:         // {Entity} mappings
692:         CreateMap<{Entity}, {Entity}Dto>()
693:             .ReverseMap();
694: 
695:         CreateMap<{Entity}, {Entity}ListDto>();
696: 
697:         CreateMap<Create{Entity}Dto, {Entity}>();
698: 
699:         CreateMap<Update{Entity}Dto, {Entity}>();
700: 
701:         // ... other entity mappings
702:     }
703: }
704: ```
705: 
706: ---
707: 
708: ## Key Patterns Demonstrated
709: 
710: ### 1. **Manual Validator Instantiation** ⚠️
711: ```csharp
712: // CRITICAL: Validators are instantiated with dependencies in handlers
713: var validator = new Create{Entity}DtoValidator(
714:     _{relatedEntity1}Repository,
715:     _{relatedEntity2}Repository,
716:     _{lookupEntity}Repository,
717:     _{parentEntity}Repository,
718:     _storageObjectRepository);
719: ```
720: 
721: ### 2. **Repository Returns Entities, Not DTOs** ⚠️
722: ```csharp
723: // Repository returns entities
724: var {entities} = await _{entity}Repository.Get{Entities}WithDetails();
725: 
726: // Handler maps to DTOs using AutoMapper
727: return _mapper.Map<List<{Entity}ListDto>>({entities});
728: ```
729: 
730: ### 3. **BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}> for Commands** ⚠️
731: ```csharp
732: public class Create{Entity}Command : IRequest<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>
733: {
734:     public Create{Entity}Dto {Entity}Dto { get; set; }
735: }
736: ```
737: 
738: ### 4. **Authorization Pattern** ⚠️
739: ```csharp
740: [HttpGet]
741: [AllowAnonymous]  // Public read access
742: 
743: [HttpPost]
744: [Authorize]  // Authenticated write access
745: ```
746: 
747: ### 5. **UserId Extraction with Fallback** ⚠️
748: ```csharp
749: var userId = _httpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.User?.FindFirst("sub")?.Value
750:     ?? _httpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.User?.FindFirst("http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/nameidentifier")?.Value
751:     ?? _httpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.User?.FindFirst("sid")?.Value;
752: ```
753: 
754: ### 6. **Complex EF Core Include Chains** ⚠️
755: ```csharp
756: return await _dbContext.{Entities}
757:     .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
758:     .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
759:     .Include(e => e.FeaturedImage)
760:     .ToListAsync();
761: ```
762: 
763: ---
764: 
765: This complete example shows **every layer** of the CQRS cycle, from domain entity to API controller, with all critical patterns highlighted.
````

## File: .claude/skills/cqrs-mediatr-guidelines/SKILL.md
````markdown
  1: ---
  2: name: cqrs-mediatr-guidelines
  3: description: CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation) patterns with MediatR for .NET Clean Architecture projects. Covers commands, queries, handlers, validation, and pipeline behaviors.
  4: type: domain
  5: enforcement: suggest
  6: priority: high
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: # CQRS + MediatR Guidelines
 10: 
 11: > **Project-Agnostic CQRS Guidelines**
 12: >
 13: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
 14: 
 15: ## Purpose
 16: 
 17: Provides best practices for implementing **CQRS** (Command Query Responsibility Segregation) using **MediatR** in .NET Clean Architecture projects. Ensures consistent, testable, and maintainable application logic.
 18: 
 19: ## When This Skill Activates
 20: 
 21: **Triggered by**:
 22: - Keywords: "command", "query", "handler", "mediatr", "cqrs", "validation", "validator"
 23: - Intent patterns: "create feature", "add endpoint", "implement use case"
 24: - File patterns: `**/*Command.cs`, `**/*Query.cs`, `**/*Handler.cs`, `**/*Validator.cs`
 25: - Content patterns: `IRequest`, `IRequestHandler`, `AbstractValidator`
 26: 
 27: ## CQRS Pattern Overview
 28: 
 29: ```mermaid
 30: graph TD
 31:     subgraph Presentation Layer
 32:         Controller -- "Sends IRequest" --> MediatR[MediatR]
 33:     end
 34: 
 35:     subgraph Application Layer
 36:         MediatR --> Handler[Handler]
 37:         Handler --> Validator[Validator]
 38:         Handler --> Mapper[AutoMapper]
 39:         Handler --> Repository[Repository]
 40:         Repository --> Domain[Domain Entities]
 41:     end
 42: 
 43:     subgraph Infrastructure Layer
 44:         Repository --> DB[Database]
 45:     end
 46: 
 47:     style MediatR fill:#fbe5c5,stroke:#333
 48:     style Handler fill:#e5c5fb,stroke:#333
 49:     style Validator fill:#e5fbe5,stroke:#333
 50:     style Mapper fill:#fbe5e5,stroke:#333
 51:     style Repository fill:#c5fbe5,stroke:#333
 52:     style Domain fill:#c5fbc5,stroke:#333
 53:     style DB fill:#c5c5fb,stroke:#333
 54: ```
 55: 
 56: ## Key Principles
 57: 
 58: 1.  **Separation**: Commands (write operations) and Queries (read operations) are distinct.
 59: 2.  **Single Responsibility**: Each handler processes one specific request (command or query).
 60: 3.  **Class Requests**: Commands and Queries are defined as classes.
 61: 4.  **Validation**: FluentValidation is used at the Application boundary for input validation.
 62: 5.  **Thin Controllers**: Controllers should be minimal, primarily responsible for receiving HTTP requests, sending them to MediatR, and returning HTTP responses.
 63: 6.  **CancellationToken**: Always pass `CancellationToken` to all asynchronous methods to enable cancellation.
 64: 7.  **Repository Returns Entities**: Repositories must return domain entities, and handlers are responsible for mapping these entities to DTOs.
 65: 8.  **Validators Use Manual Instantiation**: Validators are instantiated manually within handlers, **NOT** injected via Dependency Injection.
 66: 
 67: ## Resources
 68: 
 69: *For more detailed examples, refer to the `resources/` folder within this skill.*
 70: 
 71: | Resource | Description |
 72: |----------|-------------|
 73: | [command-patterns.md](resources/command-patterns.md) | Command structure, naming, handlers |
 74: | [query-patterns.md](resources/query-patterns.md) | Query structure, pagination, projections |
 75: | [handler-patterns.md](resources/handler-patterns.md) | Handler implementation, DI, error handling |
 76: | [validation-integration.md](resources/validation-integration.md) | FluentValidation patterns and manual integration |
 77: | [complete-examples.md](resources/complete-examples.md) | End-to-end feature examples for CQRS |
 78: | [api-endpoint-design.md](resources/api-endpoint-design.md) | API controller endpoint design conventions for CQRS request/response flows |
 79: 
 80: ## Quick Reference
 81: 
 82: ### 1. Command (Write Operation)
 83: 
 84: Commands represent actions that modify the application's state.
 85: 
 86: ```csharp
 87: // File: {Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Requests/Commands/Create{Entity}Command.cs
 88: namespace {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Requests.Commands;
 89: 
 90: using MediatR;
 91: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity};
 92: using {Project}.Application.Responses;
 93: 
 94: public class Create{Entity}Command : IRequest<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>
 95: {
 96:     public Create{Entity}Dto {Entity}Dto { get; set; } = null!; // Command wraps a DTO
 97: }
 98: ```
 99: *For more details, see [command-patterns.md](resources/command-patterns.md).*
100: 
101: ### 2. Query (Read Operation)
102: 
103: Queries represent requests for data and should not alter the application's state.
104: 
105: ```csharp
106: // File: {Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Requests/Queries/Get{Entity}ListRequest.cs
107: namespace {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Requests.Queries;
108: 
109: using System.Collections.Generic;
110: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity};
111: using MediatR;
112: 
113: public class Get{Entity}ListRequest : IRequest<List<{Entity}ListDto>>
114: {
115:     // Can include filter properties if needed
116: }
117: ```
118: *For more details, see [query-patterns.md](resources/query-patterns.md).*
119: 
120: ### 3. Handler (Processing Logic)
121: 
122: Handlers contain the business logic to execute a command or query.
123: 
124: ```csharp
125: // File: {Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Handlers/Commands/Create{Entity}CommandHandler.cs
126: namespace {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Handlers.Commands;
127: 
128: using System.Linq;
129: using System.Threading;
130: using System.Threading.Tasks;
131: using AutoMapper;
132: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
133: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity}.Validators;
134: using {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Requests.Commands;
135: using {Project}.Application.Responses;
136: using MediatR;
137: 
138: public class Create{Entity}CommandHandler : IRequestHandler<Create{Entity}Command, BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>
139: {
140:     private readonly I{Entity}Repository _{entity}Repository;
141:     private readonly IMapper _mapper;
142:     // ... other dependencies needed for validation or business logic
143: 
144:     public Create{Entity}CommandHandler(I{Entity}Repository {entity}Repository, IMapper mapper /* ... */)
145:     {
146:         _{entity}Repository = {entity}Repository;
147:         _mapper = mapper;
148:     }
149: 
150:     public async Task<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>> Handle(Create{Entity}Command request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
151:     {
152:         var response = new BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>();
153: 
154:         // ✅ CRITICAL: Manual validator instantiation with dependencies
155:         var validator = new Create{Entity}DtoValidator(/* repositories */);
156:         var validationResult = await validator.ValidateAsync(request.{Entity}Dto, cancellationToken);
157: 
158:         if (!validationResult.IsValid)
159:         {
160:             response.Success = false;
161:             response.Message = "{Entity} creation failed.";
162:             response.Errors = validationResult.Errors.Select(e => e.ErrorMessage).ToList();
163:             return response;
164:         }
165: 
166:         var {entity} = _mapper.Map<{Entity}>(request.{Entity}Dto);
167:         {entity}.ViewCount = 0; // Set properties not coming from DTO
168:         {entity} = await _{entity}Repository.Create({entity});
169: 
170:         response.Success = true;
171:         response.Id = {entity}.Id;
172:         response.Message = "{Entity} created successfully.";
173:         return response;
174:     }
175: }
176: ```
177: *For more details, see [handler-patterns.md](resources/handler-patterns.md).*
178: 
179: ### 4. Validation (Manual Integration)
180: 
181: FluentValidation is used for input validation, with validators instantiated manually within handlers.
182: 
183: ```csharp
184: // File: {Project}.Application/DTOs/{Entity}/Validators/Create{Entity}DtoValidator.cs
185: namespace {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity}.Validators;
186: 
187: using FluentValidation;
188: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
189: 
190: public class Create{Entity}DtoValidator : AbstractValidator<Create{Entity}Dto>
191: {
192:     public Create{Entity}DtoValidator(I{RelatedEntity1}Repository {relatedEntity1}Repository /* ... */)
193:     {
194:         // ... inject repositories needed for FK validation
195: 
196:         RuleFor(x => x.Title)
197:             .NotEmpty().WithMessage("Title is required")
198:             .MaximumLength(200);
199: 
200:         RuleFor(x => x.{RelatedEntity1}Id)
201:             .NotEmpty().WithMessage("{RelatedEntity1} is required")
202:             .MustAsync(async (id, cancellation) => await {relatedEntity1}Repository.Exists(id))
203:             .WithMessage("{RelatedEntity1} not found");
204:     }
205: }
206: ```
207: *For more details, see [validation-integration.md](resources/validation-integration.md).*
208: 
209: ## Do's
210: 
211: -   ✅ **DO** separate Commands (write) and Queries (read).
212: -   ✅ **DO** use classes for Commands/Queries (not records).
213: -   ✅ **DO** pass `CancellationToken` to all asynchronous methods.
214: -   ✅ **DO** use repositories that return domain entities (not DTOs).
215: -   ✅ **DO** perform DTO mapping in handlers using AutoMapper.
216: -   ✅ **DO** instantiate validators manually within handlers.
217: -   ✅ **DO** keep controllers thin, delegating to MediatR.
218: -   ✅ **DO** return `201 Created` for successful creates and `204 NoContent` for successful deletes in controllers.
219: -   ✅ **DO** use explicit route constraints for IDs (for example `{id:guid}`) to reduce ambiguous route binding.
220: -   ✅ **DO** use `BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>` for command responses (except `bool` for Delete).
221: 
222: ## Don'ts
223: 
224: -   ❌ **DON'T** return entities directly from query handlers.
225: -   ❌ **DON'T** put business logic in controllers.
226: -   ❌ **DON'T** use `IRequest` without a response type.
227: -   ❌ **DON'T** use `.Result` or `.Wait()` in asynchronous code.
228: -   ❌ **DON'T** mutate state in query handlers.
229: -   ❌ **DON'T** throw exceptions for business validation failures; return them in the `BaseCommandResponse`.
230: -   ❌ **DON'T** inject validators via Dependency Injection.
231: -   ❌ **DON'T** mix transport concerns (HTTP status mapping) into handlers.
232: -   ❌ **DON'T** expose domain entities from controller actions.
233: 
234: ---
235: 
236: **Related Documentation**:
237: - [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](../../../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) - Overall system architecture.
238: - [`clean-architecture-rules`](../clean-architecture-rules/SKILL.md) - Dependency enforcement.
````

## File: .claude/skills/error-tracking/SKILL.md
````markdown
  1: ---
  2: name: error-tracking
  3: description: Implement error tracking and observability using Prometheus (metrics) and Loki (logs). Covers centralized exception handling, structured logging, and performance monitoring for .NET services.
  4: type: guardrail
  5: enforcement: suggest
  6: priority: high
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: # Error Tracking & Observability Guidelines
 10: 
 11: > **Project-Agnostic Observability Patterns for .NET**
 12: >
 13: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
 14: 
 15: ## Purpose
 16: 
 17: Guidelines for implementing **robust error tracking** and **performance monitoring** across .NET services using:
 18: - **Prometheus** - Metrics collection and monitoring
 19: - **Loki** - Centralized log aggregation
 20: - **Structured Logging** - Consistent log formatting via Serilog
 21: - **OpenTelemetry** - Distributed tracing and telemetry
 22: 
 23: ## When This Skill Activates
 24: 
 25: **Triggered by**:
 26: - Keywords: "error handling", "logging", "prometheus", "loki", "observability", "metrics", "tracing"
 27: - Intent patterns: "add error logging", "monitor performance", "track exceptions", "implement telemetry"
 28: - File patterns: `**/Program.cs`, `**/*Controller.cs`, `**/*Handler.cs`, `**/*Repository.cs`, `**/*.razor`
 29: 
 30: ## CRITICAL RULE: Do Not Swallow Exceptions!
 31: 
 32: All errors **MUST** be handled gracefully with structured logging and centralized exception handling.
 33: 
 34: ## Resources
 35: 
 36: *Detailed patterns are available in `resources/` and [docs/CONFIGURATION.md](../../../docs/CONFIGURATION.md).*
 37: 
 38: | Resource | Description |
 39: |----------|-------------|
 40: | [api-exception-handling.md](resources/api-exception-handling.md) | Centralized API exception handling with RFC 7807 ProblemDetails |
 41: | [api-error-responses.md](resources/api-error-responses.md) | Consistent API error contract and status mapping guidance |
 42: | [mediatr-logging-behavior.md](resources/mediatr-logging-behavior.md) | MediatR pipeline behavior for request/response logging |
 43: | [prometheus-metrics.md](resources/prometheus-metrics.md) | Exposing custom metrics via `/metrics` endpoint |
 44: | [loki-logging.md](resources/loki-logging.md) | Structured logging to Loki via Serilog |
 45: | [blazor-error-boundary.md](resources/blazor-error-boundary.md) | Graceful UI error handling with ErrorBoundary component |
 46: | [opentelemetry-tracing.md](resources/opentelemetry-tracing.md) | Distributed tracing with ActivitySource |
 47: 
 48: ## Quick Reference
 49: 
 50: ### 1. Centralized API Exception Handling
 51: - Use `app.UseExceptionHandler()` to catch unhandled API exceptions
 52: - Transform exceptions into RFC 7807 `ProblemDetails` format
 53: - Log exceptions with structured logging before returning response
 54: - Return appropriate HTTP status codes (400, 404, 500)
 55: 
 56: *Details: [api-exception-handling.md](resources/api-exception-handling.md)*
 57: 
 58: ### 1.1 API Error Response Contract
 59: - Keep one predictable JSON contract for validation and runtime failures
 60: - Include correlation/trace identifiers in error extensions
 61: - Use typed status mapping for authz/authn and domain failures
 62: 
 63: *Details: [api-error-responses.md](resources/api-error-responses.md)*
 64: 
 65: ### 2. MediatR Pipeline Logging
 66: - Implement `IPipelineBehavior<TRequest, TResponse>` for centralized logging
 67: - Log request start/completion with structured data (request name, duration)
 68: - Capture and log exceptions from handlers
 69: - Attach correlation IDs and tenant context to logs
 70: 
 71: *Details: [mediatr-logging-behavior.md](resources/mediatr-logging-behavior.md)*
 72: 
 73: ### 3. Prometheus Metrics
 74: - Expose `/metrics` endpoint using `app.MapPrometheusScrapingEndpoint()`
 75: - Configure OpenTelemetry with `AddPrometheusExporter()`
 76: - Track: HTTP request durations, database query times, command/query execution
 77: - Use histograms for latency metrics (P50, P95, P99)
 78: 
 79: *Configuration: [docs/CONFIGURATION.md](../../../docs/CONFIGURATION.md) Prometheus section*
 80: 
 81: ### 4. Loki Centralized Logging
 82: - Configure Serilog with `GrafanaLoki` sink
 83: - Add structured labels: `app`, `environment`, `tenant`
 84: - Include correlation IDs for request tracing
 85: - Ship logs asynchronously to avoid performance impact
 86: 
 87: *Configuration: [docs/CONFIGURATION.md](../../../docs/CONFIGURATION.md) Loki section*
 88: 
 89: ### 5. Blazor Error Boundary
 90: - Wrap components in `<ErrorBoundary>` to catch UI exceptions
 91: - Provide `<ErrorContent>` fallback UI for graceful degradation
 92: - Log caught exceptions with component context
 93: - Display user-friendly error messages
 94: 
 95: *Implementation: [blazor-error-boundary.md](resources/blazor-error-boundary.md)*
 96: 
 97: ### 6. OpenTelemetry Tracing
 98: - Use `ActivitySource` for distributed tracing
 99: - Create spans for database operations, external API calls, long-running processes
100: - Attach custom tags (entity ID, operation type)
101: - Integrate with Prometheus for performance monitoring
102: 
103: *Details: [opentelemetry-tracing.md](resources/opentelemetry-tracing.md)*
104: 
105: ## Key Principles
106: 
107: *   **No Uncaught Exceptions**: All exceptions must be caught and logged with structured context
108: *   **Structured Logging**: Use Serilog with `ILogger<T>` for consistent log formatting
109: *   **Contextual Information**: Include user ID, tenant ID, correlation IDs, and request data in logs
110: *   **Metrics Over Logs**: Use Prometheus metrics for performance tracking; logs for debugging
111: *   **RFC 7807 Compliance**: API error responses must use `ProblemDetails` format
112: *   **Label-Based Filtering**: Add labels to Loki logs for efficient querying (app, env, tenant)
113: *   **Performance Monitoring**: Track P50/P95/P99 latencies for critical operations
114: 
115: ---
116: 
117: **Related Skills**:
118: - [`clean-architecture-rules`](../clean-architecture-rules/SKILL.md) - For proper error handling layer placement.
119: - [`cqrs-mediatr-guidelines`](../cqrs-mediatr-guidelines/SKILL.md) - For error handling patterns within MediatR handlers.
120: - [`dotnet-efcore-guidelines`](../dotnet-efcore-guidelines/SKILL.md) - For database error handling and performance considerations.
121: - [`blazor-ui-conventions`](../blazor-ui-conventions/SKILL.md) - For UI error handling patterns.
````

## File: docs/DOMAIN.md
````markdown
  1: # Domain Model
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Specific Domain Reference**
  4: >
  5: > This document describes the domain model for the ISLAMU Event platform (Explore project).
  6: > While entity names are project-specific, the architectural patterns and structure can be adapted to any .NET Clean Architecture project.
  7: >
  8: > For generic architectural guidance, see [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) and [GOVERNANCE.md](GOVERNANCE.md).
  9: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
 10: 
 11: ## Placeholder Substitutions
 12: 
 13: | Placeholder | Replace With | Example (ISLAMU Event) |
 14: |-------------|--------------|------------------------|
 15: | `{Project}` | Your solution name | `Explore` |
 16: | `{Project}.Domain` | Domain layer project | `Explore.Domain` |
 17: 
 18: ---
 19: 
 20: ## Overview
 21: 
 22: The domain layer (`{Project}.Domain/`) is the heart of the application, containing all business entities, enums, and value objects. It defines **what** the system is about, independent of any technical implementation details.
 23: 
 24: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
 25: The `Explore.Domain/` layer contains entities specific to Islamic event discovery and federation, including:
 26: - Multi-tenant organization and event management
 27: - ATProto federation actors and records
 28: - Islamic-specific metadata (Madhab, prayer times)
 29: - Event registration and approval workflows
 30: 
 31: For details on how these domain models are implemented using Entity Framework Core, including conventions for IDs, numeric types, default values, and link tables, refer to the **`dotnet-efcore-guidelines` skill**.
 32: 
 33: ## Domain Model Visualized
 34: 
 35: ```mermaid
 36: erDiagram
 37:     %% Core Identity & Multi-Tenancy
 38:     Tenant ||--o{ TenantUser : has
 39:     User ||--o{ TenantUser : belongs_to
 40:     User ||--o{ Actor : owns
 41:     Organization ||--|| Actor : is_an
 42:     Tenant ||--o{ Event : scopes
 43: 
 44:     %% Event Aggregate
 45:     Event ||--o{ EventSession : contains
 46:     Event }|--|| Actor : created_by
 47:     Event ||--o| EventIslamicAspect : extends
 48:     Event ||--o| EventTechAspect : extends
 49:     
 50:     %% Lookups & Metadata
 51:     Event }o--o{ Category : classified_by
 52:     Event }o--o{ Tag : tagged_with
 53:     Event }|--|| EventType : has_type
 54:     Event }|--|| EventStatus : has_status
 55: 
 56:     %% Session Details
 57:     EventSession }|--|| Location : occurs_at
 58:     EventSession }o--o{ Actor : speaks_at
 59:     EventSession ||--o{ EventRegistration : accepts
 60: 
 61:     %% Definitions
 62:     Event {
 63:         Guid Id
 64:         string Title
 65:         Guid TenantId
 66:         Guid ActorId
 67:     }
 68:     EventSession {
 69:         Guid Id
 70:         DateTime StartTime
 71:         DateTime EndTime
 72:     }
 73:     Actor {
 74:         Guid Id
 75:         string DID
 76:         string ActorType
 77:     }
 78: ```
 79: 
 80: ## Core Entities
 81: 
 82: ### Tenant Management
 83: 
 84: #### Tenant
 85: *   **Purpose**: Represents a distinct client or organization within the multi-tenant system, ensuring data isolation.
 86: *   **Key Relationships**: Core of multi-tenancy; all tenant-scoped entities link to `Tenant`.
 87: *   **Associated Concepts**: `TenantUser`, `TenantSettings`.
 88: 
 89: #### TenantUser
 90: *   **Purpose**: Links a User to a specific Tenant, often with associated roles.
 91: *   **Key Relationships**: Many-to-many relationship between `User` and `Tenant`.
 92: 
 93: #### TenantSettings
 94: *   **Purpose**: Stores tenant-specific configuration and policies.
 95: *   **Key Relationships**: One-to-one relationship with `Tenant`.
 96: 
 97: #### Role (Unified)
 98: *   **Purpose**: Defines roles across all scopes — Platform (SuperAdmin, Admin, Moderator, Editor, Member), Tenant (TenantOwner, TenantAdmin, TenantModerator, TenantMember), and Organization (OrgCreator, OrgCoOwner, OrgAdmin, OrgModerator, OrgMember, OrgViewer).
 99: *   **Key Relationships**: Referenced by `TenantUser.RoleId`, `OrganizationMember.RoleId`. Scoped via `RoleScopeEnum`. Linked to `Permission` via `RolePermission` join table.
100: 
101: ### User Management
102: 
103: #### User
104: *   **Purpose**: Represents a user account in the system.
105: *   **Key Relationships**: Can link to an `Actor` for federation, and associated with `UserAuthenticationToken`, `UserExternalLogin`, `OrganizationMember`, `EventRegistration`.
106: 
107: #### UserAuthenticationToken
108: *   **Purpose**: Stores authentication-related tokens for users (e.g., from Keycloak, ATProto OAuth).
109: *   **Key Relationships**: Links to `User` and `Tenant`.
110: 
111: #### UserExternalLogin
112: *   **Purpose**: Records external login details, such as DID (Decentralized Identifier) or private keys for ATProto OAuth.
113: *   **Key Relationships**: Links to `User` and `Tenant`.
114: 
115: ### Federation (ATProto)
116: 
117: #### Actor
118: *   **Purpose**: Represents a federated identity (DID) in the ATProto network. This is the core identity for all content creators and organizations.
119: *   **Key Relationships**: Linked to `ActorType`, `DidCustodyType`, `User`.
120: 
121: #### ActorType
122: *   **Purpose**: Categorizes actors (e.g., User, Organization, Service, Bot).
123: 
124: #### DidCustodyType
125: *   **Purpose**: Defines who controls an Actor's DID keys (e.g., Self-Custodied, Custodial).
126: 
127: #### ActorKeyStore
128: *   **Purpose**: Securely stores cryptographic keys associated with an `Actor`.
129: *   **Key Relationships**: Links to `Actor` and `Tenant`.
130: 
131: #### IndexedDid
132: *   **Purpose**: Tracks DIDs discovered and indexed from the ATProto network.
133: 
134: #### SyncState
135: *   **Purpose**: Manages the synchronization progress with federation firehoses/relays.
136: 
137: #### AtprotoRecord
138: *   **Purpose**: Links local entities (like `Event` or `EventRegistration`) to their corresponding records on the ATProto network.
139: *   **Key Relationships**: Linked to entities that are federated.
140: 
141: ### Organization Management
142: 
143: #### Organization
144: *   **Purpose**: Represents an entity that creates and manages events (e.g., a mosque, a university, a community group).
145: *   **Key Relationships**: Linked to `ApprovalStatus`, `Actor`, and has associated `OrganizationMember`s and `OrganizationReview`s.
146: *   **Associated Concepts**: Supports a two-tier verification system (User-Submitted vs. Verified).
147: 
148: #### OrganizationMember
149: *   **Purpose**: Represents a `User`'s membership within an `Organization`, defining their role and position.
150: *   **Key Relationships**: Links `Organization` with `User`.
151: 
152: #### OrganizationPosition
153: *   **Purpose**: Defines specific positions within an `Organization` (e.g., President, Secretary).
154: 
155: #### ApprovalStatus
156: *   **Purpose**: Defines the various stages of approval for entities like `Organization`s or `EventRegistration`s (e.g., Pending, Approved, Verified).
157: 
158: #### OrganizationReview
159: *   **Purpose**: Captures community reviews and ratings for `Organization`s.
160: 
161: ### Event Management
162: 
163: #### Event
164: *   **Purpose**: The central entity representing a scheduled occurrence (e.g., a conference, webinar, workshop).
165: *   **Key Relationships**: Links to `EventType`, `AudienceGender`, `AudienceAge`, `Actor`, `EventStatus`, `VisibilityType`, `EventFormat`, `Madhab`, `StorageObject` (for featured image), and potentially `AtprotoRecord`.
166: *   **Associated Concepts**: Can have multiple `EventSession`s.
167: 
168: #### EventSession
169: *   **Purpose**: Represents a specific time slot or segment of an `Event`. Events can have one or many sessions.
170: *   **Key Relationships**: Links to `Event`, `Location`, `RegistrationMode`.
171: *   **Associated Concepts**: Can contain `EventSessionAgendaItem`s, `EventSessionSpeaker`s, `EventSessionLanguage`s, and `EventRegistration`s.
172: 
173: #### EventSessionAgendaItem
174: *   **Purpose**: Details specific activities or segments within an `EventSession` (e.g., a speaker's talk, a break).
175: *   **Key Relationships**: Links to `EventSession`, `Location`.
176: 
177: #### EventSessionSpeaker
178: *   **Purpose**: Links an `Actor` (speaker) to an `EventSession`.
179: *   **Key Relationships**: Many-to-many relationship between `Actor` and `EventSession`.
180: 
181: #### EventSessionLanguage
182: *   **Purpose**: Indicates the languages supported or used in an `EventSession`.
183: *   **Key Relationships**: Many-to-many relationship between `EventSession` and `Language`.
184: 
185: #### EventRegistration
186: *   **Purpose**: Records a `User`'s registration for an `EventSession`.
187: *   **Key Relationships**: Links to `User`, `EventSession`, `ApprovalStatus`, and potentially `AtprotoRecord`.
188: 
189: #### RegistrationMode
190: *   **Purpose**: Defines the method of registration for an `EventSession` (e.g., Open, Approval Required, Invitation Only).
191: 
192: ### Module-Specific Entity Extensions
193: 
194: The system supports **modular event types** through aspect entities that extend the base `Event` entity with domain-specific fields. This pattern allows different event types to have specialized properties while maintaining a consistent core event model.
195: 
196: #### EventIslamicAspect
197: *   **Purpose**: Extends `Event` with Islamic-specific fields for religious events (e.g., prayer times, gender segregation, madhab compatibility).
198: *   **Key Fields**:
199:     -   `PrayerTimesAvailable` (bool) - Indicates if prayer facilities are provided
200:     -   `GenderSegregated` (bool) - Indicates gender-separated seating/areas
201:     -   `MadhabFocus` - Primary Islamic jurisprudence school
202:     -   `IslamicCalendarDate` - Date in Hijri calendar
203: *   **Relationship**: One-to-one with `Event` (optional)
204: *   **Module Governance**: Enabled per-tenant via `TenantCapability` table
205: 
206: #### EventTechAspect
207: *   **Purpose**: Extends `Event` with technology-specific fields for tech conferences, workshops, and hackathons.
208: *   **Key Fields**:
209:     -   `TechStack` (string) - Primary technologies covered (e.g., ".NET, React, Azure")
210:     -   `SkillLevel` (enum) - Target audience skill level (Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced, Expert)
211:     -   `Platform` (string) - Development platform focus (Web, Mobile, Desktop, Cloud)
212:     -   `HandsOnLab` (bool) - Indicates if hands-on coding exercises included
213: *   **Relationship**: One-to-one with `Event` (optional)
214: *   **Module Governance**: Enabled per-tenant via `TenantCapability` table
215: 
216: #### Module Resolution Strategy Pattern
217: 
218: The system uses a **strategy pattern** to resolve module-specific aspects:
219: 
220: ```csharp
221: // Simplified conceptual example
222: public interface IModuleService<TEntity, TAspect>
223: {
224:     Task<TAspect?> GetAspectAsync(Guid entityId);
225:     Task SaveAspectAsync(TAspect aspect);
226: }
227: 
228: // Usage in handlers
229: var islamicAspect = await _islamicModuleService.GetAspectAsync(eventId);
230: if (islamicAspect != null)
231: {
232:     // Event has Islamic-specific data
233:     dto.PrayerTimes = islamicAspect.PrayerTimesAvailable;
234: }
235: ```
236: 
237: **Key Design Principles**:
238: -   **Opt-in Architecture**: Events don't require aspect entities. Only create aspect when needed.
239: -   **Tenant Control**: Modules are enabled/disabled per tenant via `TenantCapability` table
240: -   **Type Safety**: Each aspect has its own strongly-typed entity and DTO
241: -   **Separation of Concerns**: Core event logic remains clean; domain-specific logic in aspects
242: 
243: **See Also**: [CODEBASE_INSIGHTS.md](CODEBASE_INSIGHTS.md) Section 7 for module governance implementation details.
244: 
245: ### Event Session Hierarchy
246: 
247: The event session system supports complex, multi-session events with detailed scheduling:
248: 
249: ```
250: Event (e.g., "Annual Tech Conference 2026")
251: ├── EventSession 1 (e.g., "Day 1 - Morning Keynote")
252: │   ├── EventSessionAgendaItem 1 (e.g., "09:00 - Opening Remarks")
253: │   ├── EventSessionAgendaItem 2 (e.g., "09:30 - Keynote Speaker")
254: │   ├── EventSessionSpeaker 1 → Actor (Speaker)
255: │   ├── EventSessionSpeaker 2 → Actor (Speaker)
256: │   ├── EventSessionLanguage 1 → Language (English)
257: │   └── EventRegistration records (Users registered for this session)
258: ├── EventSession 2 (e.g., "Day 1 - Afternoon Workshop Track A")
259: │   ├── EventSessionAgendaItem 1 (e.g., "14:00 - Workshop: Clean Architecture")
260: │   ├── EventSessionSpeaker 1 → Actor (Instructor)
261: │   ├── EventSessionLanguage 1 → Language (English)
262: │   └── EventRegistration records
263: └── EventSession 3 (e.g., "Day 2 - Closing Session")
264:     └── ...
265: ```
266: 
267: **Relationships**:
268: -   **Event → EventSession**: One-to-many (an event can have multiple sessions)
269: -   **EventSession → EventSessionAgendaItem**: One-to-many (a session has a timeline of agenda items)
270: -   **EventSession → EventSessionSpeaker**: Many-to-many (a session can have multiple speakers; a speaker can appear in multiple sessions)
271: -   **EventSession → EventSessionLanguage**: Many-to-many (a session can support multiple languages)
272: -   **EventSession → EventRegistration**: One-to-many (users register for specific sessions)
273: -   **EventSession → Location**: Many-to-one (each session has a location; location can host multiple sessions)
274: -   **EventSession → RegistrationMode**: Many-to-one (defines registration requirements)
275: 
276: **Design Notes**:
277: -   Sessions provide flexibility for multi-day, multi-track events
278: -   Each session can have its own location (useful for hybrid events)
279: -   Registration is at the session level (users can attend specific sessions)
280: -   Agenda items provide detailed scheduling within a session
281: -   Speaker and language associations are session-specific (different speakers/languages per session)
282: 
283: ### Event Metadata
284: 
285: #### EventType
286: *   **Purpose**: Classifies `Event`s (e.g., Conference, Webinar, Workshop).
287: 
288: #### EventStatus
289: *   **Purpose**: Tracks the lifecycle status of an `Event` (e.g., Draft, Published, Cancelled).
290: 
291: #### VisibilityType
292: *   **Purpose**: Controls the visibility of an `Event` (e.g., Public, Private, Unlisted).
293: 
294: #### EventFormat
295: *   **Purpose**: Describes the delivery format of an `Event` (e.g., In-person, Online, Hybrid).
296: 
297: #### Madhab
298: *   **Purpose**: Classifies `Event`s or `Actor`s by Islamic jurisprudence school (e.g., Hanafi, Maliki).
299: 
300: #### AudienceAge
301: *   **Purpose**: Categorizes the target age demographic for an `Event` (e.g., Children, Youth, Adults).
302: 
303: #### AudienceGender
304: *   **Purpose**: Categorizes the target gender for an `Event` (e.g., Men-only, Women-only, Mixed).
305: 
306: #### Category
307: *   **Purpose**: Provides hierarchical categorization for `Event`s (e.g., Aqidah, Fiqh, Tafsir).
308: *   **Key Relationships**: Can be self-referencing for parent-child relationships.
309: 
310: #### EventCategories
311: *   **Purpose**: Links `Event`s to `Category`s.
312: 
313: #### Tag
314: *   **Purpose**: Provides flexible tagging for `Event`s, `Actor`s, or other entities.
315: 
316: #### TagType
317: *   **Purpose**: Classifies the type of a `Tag` (e.g., Person, Channel, Oeuvre).
318: 
319: #### TagTypeTags
320: *   **Purpose**: Links `Tag`s to `TagType`s.
321: 
322: #### EventTags
323: *   **Purpose**: Links `Event`s to `Tag`s.
324: 
325: ### Location Management
326: 
327: #### Location
328: *   **Purpose**: Defines physical or virtual locations where `EventSession`s can occur.
329: *   **Associated Concepts**: Can include geographic coordinates for spatial queries.
330: 
331: ### Storage Management
332: 
333: #### StorageObject
334: *   **Purpose**: Represents files stored in the system (e.g., images, documents).
335: *   **Key Relationships**: Links to `FileType` and `Actor` (owner).
336: 
337: #### FileType
338: *   **Purpose**: Classifies `StorageObject`s (e.g., Image, Document, Video).
339: 
340: ### Language Support
341: 
342: #### Language
343: *   **Purpose**: Represents supported human languages for `EventSession`s.
344: 
345: ## Domain Invariants
346: 
347: Domain invariants are rules that must always be true for an entity to be in a valid state. These are typically enforced within the domain entities themselves or orchestrated by the application layer.
348: 
349: *   **Event-related**: Session end time must be after start time; an event must have at least one session to be published.
350: *   **Organization-related**: Organization email must be unique within a tenant; an owner role is required for organization creation.
351: *   **Category-related**: Categories cannot form circular references in their hierarchy.
352: *   **Actor-related**: DID must be globally unique; custodial DIDs require associated keys.
353: 
354: ## Domain Events
355: 
356: Domain events are discrete occurrences within the domain that other parts of the system might need to react to.
357: 
358: *   **Event Lifecycle Events**: `EventCreated`, `EventPublished`, `EventCancelled`, `EventStarted`, `EventEnded`.
359: *   **Organization Events**: `OrganizationCreated`, `OrganizationVerified`, `OrganizationMemberAdded`.
360: *   **Registration Events**: `UserRegisteredForSession`, `RegistrationApproved`.
````

## File: docs/GOVERNANCE.md
````markdown
  1: # Code Conventions & Governance
  2: 
  3: > **Standards and Conventions for .NET Clean Architecture Projects**
  4: >
  5: > This document defines naming conventions, organizational patterns, and architectural decisions.
  6: > For code examples and implementation patterns, see the relevant skills in `.claude/skills/`.
  7: 
  8: **Last Updated**: January 2026
  9: 
 10: ---
 11: 
 12: ## Table of Contents
 13: 
 14: 1. [Critical Rules Summary](#critical-rules-summary)
 15: 2. [Naming Conventions](#naming-conventions)
 16: 3. [File Organization](#file-organization)
 17: 4. [Layer Responsibilities](#layer-responsibilities)
 18: 5. [Design Principles](#design-principles)
 19: 6. [Pattern Selection Guide](#pattern-selection-guide)
 20: 7. [Decision Framework](#decision-framework)
 21: 
 22: ---
 23: 
 24: ## Critical Rules Summary
 25: 
 26: These rules are **non-negotiable**. Violations break architectural integrity.
 27: 
 28: | # | Rule | Rationale |
 29: |---|------|-----------|
 30: | 1 | Repositories return **entities**, never DTOs | Single responsibility; mapping belongs in handlers |
 31: | 2 | Validators use **manual instantiation**, not DI | Fine-grained control; consistent pattern |
 32: | 3 | Navigation properties are **readonly for writes** | Tenant isolation; explicit repository operations |
 33: | 4 | Use `int` for IDs (except where `Guid`/`long` needed) | Consistency; sufficient for most scenarios |
 34: | 5 | No default values in entity properties | Explicit initialization; clear value origins |
 35: | 6 | Keep all using statements | Build system dependencies; prevents issues |
 36: | 7 | Commands return `BaseCommandResponse<T>` | Consistent error handling; structured responses |
 37: | 8 | GET = AllowAnonymous, Write = Authorize | Public discovery; protected writes |
 38: | 9 | UserId extraction uses fallback pattern | Provider compatibility; claim name variations |
 39: | 10 | Use file-scoped namespaces | C# 10+ convention; cleaner code |
 40: 
 41: **For detailed examples**: See `QUICK_REFERENCE.md` and relevant skills.
 42: 
 43: ---
 44: 
 45: ## Naming Conventions
 46: 
 47: ### General Rules
 48: 
 49: | Element | Convention | Example |
 50: |---------|------------|---------|
 51: | Public members | PascalCase | `Title`, `CreatedAt` |
 52: | Private fields | _camelCase with underscore | `_eventRepository` |
 53: | Parameters | camelCase | `eventId`, `createDto` |
 54: | Constants | PascalCase | `DefaultPageSize` |
 55: | Interfaces | IPascalCase | `IEventRepository` |
 56: | Async methods | Suffix with Async | `GetEventsAsync()` |
 57: 
 58: ### Entity Naming
 59: 
 60: | Type | Pattern | Example |
 61: |------|---------|---------|
 62: | Core entity | Singular noun | `Event`, `Organization` |
 63: | Lookup/enum entity | Singular noun | `EventType`, `ApprovalStatus` |
 64: | Join table | Combined names | `EventCategories`, `EventTags` |
 65: | Aspect table | Parent + Details | `EventIslamicDetails` |
 66: 
 67: ### DTO Naming
 68: 
 69: | Type | Pattern | Purpose |
 70: |------|---------|---------|
 71: | Full details | `{Entity}Dto` | Read operations with all fields |
 72: | List view | `{Entity}ListDto` | Minimal fields for lists |
 73: | Create payload | `Create{Entity}Dto` | Write operations (no ID) |
 74: | Update payload | `Update{Entity}Dto` | Write operations (ID required) |
 75: 
 76: ### Handler Naming
 77: 
 78: | Type | Pattern | Example |
 79: |------|---------|---------|
 80: | Command | `Create{Entity}Command` | `CreateEventCommand` |
 81: | Command Handler | `Create{Entity}CommandHandler` | `CreateEventCommandHandler` |
 82: | Query | `Get{Entity}ListRequest` | `GetEventListRequest` |
 83: | Query Handler | `Get{Entity}ListRequestHandler` | `GetEventListRequestHandler` |
 84: 
 85: ### Repository Naming
 86: 
 87: | Type | Pattern | Example |
 88: |------|---------|---------|
 89: | Interface | `I{Entity}Repository` | `IEventRepository` |
 90: | Implementation | `{Entity}Repository` | `EventRepository` |
 91: | Generic base | `IGenericRepository<T, TId>` | Base interface |
 92: 
 93: ---
 94: 
 95: ## File Organization
 96: 
 97: ### Solution Structure
 98: 
 99: ```
100: {Project}.sln
101: ├── src/
102: │   ├── {Project}.Domain/           # Entities, Enums, Interfaces
103: │   ├── {Project}.Application/      # CQRS, DTOs, Validators
104: │   ├── {Project}.Persistence/      # DbContext, Repositories
105: │   ├── {Project}.Infrastructure/   # External services
106: │   ├── {Project}.API/              # REST endpoints
107: │   ├── {Project}.Blazor/           # BFF (Blazor Server)
108: │   └── {Project}.Blazor.Client/    # UI (Blazor WASM)
109: ├── tests/
110: │   ├── {Project}.Domain.UnitTests/
111: │   ├── {Project}.Application.UnitTests/
112: │   ├── {Project}.API.IntegrationTests/
113: │   └── {Project}.Persistence.IntegrationTests/
114: └── docs/
115: ```
116: 
117: ### Application Layer Organization
118: 
119: ```
120: {Project}.Application/
121: ├── Features/{Entity}/
122: │   ├── Requests/
123: │   │   ├── Commands/           # Create, Update, Delete
124: │   │   └── Queries/            # Get, List, Search
125: │   └── Handlers/
126: │       ├── Commands/           # Command handlers
127: │       └── Queries/            # Query handlers
128: ├── DTOs/{Entity}/
129: │   ├── {Entity}Dto.cs
130: │   ├── {Entity}ListDto.cs
131: │   ├── Create{Entity}Dto.cs
132: │   ├── Update{Entity}Dto.cs
133: │   └── Validators/
134: ├── Contracts/
135: │   ├── Persistence/            # Repository interfaces
136: │   ├── Infrastructure/         # Service interfaces
137: │   └── Identity/               # User context interfaces
138: ├── Responses/                  # BaseCommandResponse, etc.
139: ├── Exceptions/                 # Custom exceptions
140: └── Profiles/                   # AutoMapper profiles
141: ```
142: 
143: ### Domain Layer Organization
144: 
145: ```
146: {Project}.Domain/
147: ├── Entities/                   # Core business entities
148: ├── Enums/                      # Enum definitions
149: ├── Interfaces/                 # Domain interfaces
150: │   ├── ITenantEntity.cs
151: │   ├── IAuditableEntity.cs
152: │   └── ISoftDeletable.cs
153: └── ValueObjects/               # Value objects (if any)
154: ```
155: 
156: ### Persistence Layer Organization
157: 
158: ```
159: {Project}.Persistence/
160: ├── Configurations/
161: │   └── Entities/               # EF Core configurations
162: ├── Repositories/               # Repository implementations
163: ├── Migrations/                 # Database migrations
164: └── {DbContext}.cs              # Main DbContext
165: ```
166: 
167: ---
168: 
169: ## Layer Responsibilities
170: 
171: ### What Goes Where
172: 
173: | Concern | Layer | Location |
174: |---------|-------|----------|
175: | Entity definition | Domain | `{Project}.Domain/` |
176: | Business rules | Domain | Entity methods, value objects |
177: | Repository interface | Application | `Contracts/Persistence/` |
178: | Command/Query | Application | `Features/{Entity}/Requests/` |
179: | Handler logic | Application | `Features/{Entity}/Handlers/` |
180: | DTO definition | Application | `DTOs/{Entity}/` |
181: | Validation rules | Application | `DTOs/{Entity}/Validators/` |
182: | Repository implementation | Persistence | `Repositories/` |
183: | EF configuration | Persistence | `Configurations/Entities/` |
184: | External service impl | Infrastructure | Service classes |
185: | API endpoint | Presentation | `Controllers/` |
186: | UI component | Presentation | `Components/` |
187: 
188: ### Dependency Rules
189: 
190: | Layer | Can Reference | Cannot Reference |
191: |-------|--------------|------------------|
192: | Domain | Nothing | Application, Infrastructure, Presentation |
193: | Application | Domain | Infrastructure, Presentation |
194: | Infrastructure | Domain, Application | Presentation |
195: | Presentation | All | (Entry point) |
196: 
197: ---
198: 
199: ## Design Principles
200: 
201: ### SOLID Application
202: 
203: | Principle | How We Apply It |
204: |-----------|-----------------|
205: | **S**ingle Responsibility | One handler per command/query; one repository per entity |
206: | **O**pen/Closed | Extend via new handlers, not modifying existing |
207: | **L**iskov Substitution | All repository implementations honor interface contracts |
208: | **I**nterface Segregation | Small, focused interfaces per entity type |
209: | **D**ependency Inversion | Application defines interfaces; Infrastructure implements |
210: 
211: ### Additional Principles
212: 
213: | Principle | Application |
214: |-----------|-------------|
215: | **DRY** | Generic repository base; shared validation patterns |
216: | **KISS** | Simple handlers; one responsibility per class |
217: | **YAGNI** | Don't add abstractions until needed |
218: | **Explicit > Implicit** | Clear initialization; obvious dependencies |
219: | **Fail Fast** | Validate early; return errors immediately |
220: 
221: ---
222: 
223: ## Pattern Selection Guide
224: 
225: ### When to Use Each Pattern
226: 
227: | Scenario | Pattern | Reasoning |
228: |----------|---------|-----------|
229: | Simple CRUD | CQRS + Generic Repository | Standard approach |
230: | Complex query | Custom repository method | Optimize for specific needs |
231: | Cross-entity operation | Domain service | Coordinate multiple entities |
232: | External integration | Infrastructure service | Isolate external dependencies |
233: | Validation | FluentValidation | Consistent, testable rules |
234: | Mapping | AutoMapper | Convention-based, less boilerplate |
235: 
236: ### When NOT to Use Patterns
237: 
238: | Anti-Pattern | Why to Avoid |
239: |--------------|--------------|
240: | Repository for simple lookups | Over-engineering |
241: | Domain service for single-entity ops | Should be in handler |
242: | Generic repository for complex queries | Loses optimization |
243: | MediatR behaviors for one-off logic | Use handler directly |
244: 
245: ---
246: 
247: ## Decision Framework
248: 
249: ### Choosing ID Types
250: 
251: | Type | Use When | Examples |
252: |------|----------|----------|
253: | `Guid` | Main entities, distributed systems | Event, Organization, User |
254: | `int` | Lookup tables, enums, sequential IDs | EventType, ApprovalStatus |
255: | `long` | Large sequences, file sizes, cursors | Pagination, storage metrics |
256: 
257: ### Choosing Validation Location
258: 
259: | Location | Use When |
260: |----------|----------|
261: | DTO Validator | Input validation, format checks |
262: | Handler | Business rules requiring data access |
263: | Entity | Invariants that must always hold |
264: | Controller | Quick format/auth checks |
265: 
266: ### Choosing Query Strategy
267: 
268: | Strategy | Use When |
269: |----------|----------|
270: | Repository method | Standard queries, reusable |
271: | Handler-specific query | One-off, optimized for use case |
272: | Specification pattern | Complex, composable filters |
273: 
274: ---
275: 
276: ## Code Quality Standards
277: 
278: ### Required in Every File
279: 
280: - File-scoped namespace
281: - All necessary using statements preserved
282: - Async suffix on async methods
283: - CancellationToken passed through
284: 
285: ### Required in Every Entity
286: 
287: - Primary key property
288: - TenantId (for tenant-scoped entities)
289: - Audit fields (CreatedAt, UpdatedAt)
290: - Soft delete support (IsDeleted)
291: 
292: ### Required in Every Controller
293: 
294: - Route attribute with version
295: - OpenAPI attributes on actions
296: - Authorization attributes
297: - Proper HTTP status codes
298: 
299: ---
300: 
301: ## Related Documentation
302: 
303: - **[QUICK_REFERENCE.md](QUICK_REFERENCE.md)** - Critical rules with examples
304: - **[ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md)** - System architecture overview
305: - **[TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md)** - Placeholder definitions
306: 
307: ## Implementation Reference
308: 
309: For detailed code patterns and examples, see:
310: 
311: | Skill | Content |
312: |-------|---------|
313: | `clean-architecture-rules` | Layer boundaries, dependency rules |
314: | `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines` | Commands, queries, handlers |
315: | `dotnet-efcore-guidelines` | DbContext, repositories, queries |
316: | `blazor-ui-conventions` | Component patterns, state management |
317: | `auth-patterns` | User ID extraction, authorization |
