## File: docs/QUICK_REFERENCE.md
````markdown
  1: # Quick Reference - Critical Rules
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic .NET Clean Architecture Quick Reference**
  4: >
  5: > Fast lookup for critical rules and patterns. For full details, see [GOVERNANCE.md](GOVERNANCE.md).
  6: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  7: 
  8: **Last Updated**: January 2026
  9: 
 10: ---
 11: 
 12: ## 12 Critical Rules (Never Violate)
 13: 
 14: ### 1. Repositories Return ENTITIES, Never DTOs
 15: 
 16: ```csharp
 17: // ❌ WRONG
 18: public interface I{Entity}Repository
 19: {
 20:     Task<List<{Entity}ListDto>> Get{Entities}WithDetails();  // WRONG
 21: }
 22: 
 23: // ✅ CORRECT
 24: public interface I{Entity}Repository
 25: {
 26:     Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}WithDetails();  // CORRECT
 27: }
 28: 
 29: // Handler maps entities to DTOs
 30: public async Task<List<{Entity}ListDto>> Handle(...)
 31: {
 32:     var entities = await _{entity}Repository.Get{Entities}WithDetails();  // Entities
 33:     return _mapper.Map<List<{Entity}ListDto>>(entities);  // DTOs
 34: }
 35: ```
 36: 
 37: **Why (SOLID - Single Responsibility)**: Repositories handle data access; handlers handle mapping.
 38: 
 39: ---
 40: 
 41: ### 2. Validators Use Manual Instantiation (NOT DI)
 42: 
 43: ```csharp
 44: // ❌ WRONG - DI injection
 45: public Create{Entity}CommandHandler(
 46:     I{Entity}Repository {entity}Repository,
 47:     IValidator<Create{Entity}Dto> validator)  // WRONG
 48: {
 49:     _validator = validator;
 50: }
 51: 
 52: // ✅ CORRECT - Manual instantiation
 53: public async Task<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>> Handle(...)
 54: {
 55:     var validator = new Create{Entity}DtoValidator(
 56:         _{relatedEntity}Repository,
 57:         _{lookupEntity}Repository);
 58: 
 59:     var validationResult = await validator.ValidateAsync(request.{Entity}Dto);
 60: }
 61: ```
 62: 
 63: **Why**: Fine-grained control; avoids DI complexity; consistent pattern.
 64: 
 65: ---
 66: 
 67: ### 3. Navigation Properties on Link Tables Are Readonly
 68: 
 69: ```csharp
 70: // ❌ WRONG - Write through navigation
 71: var {parentEntity} = await _{parentEntity}Repository.GetById(id);
 72: {parentEntity}.{ChildEntities}.Add({childEntity});  // WRONG
 73: await _dbContext.SaveChangesAsync();
 74: 
 75: // ✅ CORRECT - Write through repository
 76: var {linkEntity} = new {LinkEntity}
 77: {
 78:     {ParentEntity}Id = id,
 79:     {ChildEntity}Id = childId
 80: };
 81: await _{linkEntity}Repository.Create({linkEntity});  // CORRECT
 82: ```
 83: 
 84: **Why**: Tenant isolation; explicit writes; prevents accidental cross-tenant data mixing.
 85: 
 86: ---
 87: 
 88: ### 4. Use int Instead of long (Except Size/Cursor)
 89: 
 90: ```csharp
 91: // ❌ WRONG
 92: public long Id { get; set; }
 93: 
 94: // ✅ CORRECT
 95: public int Id { get; set; }      // For lookup tables
 96: public Guid Id { get; set; }     // For main entities
 97: public long Size { get; set; }   // OK for file size
 98: public long Cursor { get; set; } // OK for pagination cursor
 99: ```
100: 
101: **Why**: Consistent conventions; `int` sufficient for most scenarios.
102: 
103: ---
104: 
105: ### 5. No Default Values in Entities
106: 
107: ```csharp
108: // ❌ WRONG
109: public class {Entity}
110: {
111:     public int ViewCount { get; set; } = 0;  // WRONG
112: }
113: 
114: // ✅ CORRECT
115: public class {Entity}
116: {
117:     public int ViewCount { get; set; }  // Set in handler or DB
118: }
119: 
120: // In handler:
121: var entity = _mapper.Map<{Entity}>(request.{Entity}Dto);
122: entity.ViewCount = 0;  // Set here
123: ```
124: 
125: **Why**: Clear initialization; avoids confusion between default and database values.
126: 
127: ---
128: 
129: ### 6. Do Not Remove Using Statements
130: 
131: ```csharp
132: // ✅ KEEP all using statements even if they appear unused
133: using System;
134: using System.Collections.Generic;
135: using System.Linq;
136: using System.Threading;
137: using System.Threading.Tasks;
138: using AutoMapper;
139: using MediatR;
140: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
141: using {Project}.Domain;
142: // ... keep all
143: ```
144: 
145: **Why**: Build system may need them; prevents hard-to-debug issues.
146: 
147: ---
148: 
149: ### 7. Commands Return BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>
150: 
151: ```csharp
152: // ❌ WRONG
153: public class Create{Entity}Command : IRequest<{IdType}>
154: 
155: // ✅ CORRECT
156: public class Create{Entity}Command : IRequest<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>
157: ```
158: 
159: **Response Structure**:
160: ```csharp
161: public class BaseCommandResponse<T>
162: {
163:     public bool Success { get; set; }
164:     public string Message { get; set; } = string.Empty;
165:     public T? Id { get; set; }
166:     public List<string> Errors { get; set; } = new();
167: }
168: ```
169: 
170: **Why**: Consistent error handling; validation messages; success/failure distinction.
171: 
172: ---
173: 
174: ### 8. GET = AllowAnonymous, Write = Authorize, Admin = Roles
175: 
176: ```csharp
177: [HttpGet]
178: [AllowAnonymous]  // ✅ Public read access
179: public async Task<ActionResult<List<{Entity}ListDto>>> GetAll() { }
180: 
181: [HttpPost]
182: [Authorize]  // ✅ Authenticated write access
183: public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>> Create(...) { }
184: 
185: [HttpPut("{id}")]
186: [Authorize]  // ✅ Authenticated write access
187: public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>> Update(...) { }
188: 
189: [HttpDelete("{id}")]
190: [Authorize]  // ✅ Authenticated write access (or use Roles="Admin" for admin-only)
191: public async Task<ActionResult> Delete({IdType} id) { }
192: 
193: // Admin-only endpoints
194: [HttpDelete("{id}")]
195: [Authorize(Roles = "Admin")]  // ✅ Admin-only access
196: public async Task<ActionResult> DeletePermanent({IdType} id) { }
197: ```
198: 
199: **Why (Security)**: Public discovery; protected writes; role-based access control for sensitive operations.
200: 
201: ---
202: 
203: ### 9. Extract UserId with Fallback Pattern
204: 
205: ```csharp
206: var userId = _httpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.User?.FindFirst("sub")?.Value
207:     ?? _httpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.User?.FindFirst(
208:         "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/nameidentifier")?.Value
209:     ?? _httpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.User?.FindFirst("sid")?.Value;
210: 
211: if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(userId))
212: {
213:     return Unauthorized(new { error = "User ID not found in token" });
214: }
215: ```
216: 
217: **Claim Priority**: `sub` → `nameidentifier` → `sid`
218: 
219: **Why**: Different auth providers use different claim names.
220: 
221: ---
222: 
223: ### 10. File-Scoped Namespaces
224: 
225: ```csharp
226: // ❌ WRONG - Nested namespace
227: namespace {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Handlers.Commands
228: {
229:     public class Create{Entity}CommandHandler { }
230: }
231: 
232: // ✅ CORRECT - File-scoped namespace
233: namespace {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Handlers.Commands;
234: 
235: public class Create{Entity}CommandHandler { }
236: ```
237: 
238: **Why (Clean Code)**: C# 10+ convention; reduces nesting; cleaner code.
239: 
240: ---
241: 
242: ### 11. Entities Include Auditing Fields (ENHANCED with Soft Delete Audit)
243: 
244: ```csharp
245: // ✅ CORRECT - Include auditing fields
246: public class {Entity}
247: {
248:     public {IdType} Id { get; set; }
249:     public string Title { get; set; } = string.Empty;
250: 
251:     // Standard auditing fields
252:     public DateTime CreatedAt { get; set; }
253:     public Guid? CreatedBy { get; set; }
254:     public DateTime? UpdatedAt { get; set; }
255:     public Guid? UpdatedBy { get; set; }
256: 
257:     // Enhanced soft delete with audit trail
258:     public bool IsDeleted { get; set; }
259:     public DateTime? DeletedAt { get; set; }
260:     public Guid? DeletedBy { get; set; }
261: 
262:     // Tenant isolation
263:     public Guid TenantId { get; set; }
264: }
265: 
266: // Set in handler
267: var entity = _mapper.Map<{Entity}>(request.{Entity}Dto);
268: entity.CreatedAt = DateTime.UtcNow;
269: entity.CreatedBy = currentUserId;  // From HttpContext
270: entity.IsDeleted = false;
271: 
272: // Soft delete is automatically handled by SaveChangesAsync override in DbContext
273: // which sets IsDeleted, DeletedAt, and DeletedBy when an entity is deleted
274: ```
275: 
276: **Why (Audit Trail)**: Track who created/modified entities and when; enables soft delete with complete audit trail (who deleted and when); maintains full data history.
277: 
278: ---
279: 
280: ### 12. Use Named Query Filters for Soft Delete
281: 
282: ```csharp
283: // ❌ WRONG - Single combined filter
284: modelBuilder.Entity<{Entity}>()
285:     .HasQueryFilter(e => !e.IsDeleted && (TenantContext == null || e.TenantId == TenantContext.TenantId));
286: 
287: // ✅ CORRECT - Named filters (EF Core 10+)
288: modelBuilder.Entity<{Entity}>()
289:     .HasQueryFilter(e => TenantContext == null || e.TenantId == TenantContext.TenantId);
290: 
291: modelBuilder.Entity<{Entity}>()
292:     .HasQueryFilter(name: "SoftDelete", predicate: e => !e.IsDeleted);
293: 
294: // Temporarily disable soft delete filter when needed
295: var allEntities = await _dbContext.{Entities}
296:     .IgnoreQueryFilter("SoftDelete")
297:     .ToListAsync();
298: ```
299: 
300: **Why (EF Core 10)**: Named filters allow selective disabling; tenant filter always active; soft delete filter can be bypassed for admin operations.
301: 
302: ---
303: 
304: ## CQRS Pattern Quick Reference
305: 
306: ### Command Pattern (Write)
307: 
308: ```csharp
309: // 1. Command Request
310: public class Create{Entity}Command : IRequest<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>
311: {
312:     public Create{Entity}Dto {Entity}Dto { get; set; } = null!;
313: }
314: 
315: // 2. Command Handler
316: public class Create{Entity}CommandHandler : IRequestHandler<Create{Entity}Command, BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>
317: {
318:     private readonly I{Entity}Repository _{entity}Repository;
319:     private readonly I{RelatedEntity}Repository _{relatedEntity}Repository;
320:     private readonly IMapper _mapper;
321: 
322:     public async Task<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>> Handle(...)
323:     {
324:         var response = new BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>();
325: 
326:         // Instantiate validator manually
327:         var validator = new Create{Entity}DtoValidator(_{relatedEntity}Repository);
328:         var validationResult = await validator.ValidateAsync(request.{Entity}Dto);
329: 
330:         if (!validationResult.IsValid)
331:         {
332:             response.Success = false;
333:             response.Errors = validationResult.Errors.Select(e => e.ErrorMessage).ToList();
334:             return response;
335:         }
336: 
337:         var entity = _mapper.Map<{Entity}>(request.{Entity}Dto);
338:         entity = await _{entity}Repository.Create(entity);
339: 
340:         response.Success = true;
341:         response.Id = entity.Id;
342:         return response;
343:     }
344: }
345: ```
346: 
347: ### Query Pattern (Read)
348: 
349: ```csharp
350: // 1. Query Request
351: public class Get{Entity}ListRequest : IRequest<List<{Entity}ListDto>> { }
352: 
353: // 2. Query Handler
354: public class Get{Entity}ListRequestHandler : IRequestHandler<Get{Entity}ListRequest, List<{Entity}ListDto>>
355: {
356:     private readonly I{Entity}Repository _{entity}Repository;
357:     private readonly IMapper _mapper;
358: 
359:     public async Task<List<{Entity}ListDto>> Handle(...)
360:     {
361:         var entities = await _{entity}Repository.Get{Entities}WithDetails();  // Entities
362:         return _mapper.Map<List<{Entity}ListDto>>(entities);  // DTOs
363:     }
364: }
365: ```
366: 
367: ---
368: 
369: ## Folder Structure
370: 
371: ```
372: {Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/
373: ├── Requests/
374: │   ├── Commands/
375: │   │   ├── Create{Entity}Command.cs
376: │   │   ├── Update{Entity}Command.cs
377: │   │   └── Delete{Entity}Command.cs
378: │   └── Queries/
379: │       ├── Get{Entity}ListRequest.cs
380: │       ├── Get{Entity}DetailsRequest.cs
381: │       └── Get{Entities}By{RelatedEntity}Request.cs
382: └── Handlers/
383:     ├── Commands/
384:     │   ├── Create{Entity}CommandHandler.cs
385:     │   ├── Update{Entity}CommandHandler.cs
386:     │   └── Delete{Entity}CommandHandler.cs
387:     └── Queries/
388:         ├── Get{Entity}ListRequestHandler.cs
389:         ├── Get{Entity}DetailsRequestHandler.cs
390:         └── Get{Entities}By{RelatedEntity}RequestHandler.cs
391: 
392: {Project}.Application/DTOs/{Entity}/
393: ├── {Entity}Dto.cs              // Full details
394: ├── {Entity}ListDto.cs          // List view
395: ├── Create{Entity}Dto.cs        // Create payload
396: ├── Update{Entity}Dto.cs        // Update payload
397: └── Validators/
398:     ├── Create{Entity}DtoValidator.cs
399:     └── Update{Entity}DtoValidator.cs
400: ```
401: 
402: ---
403: 
404: ## Controller Pattern
405: 
406: ```csharp
407: [Route("api/[controller]")]
408: [ApiController]
409: public class {Entity}Controller : ControllerBase
410: {
411:     private readonly IMediator _mediator;
412: 
413:     public {Entity}Controller(IMediator mediator) => _mediator = mediator;
414: 
415:     [HttpGet]
416:     [AllowAnonymous]
417:     [EndpointSummary("Get all {Entities}")]
418:     [ProducesResponseType(typeof(List<{Entity}ListDto>), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]
419:     public async Task<ActionResult<List<{Entity}ListDto>>> GetAll()
420:         => Ok(await _mediator.Send(new Get{Entity}ListRequest()));
421: 
422:     [HttpGet("{id}")]
423:     [AllowAnonymous]
424:     [EndpointSummary("Get {Entity} by ID")]
425:     [ProducesResponseType(typeof({Entity}Dto), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]
426:     [ProducesResponseType(StatusCodes.Status404NotFound)]
427:     public async Task<ActionResult<{Entity}Dto>> GetById({IdType} id)
428:         => Ok(await _mediator.Send(new Get{Entity}DetailsRequest { Id = id }));
429: 
430:     [HttpPost]
431:     [Authorize]
432:     [EndpointSummary("Create {Entity}")]
433:     [Consumes("application/json")]
434:     [ProducesResponseType(typeof(BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]
435:     [ProducesResponseType(typeof(BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>), StatusCodes.Status400BadRequest)]
436:     public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>> Create([FromBody] Create{Entity}Dto dto)
437:     {
438:         var response = await _mediator.Send(new Create{Entity}Command { {Entity}Dto = dto });
439:         return response.Success ? Ok(response) : BadRequest(response);
440:     }
441: 
442:     [HttpPut("{id}")]
443:     [Authorize]
444:     [EndpointSummary("Update {Entity}")]
445:     [Consumes("application/json")]
446:     public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>> Update({IdType} id, [FromBody] Update{Entity}Dto dto)
447:     {
448:         if (id != dto.Id) return BadRequest(new { error = "ID mismatch" });
449:         var response = await _mediator.Send(new Update{Entity}Command { {Entity}Dto = dto });
450:         return response.Success ? Ok(response) : BadRequest(response);
451:     }
452: 
453:     [HttpDelete("{id}")]
454:     [Authorize]
455:     [EndpointSummary("Delete {Entity}")]
456:     [ProducesResponseType(StatusCodes.Status204NoContent)]
457:     [ProducesResponseType(StatusCodes.Status404NotFound)]
458:     public async Task<ActionResult> Delete({IdType} id)
459:     {
460:         var result = await _mediator.Send(new Delete{Entity}Command { Id = id });
461:         return result ? NoContent() : NotFound();
462:     }
463: }
464: ```
465: 
466: ---
467: 
468: ## API Endpoint Metadata (Required)
469: 
470: All controller actions must include OpenAPI attributes:
471: 
472: ```csharp
473: [HttpGet("{id}")]
474: [EndpointSummary("Get {Entity} Details")]
475: [EndpointDescription("Returns full {entity} details including related entities.")]
476: [AllowAnonymous]
477: [ProducesResponseType(typeof({Entity}Dto), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]
478: [ProducesResponseType(StatusCodes.Status404NotFound)]
479: public async Task<ActionResult<{Entity}Dto>> GetById({IdType} id)
480: ```
481: 
482: **Required Attributes**:
483: - `[EndpointSummary]` - Short title
484: - `[EndpointDescription]` - Detailed description
485: - `[ProducesResponseType]` - Success + failure codes
486: - `[Consumes]` - For POST/PUT with JSON body
487: 
488: ---
489: 
490: ## Common Mistakes & Fixes
491: 
492: | Mistake | Fix |
493: |---------|-----|
494: | Repository returns DTOs | Return entities; map in handler |
495: | Validator injected via DI | Instantiate manually in handler |
496: | `{parentEntity}.{ChildEntities}.Add()` | Use `_{linkEntity}Repository.Create()` |
497: | `public long Id` | Use `public int Id` or `public Guid Id` |
498: | `= 0` default in entity | Remove; set in handler |
499: | Removed using statements | Keep all using statements |
500: | `IRequest<{IdType}>` | Use `IRequest<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>` |
501: | Nested namespaces | Use file-scoped namespaces |
502: | Missing userId fallback | Use sub → nameidentifier → sid |
503: | Missing [AllowAnonymous] on GET | Add for public read access |
504: | Missing auditing fields | Add CreatedAt, CreatedBy, UpdatedAt, UpdatedBy, DeletedAt, DeletedBy |
505: | Missing soft delete | Add IsDeleted, DeletedAt, DeletedBy; use named query filter |
506: | **Delete command returns `bool`** | **Use `IRequest<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>` for ALL commands (including deletes)** |
507: | Admin endpoint without Roles | Add `[Authorize(Roles = "Admin")]` |
508: | Combined query filters | Use named filters: `HasQueryFilter(name: "SoftDelete", ...)` |
509: 
510: ---
511: 
512: ## Design Principles Summary
513: 
514: | Principle | Application |
515: |-----------|-------------|
516: | **S**ingle Responsibility | Each handler handles ONE command/query |
517: | **O**pen/Closed | Use interfaces for extension |
518: | **L**iskov Substitution | Repositories implement interfaces correctly |
519: | **I**nterface Segregation | Small, focused interfaces |
520: | **D**ependency Inversion | Depend on abstractions |
521: | **DRY** | Use `GenericRepository<T, TId>` |
522: | **KISS** | Simple handlers, one responsibility |
523: | **YAGNI** | Don't add unused abstractions |
524: 
525: ---
526: 
527: ## Related Documentation
528: 
529: - **[TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md)** - Placeholder substitution guide
530: - **[GOVERNANCE.md](GOVERNANCE.md)** - Complete coding conventions
531: - **[ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md)** - System architecture overview
532: 
533: ## Skills Reference
534: 
535: - **`clean-architecture-rules`** - Dependency rules and layer boundaries
536: - **`cqrs-mediatr-guidelines`** - CQRS patterns with MediatR
537: - **`dotnet-efcore-guidelines`** - EF Core and repository patterns
538: 
539: ---
540: 
541: **Remember**: These rules ensure architectural consistency across all projects. Follow them without exception.
````

## File: docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md
````markdown
  1: # Troubleshooting
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic .NET Backend Troubleshooting Guide**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: **Last Updated**: January 2026
  8: 
  9: ---
 10: 
 11: ## Placeholder Substitutions
 12: 
 13: | Placeholder | Replace With | Example (ISLAMU Event) |
 14: |-------------|--------------|------------------------|
 15: | `{Project}` | Your solution name | `Explore` |
 16: | `{Project}.API` | API project | `Explore.API` |
 17: | `{Project}.Application` | Application project | `Explore.Application` |
 18: | `{Project}.Domain` | Domain project | `Explore.Domain` |
 19: | `{Project}.Persistence` | Persistence project | `Explore.Persistence` |
 20: | `{Project}.Infrastructure` | Infrastructure project | `Explore.Infrastructure` |
 21: 
 22: ---
 23: 
 24: This guide focuses on common issues when working on the **backend** projects:
 25: 
 26: - `{Project}.API`
 27: - `{Project}.Application`
 28: - `{Project}.Domain`
 29: - `{Project}.Persistence`
 30: - `{Project}.Infrastructure`
 31: - Migration/worker services (if applicable)
 32: 
 33: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
 34: 
 35: ```
 36: - Explore.API
 37: - Explore.Application
 38: - Explore.Domain
 39: - Explore.Persistence
 40: - Explore.Infrastructure
 41: - Event.MigrationService
 42: ```
 43: 
 44: ## Build & Restore
 45: 
 46: ### Effective Commands for Error Visibility
 47: 
 48: Basic `dotnet build` and `dotnet test` hide important error details. Use these commands instead:
 49: 
 50: #### Building
 51: 
 52: ```bash
 53: # Clean summary with error/warning counts
 54: dotnet build --configuration Release --verbosity quiet
 55: 
 56: # Full error details when you need them
 57: dotnet build --configuration Release --verbosity normal
 58: ```
 59: 
 60: #### Running Tests
 61: 
 62: **Always run test projects individually** — solution-level `dotnet test` fails if any project has MSBuild issues (e.g., placeholder projects without a test framework).
 63: 
 64: ```bash
 65: # Clean pass/fail summary per project
 66: dotnet test --project Event.Application.UnitTests/Event.Application.UnitTests.csproj --configuration Release --verbosity quiet
 67: 
 68: # Inline error details
 69: dotnet test --project Event.API.IntegrationTests/Event.API.IntegrationTests.csproj --configuration Release --verbosity normal
 70: ```
 71: 
 72: **Important:** Always use `--project` flag. Positional project path (e.g., `dotnet test path.csproj`) does not work reliably — use `dotnet test --project path.csproj`.
 73: 
 74: #### Debugging Test Failures with TRX Reports
 75: 
 76: When you need detailed failure analysis (failed test names, error messages, stack traces), generate a TRX report:
 77: 
 78: ```bash
 79: # Generate TRX report
 80: dotnet test --project Event.API.IntegrationTests/Event.API.IntegrationTests.csproj --configuration Release -- --report-trx --report-trx-filename results.trx
 81: ```
 82: 
 83: **TRX file location:** `<ProjectDir>/bin/Release/net10.0/TestResults/results.trx`
 84: 
 85: **Analyzing the TRX file** (use Grep tool, not bash grep):
 86: 
 87: ```
 88: # Find all failed tests
 89: Grep pattern: outcome="Failed"
 90: 
 91: # Get full class.method names for failed tests
 92: Grep pattern: className=
 93: # Correlate testId from failed entries to className entries
 94: 
 95: # Read error messages and stack traces
 96: Grep pattern: <Message>
 97: Grep pattern: <StackTrace>
 98: ```
 99: 
100: **TRX workflow summary:**
101: 1. Generate TRX with `-- --report-trx --report-trx-filename results.trx`
102: 2. Grep for `outcome="Failed"` to find failed test entries and their `testId`
103: 3. Grep for `className=` with the `testId` to get the full `Namespace.Class.Method`
104: 4. Read the `<Message>` and `<StackTrace>` elements for error details
105: 
106: #### Test Projects (Run Individually)
107: 
108: ```bash
109: dotnet test --project Event.Application.UnitTests/Event.Application.UnitTests.csproj --configuration Release
110: dotnet test --project Event.Domain.UnitTests/Event.Domain.UnitTests.csproj --configuration Release
111: dotnet test --project Event.Architecture.Tests/Event.Architecture.Tests.csproj --configuration Release
112: dotnet test --project Explore.Secrets.UnitTests/Explore.Secrets.UnitTests.csproj --configuration Release
113: dotnet test --project Event.Persistence.IntegrationTests/Event.Persistence.IntegrationTests.csproj --configuration Release
114: dotnet test --project Event.API.IntegrationTests/Event.API.IntegrationTests.csproj --configuration Release
115: dotnet test --project Explore.Blazor.Client.Tests/Explore.Blazor.Client.Tests.csproj --configuration Release
116: ```
117: 
118: #### Known Pitfalls
119: 
120: | Pitfall | Solution |
121: |---------|----------|
122: | `dotnet test` at solution level fails | Run each test project individually |
123: | Positional project path doesn't work | Use `--project` flag: `dotnet test --project path.csproj` |
124: | `findstr /i` fails on French-locale Windows | Use exact case patterns instead of `/i` flag |
125: | `--treenode-filter` for TUnit filtering | Does not work reliably — use TRX reports instead |
126: | Running test DLL directly | Causes MSBuild errors — always test via `.csproj` |
127: | Basic `dotnet test` hides failures | Use `--verbosity normal` or TRX reports |
128: | Basic `dotnet build` hides errors | Use `--verbosity quiet` for summary or `normal` for details |
129: 
130: ### Common issues
131: 
132: #### Target framework / SDK mismatch
133: 
134: All backend projects target `net10.0`. If your SDK is older, install the .NET 10 SDK.
135: 
136: #### "The type or namespace name 'X' could not be found"
137: 
138: Typical causes:
139: 
140: - Missing `using` (do not remove existing usings)
141: - Missing project reference (check `.csproj`)
142: - Wrong layer dependency (see `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` and `docs/QUICK_REFERENCE.md`)
143: 
144: ## OpenAPI / Swagger / Scalar
145: 
146: ### Swagger UI loads but endpoints are missing metadata
147: 
148: Controllers should annotate actions with:
149: 
150: - `[EndpointSummary]`
151: - `[EndpointDescription]`
152: - `[ProducesResponseType]`
153: 
154: See `docs/API.md`.
155: 
156: ### swagger.json file is stale
157: 
158: In Development, `{Project}.API` runs `OpenApiExportService` which exports a `swagger.json` file at startup.
159: 
160: If it doesn't update:
161: 
162: - Ensure `{Project}.API` starts successfully in Development.
163: - Check startup logs for the hosted service.
164: - Confirm the file is not locked by another process.
165: 
166: **Example (ISLAMU Event)**: `Explore.API` exports `swagger.json` to `Explore.API/swagger.json`
167: 
168: ## Authentication / Authorization
169: 
170: ### 401 Unauthorized on write endpoints
171: 
172: - Ensure you are sending `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
173: - Confirm Keycloak settings in configuration match your environment.
174: 
175: ### UserId missing in token
176: 
177: Controllers that require a user id MUST use the fallback claim extraction:
178: 
179: `sub` → `http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/nameidentifier` → `sid`
180: 
181: If all are missing, return `401`.
182: 
183: ## Database / EF Core / Migrations
184: 
185: ### Apply migrations (Development)
186: 
187: `{Project}.API` exposes a Development-only endpoint:
188: 
189: ```http
190: POST /admin/migrate
191: ```
192: 
193: It is protected with `.RequireAuthorization()`.
194: 
195: **Example (ISLAMU Event)**: `Explore.API` provides `POST /admin/migrate`
196: 
197: ### Migration worker (if applicable)
198: 
199: If your project has a dedicated migration service, it's responsible for background migration/maintenance tasks.
200: 
201: **Example (ISLAMU Event)**: `Event.MigrationService` handles background migrations (see `Event.MigrationService/Program.cs`)
202: 
203: ### Duplicate key violations
204: 
205: `GenericRepository.Create` catches PostgreSQL unique constraint violations (`SqlState == "23505"`) and rethrows with more context.
206: 
207: If you see duplicate key errors:
208: 
209: - Check unique constraints in EF configurations/migrations.
210: - Verify seed data and id generation.
211: 
212: 
213: ### Development URLs (Default)
214: 
215: | Service | URL |
216: |---------|-----|
217: | Aspire Dashboard | `https://localhost:17225` |
218: | API | `https://localhost:7001` |
219: | Blazor | `https://localhost:7002` |
220: | Scalar API Docs | `https://localhost:7001/scalar/v1` |
221: | Swagger UI | `https://localhost:7001/swagger` |
222: 
223: ---
224: 
225: ## 6. HATEOAS & Links
226: 
227: ### Links missing from API response
228: If the `_links` section is missing or incomplete:
229: 1.  Check if `Prefer: return=minimal` header was sent.
230: 2.  **Cerbos Permissions**: Links are filtered by `HateoasAuthorizationEvaluator`. If the user lacks permission for an action (e.g., `update`), the link is hidden. Check Cerbos logs or policies.
231: 
232: ## 7. Caching Issues
233: 
234: ### Data not updating (Stale Cache)
235: 1.  **Output Cache**: Wait 5 minutes or restart the API. Public GET endpoints are output cached.
236: 2.  **Hybrid Cache**: If entity updates aren't reflected in authenticated views, check if the Command Handler calls `_hybridCache.RemoveAsync()`.
237: 
238: ## 8. Blazor UI Issues
239: 
240: ### Infinite Loading / White Screen
241: If the app hangs on startup:
242: 1.  **SignalR Connection**: Check browser console for WebSocket errors. `InteractiveServer` mode requires a stable SignalR connection.
243: 2.  **WASM Download**: Check network tab. If WASM download fails (e.g., firewall), the app should fallback to Server, but hybrid transition can stall if configured incorrectly.
244: 
245: ### OIDC "Invalid parameter: redirect_uri"
246: Common in Docker/Coolify deployments behind Nginx.
247: *   **Cause**: The app thinks it's running on `http://` but Keycloak expects `https://`.
248: *   **Fix**: Ensure `ForwardedHeaders` middleware is active (it is in `Program.cs`) and your proxy sends `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`.
````

137:                         </div>
138:                     </NoRecordsContent>
139:                 </MudTable>
140:             </MudPaper>
141:         </div>
142:     }
143: </div>
````

## File: Explore.Blazor.Client/Pages/Admin/EventStatuses.razor
````razor
 1: @page "/admin/event-statuses"
 2: @using Explore.Blazor.Client.Clients
 3: @using Explore.Blazor.Client.Services.Contracts
 4: @using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization
 5: @attribute [Authorize]
 6: @rendermode @(new InteractiveAutoRenderMode(prerender: false))
 7: 
 8: <MudText Typo="Typo.h4" GutterBottom="true">Event Statuses</MudText>
 9: 
10: <MudTable Items="@_eventStatuses"
11:           Dense="true" Hover="true" Striped="true" @ref="_table">
12:     <ToolBarContent>
13:         <MudText Typo="Typo.h6">Manage Event Statuses</MudText>
14:         <MudSpacer />
15:         <MudButton Variant="Variant.Filled" Color="Color.Primary" @onclick="(() => OpenDialog(null))">Create Event Status</MudButton>
16:     </ToolBarContent>
17:     <HeaderContent>
18:         <MudTh>Name</MudTh>
19:         <MudTh>Description</MudTh>
20:         <MudTh>Actions</MudTh>
21:     </HeaderContent>
22:     <RowTemplate>
23:         <MudTd DataLabel="Name">@context.FullName</MudTd>
24:         <MudTd DataLabel="Description">@context.Description</MudTd>
25:         <MudTd DataLabel="Actions">
26:             <MudIconButton Icon="@Icons.Material.Filled.Edit" OnClick="@(() => OpenDialog(context.Id ?? 0))" />
27:             <MudIconButton Icon="@Icons.Material.Filled.Delete" OnClick="@(() => DeleteEventStatus(context.Id ?? 0))" />
28:         </MudTd>
29:     </RowTemplate>
30: 
31: </MudTable>
````

335:     private bool ValidateForm()
336:     {
337:         errorMessage = string.Empty;
338: 
339: 
340:         if (_publisherMode == "organization")
341:         {
342:             if (!_selectedOrganizationId.HasValue)
343:             {
344:                 errorMessage = "Please select an organization.";
345:                 return false;
346:             }
347:             if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(_organizationRoleError))
348:             {
349:                 errorMessage = _organizationRoleError;
350:                 return false;
351:             }
352:         }
353: 
354:         if (_publisherMode == "group")
355:         {
356:             if (!_selectedGroupId.HasValue)
357:             {
358:                 errorMessage = "Please select a group.";
359:                 return false;
360:             }
361:             if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(_groupRoleError))
362:             {
363:                 errorMessage = _groupRoleError;
364:                 return false;
365:             }
366:         }
367: 
368: 
369: 
370:         if (sessions == null || !sessions.Any())
371:         {
372:             errorMessage = "You must add at least one session.";
373:             return false;
374:         }
375: 
376:         return true;
377:     }

379:     private async Task HandleSubmit()
380:     {
381:         if (!ValidateForm())
382:         {
383:             return;
384:         }
385: 
386: 
387:         if (_isUploadingImage)
388:         {
389:             errorMessage = "Please wait for the image upload to complete.";
390:             return;
391:         }
392: 
393:         if (isProcessing) return;
394:         isProcessing = true;
395:         errorMessage = string.Empty;
396: 
397:         try
398:         {
399: 
400:             Guid? featuredImageId = _uploadedImageStorageObjectId;
401: 
402:             if (featuredImageId.HasValue)
403:             {
404:                 Logger.LogInformation("Using pre-uploaded image. StorageObjectId: {StorageObjectId}", featuredImageId);
405:             }
406: 
407: 
408:             createDto.OrganizationId = _publisherMode == "organization" ? _selectedOrganizationId : null;
409:             createDto.GroupId = _publisherMode == "group" ? _selectedGroupId : null;
410:             createDto.FeaturedImageId = featuredImageId;
411:             createDto.MadhabId = selectedMadhabId;
412:             createDto.MetadataJson = EventAppearanceMetadataHelper.Upsert(createDto.MetadataJson, _appearance);
413: 
414: 
415:             var earliestStart = sessions.Min(s => DateTimeHelper.ConvertLocalToUtc(s.StartTime));
416:             var latestEnd = sessions.Max(s => DateTimeHelper.ConvertLocalToUtc(s.EndTime));
417: 
418:             createDto.FirstSessionDate = earliestStart;
419:             createDto.LastSessionDate = latestEnd;
420: 
421: 
422:             Logger.LogInformation(
423:                 "Creating event record (publisherMode={Mode}, organizationId={OrgId}, groupId={GroupId})",
424:                 _publisherMode,
425:                 createDto.OrganizationId,
426:                 createDto.GroupId);
427:             var response = await EventService.CreateEventAsync(createDto);
428: 
429:             if (response?.Success == true && response.Id.HasValue && response.Id != Guid.Empty)
430:             {
431:                 createdEventId = response.Id.Value;
432:                 Logger.LogInformation("Event created with ID: {EventId}", createdEventId);
433: 
434: 
435:                 var tenantId = Constants.TenantConstants.DefaultTenantId;
436:                 foreach (var categoryId in selectedCategoryIds)
437:                 {
438:                     await CategoryService.AssignCategoryToEventAsync(new { EventId = createdEventId, CategoryId = categoryId, TenantId = tenantId });
439:                 }
440: 
441: 
442:                 foreach (var tagId in selectedTagIds)
443:                 {
444:                     await TagService.AssignTagToEventAsync(new { EventId = createdEventId, TagId = tagId, TenantId = tenantId });
445:                 }
446: 
447: 
448:                 var existingSessions = await EventService.GetSessionsByEventAsync(createdEventId);
449:                 var defaultSession = existingSessions?.FirstOrDefault();
450: 
451: 
452:                 if (defaultSession != null && sessions.Count > 0)
453:                 {
454:                     var firstSessionModel = sessions[0];
455:                     firstSessionModel.Id = defaultSession.Id;
456: 
457:                     var updateDto = firstSessionModel.ToUpdateDto(createdEventId);
458:                     await EventService.UpdateSessionAsync(updateDto);
459: 
460:                     if (defaultSession.Id.HasValue)
461:                     {
462:                         await SaveSessionLanguages(firstSessionModel, defaultSession.Id.Value, tenantId);
463:                     }
464:                 }
465: 
466: 
467:                 for (int i = 1; i < sessions.Count; i++)
468:                 {
469:                     var sessionModel = sessions[i];
470:                     var createSessionDto = sessionModel.ToCreateDto(createdEventId, tenantId);
471:                     var createResponse = await EventService.CreateSessionAsync(createSessionDto);
472: 
473:                     if (createResponse?.Success == true && createResponse.Id.HasValue)
474:                     {
475:                         await SaveSessionLanguages(sessionModel, createResponse.Id.Value, tenantId);
476:                     }
477:                 }
478: 
479:                 Navigation.NavigateTo($"/event/detail/{createdEventId}");
480:             }
481:             else
482:             {
483:                 var errorMsg = response?.Message ?? "Failed to create event.";
484:                 if (response?.Errors != null && response.Errors.Any())
485:                 {
486:                     errorMsg += " Errors: " + string.Join(", ", response.Errors);
487:                 }
488:                 errorMessage = errorMsg;
489:             }
490:         }
491:         catch (Exception ex)
492:         {
493:             Logger.LogError(ex, "Exception during event creation");
494:             errorMessage = $"Error creating event: {ex.Message}";
495:         }
496:         finally
497:         {
498:             isProcessing = false;
499:         }
500:     }

518:     private void AddSession()
519:     {
520:         var defaultStart = DateTime.Today.AddDays(1).AddHours(9);
521:         var defaultEnd = DateTime.Today.AddDays(1).AddHours(17);
522: 
523:         if (sessions.Any())
524:         {
525:             var last = sessions.Last();
526:             defaultStart = last.StartTime.AddDays(1);
527:             defaultEnd = last.EndTime.AddDays(1);
528:         }
529: 
530:         sessions.Add(new SessionEditorModel
531:         {
532:             StartTime = defaultStart,
533:             EndTime = defaultEnd,
534:             RegistrationModeId = sessions.FirstOrDefault()?.RegistrationModeId ?? 1
535:         });
536:     }
537: 
538:     private async void RemoveSession(int index)
539:     {
540:         if (index >= 0 && index < sessions.Count)
541:         {
542:             if (sessions.Count <= 1)
543:             {
544:                 errorMessage = "You must have at least one session.";
545:                 return;
546:             }
547: 
548:             var session = sessions[index];
549: 
550:             if (session.Id.HasValue && session.Id != Guid.Empty)
551:             {
552:                 bool? confirm = await DialogService.ShowMessageBox(
553:                     "Delete Session",
554:                     "This session already exists. Deleting it here will remove it permanently. Continue?",
555:                     yesText: "Delete", cancelText: "Cancel");
556: 
557:                 if (confirm == true)
558:                 {
559:                     try
560:                     {
561:                         await EventService.DeleteSessionAsync(session.Id.Value);
562:                         sessions.RemoveAt(index);
563:                     }
564:                     catch (Exception ex)
565:                     {
566:                         errorMessage = $"Failed to delete session: {ex.Message}";
567:                     }
568:                 }
569:             }
570:             else
571:             {
572:                 sessions.RemoveAt(index);
573:             }
574:         }
575:     }

579:         if (index >= 0 && index < sessions.Count)
580:         {
581:             sessions[index] = session;

585:     private string GetPublisherDescription()
586:     {
587:         if (_publisherMode == "personal")
588:             return "Publishing as yourself (User Reported)";
589: 
590:         if (_selectedOrganizationId.HasValue && _myOrganizations != null)
591:         {
592:             var org = _myOrganizations.FirstOrDefault(o => o.Id == _selectedOrganizationId.Value);
593:             if (org != null) return $"Publishing for {org.FullName}";
594:         }
595: 
596:         if (_publisherMode == "group" && _selectedGroupId.HasValue && _myGroups != null)
597:         {

599:             if (group != null) return $"Publishing for {group.FullName}";
600:         }
601: 
602:         return "Select who is publishing this event";
603:     }

605:     private static string GetRoleName(int roleId) => roleId switch
606:     {
607:         GroupCreatorRoleId => "Group Creator",
608:         GroupAdminRoleId => "Group Admin",
609:         32 => "Group Moderator",
610:         33 => "Group Member",
611:         _ => RoleHelper.GetRoleName(roleId)
612:     };
613: 
614:     private static bool CanPublishAsGroup(int? roleId) => roleId is GroupCreatorRoleId or GroupAdminRoleId;
615: }
````

## File: .claude/agents/auto-error-resolver.md
````markdown
  1: ---
  2: name: auto-error-resolver
  3: description: Automatically resolves C# / .NET compilation and runtime errors for {Project}.
  4: tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash
  5: ---
  6: 
  7: > **Project-Agnostic Error Resolution Agent**
  8: >
  9: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
 10: 
 11: You are a specialized agent for fixing **C# / .NET** compilation and runtime errors in the {Project} project.
 12: 
 13: ## Triage Workflow
 14: 
 15: 1. Analyze build/runtime output and capture exact error code, file, and symbol.
 16: 2. Classify error root cause (reference, type mismatch, DI registration, routing/binding, architecture boundary).
 17: 3. Apply minimal fix aligned with project architecture rules.
 18: 4. Rebuild and rerun targeted tests to verify the fix.
 19: 
 20: ## Technology Stack
 21: 
 22: - **.NET**: 10.0
 23: - **Language**: C# 13
 24: - **Build System**: MSBuild
 25: - **Solution**: {Project}.sln with multiple projects
 26: - **Logging**: Serilog (logs in `{Project}.API/logs/`)
 27: 
 28: ## Your Process
 29: 
 30: ### 1. Check for Error Information
 31: 
 32: **Build Errors**:
 33: ```powershell
 34: # Run build to get latest errors
 35: dotnet build {Project}.sln
 36: 
 37: # Check specific project
 38: dotnet build {Project}.Application/{Project}.Application.csproj
 39: ```
 40: 
 41: **Runtime Errors**:
 42: ```powershell
 43: # Check today's server logs (PowerShell)
 44: $today = Get-Date -Format "yyyyMMdd"
 45: Get-Content "{Project}.API/logs/log-$today.txt"
 46: 
 47: # Tail logs in real-time (PowerShell)
 48: Get-Content "{Project}.API/logs/log-$today.txt" -Wait -Tail 50
 49: ```
 50: 
 51: ### 2. Analyze Error Codes
 52: 
 53: #### CS0246: Type or Namespace Not Found
 54: 
 55: **Cause**: Missing `using` statement or missing project reference
 56: 
 57: ```csharp
 58: // ❌ Error: CS0246: The type or namespace name '{Entity}' could not be found
 59: var entity = new {Entity}();
 60: 
 61: // ✅ Fix 1: Add using
 62: using {Project}.Domain;
 63: 
 64: // ✅ Fix 2: Fully qualify
 65: var entity = new {Project}.Domain.{Entity}();
 66: 
 67: // ✅ Fix 3: Add project reference (if missing)
 68: // In .csproj:
 69: // <ItemGroup>
 70: //   <ProjectReference Include="..\{Project}.Domain\{Project}.Domain.csproj" />
 71: // </ItemGroup>
 72: ```
 73: 
 74: #### CS1061: Definition Does Not Exist
 75: 
 76: **Cause**: Wrong property name (C# is case-sensitive!)
 77: 
 78: ```csharp
 79: // ❌ Error: CS1061: 'User' does not contain a definition for 'email'
 80: var email = user.email;
 81: 
 82: // ✅ Fix: Use PascalCase (C# convention)
 83: var email = user.Email;
 84: ```
 85: 
 86: #### CS0029: Cannot Implicitly Convert Type
 87: 
 88: **Cause**: Type mismatch (e.g., DTO vs Entity, int vs long)
 89: 
 90: ```csharp
 91: // ❌ Error: CS0029: Cannot implicitly convert type '{Entity}Dto' to '{Entity}'
 92: {Entity} entity = {entity}Dto;
 93: 
 94: // ✅ Fix: Use AutoMapper
 95: var entity = _mapper.Map<{Entity}>({entity}Dto);
 96: 
 97: // Or manual mapping
 98: var entity = new {Entity}
 99: {
100:     Id = {entity}Dto.Id,
101:     Title = {entity}Dto.Title
102: };
103: ```
104: 
105: #### CS0103: Name Does Not Exist in Current Context
106: 
107: **Cause**: Variable not declared or typo
108: 
109: ```csharp
110: // ❌ Error: CS0103: The name '{entity}Id' does not exist in the current context
111: return await _repository.GetById({entity}Id);
112: 
113: // ✅ Fix: Declare variable
114: Guid {entity}Id = Guid.NewGuid();
115: return await _repository.GetById({entity}Id);
116: ```
117: 
118: #### CS8600: Possible Null Reference Assignment
119: 
120: **Cause**: Nullable reference type mismatch
121: 
122: ```csharp
123: // ❌ Warning CS8600: Converting null literal or possible null value to non-nullable type
124: {Entity}Dto entity = await _repository.GetById(id);
125: 
126: // ✅ Fix: Make nullable
127: {Entity}Dto? entity = await _repository.GetById(id);
128: 
129: // Or handle null
130: var entity = await _repository.GetById(id);
131: if (entity == null)
132: {
133:     return NotFound();
134: }
135: ```
136: 
137: #### CS1503: Argument Type Mismatch
138: 
139: **Cause**: Wrong parameter type
140: 
141: ```csharp
142: // ❌ Error: CS1503: Argument 1: cannot convert from 'string' to 'System.Guid'
143: var entity = await _repository.GetById("123");
144: 
145: // ✅ Fix: Parse to Guid
146: var entity = await _repository.GetById(Guid.Parse("123"));
147: ```
148: 
149: ### 3. Common Patterns and Fixes
150: 
151: #### Missing Using Statements
152: 
153: If you encounter "Type or Namespace Not Found" (CS0246) errors, ensure the necessary `using` statements are present and corresponding project references exist.
154: 
155: - **Domain Entities**: `{Project}.Domain` (e.g., `{Entity}`, `{RelatedEntity}`)
156: - **Application DTOs, Commands, Queries**: `{Project}.Application.DTOs.*`, `{Project}.Application.Features.*`
157: - **Persistence Interfaces/Implementations**: `{Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence`, `{Project}.Persistence.*`
158: - **MediatR**: `MediatR`
159: - **AutoMapper**: `AutoMapper`
160: - **FluentValidation**: `FluentValidation`
161: - **EF Core**: `Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore`
162: - **Blazor UI Components**: `MudBlazor`
163: 
164: For more details on layer responsibilities and project references, refer to the `clean-architecture-rules` skill.
165: 
166: #### AutoMapper Mapping Errors
167: 
168: If you encounter errors related to object mapping, ensure your AutoMapper profiles are correctly configured.
169: 
170: ```csharp
171: // ❌ No mapping configured
172: var dto = _mapper.Map<{Entity}ListDto>(entity);  // Runtime error!
173: 
174: // ✅ Create mapping profile in {Project}.Application/Profiles/MappingProfile.cs
175: CreateMap<{Entity}, {Entity}ListDto>.ReverseMap();
176: CreateMap<Create{Entity}Dto, {Entity}>.ReverseMap();
177: ```
178: 
179: For detailed AutoMapper usage within CQRS patterns, refer to the `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines` skill.
180: 
181: #### EF Core Migration Errors
182: 
183: If you encounter migration-related errors ("The model backing the context has changed"), refer to the `dotnet-efcore-guidelines` skill for detailed instructions on creating and applying EF Core migrations.
184: 
185: ```powershell
186: # If manual migration needed:
187: dotnet ef migrations add DescriptiveName --project {Project}.Persistence
188: 
189: # Apply migration (usually automatic)
190: dotnet ef database update --project {Project}.Persistence
191: ```
192: 
193: #### Dependency Injection Errors
194: 
195: If you encounter "Unable to resolve service" runtime errors, ensure the service and its implementation are correctly registered in the Dependency Injection container.
196: 
197: ```csharp
198: // ❌ Service not registered
199: public {Entity}Controller(I{Entity}Repository repository)  // Runtime error: Unable to resolve service
200: 
201: // ✅ Register in {Project}.Persistence/PersistenceServicesRegistration.cs
202: services.AddScoped<I{Entity}Repository, {Entity}Repository>();
203: ```
204: 
205: For guidelines on where to register services and adhere to architectural boundaries, refer to the `clean-architecture-rules` skill.
206: 
207: ### 4. Layer-Specific Errors
208: 
209: For understanding the responsibilities and allowed dependencies of each architectural layer (Domain, Application, Persistence, API), and common violations, refer to the `clean-architecture-rules` skill. This skill details what code belongs where and why.
210: 
211: ### 5. Fix Actions
212: 
213: **Priority Order**:
214: 1. Fix missing `using` statements
215: 2. Fix type errors (conversions, mappings)
216: 3. Fix dependency injection registrations
217: 4. Fix EF Core model/database mismatches
218: 5. Handle remaining warnings
219: 
220: **Commands to Run**:
221: ```powershell
222: # Clean build
223: dotnet clean
224: dotnet build
225: 
226: # Restore packages if needed
227: dotnet restore
228: 
229: # Check for outdated packages
230: dotnet list package --outdated
231: 
232: # Run tests after fixing
233: dotnet test
234: ```
235: 
236: ### 6. Verify Fixes
237: 
238: After making changes:
239: 
240: ```powershell
241: # 1. Build the solution
242: dotnet build
243: 
244: # 2. If build succeeds, run the app with Aspire
245: dotnet run --project {Project}.AppHost/{Project}.AppHost.csproj
246: 
247: # 3. Run tests
248: dotnet test
249: 
250: # 4. Check for code quality issues (optional)
251: dotnet format --verify-no-changes
252: ```
253: 
254: ## CRITICAL RULES (Must Follow)
255: 
256: Based on 45+ entity implementations. **DO NOT VIOLATE THESE RULES when fixing errors:**
257: 
258: ### 1. Repositories Return ENTITIES, Never DTOs
259: 
260: Repositories **MUST** return domain entities. DTO mapping always happens in the Application layer handlers via AutoMapper. For detailed patterns, refer to the `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines` skill and `dotnet-efcore-guidelines` skill.
261: 
262: ### 2. Validators Use Manual Instantiation (NOT DI)
263: 
264: Validators are instantiated manually within handlers, with all required dependencies passed to their constructor. They are **NOT** injected via Dependency Injection. For detailed explanation and examples, refer to the `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines` skill and the `clean-architecture-rules` skill.
265: 
266: ### 3. Navigation Properties Are Readonly
267: 
268: Navigation properties on link/mapping tables are **readonly for queries only**. Writes must go through the link table's repository directly. For details, refer to the `dotnet-efcore-guidelines` skill.
269: 
270: ### 4. Use int Instead of long (except size/cursor)
271: 
272: Unless explicitly required for large values (e.g., file sizes, pagination cursors), use `int` for lookup table IDs and `Guid` for main entities. For details, refer to the `dotnet-efcore-guidelines` skill.
273: 
274: ### 5. No Default Values in Entities
275: 
276: **DO NOT** add default values in domain entity property initializers (e.g., `public int TotalViews { get; set; } = 0;`). Set defaults in application handlers or use database-level defaults via `IEntityTypeConfiguration`. For details, refer to the `dotnet-efcore-guidelines` skill.
277: 
278: ### 6. Do Not Remove Using Statements
279: 
280: Keep ALL `using` statements even if they appear unused, except for old references that are broken (e.g., old entities or renamed namespaces). This is crucial for avoiding unnecessary re-imports by other agents and maintaining consistency.
281: 
282: ### 7. File-Scoped Namespaces
283: 
284: All new C# files should use file-scoped namespaces.
285: 
286: ```csharp
287: // ✅ CORRECT
288: namespace {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Handlers.Commands;
289: 
290: public class Create{Entity}CommandHandler { }
291: ```
292: 
293: ## Important Guidelines
294: 
295: - ✅ **DO** fix the root cause, not symptoms
296: - ✅ **DO** follow project patterns (check skills: `clean-architecture-rules`, `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines`)
297: - ✅ **DO** use PascalCase for public members, _camelCase for private fields
298: - ✅ **DO** verify fixes with `dotnet build`
299: - ✅ **DO** check validator instantiation pattern (manual, not DI)
300: - ❌ **DON'T** refactor unrelated code
301: - ❌ **DON'T** change architectural patterns
302: - ❌ **DON'T** ignore warnings (they become errors later)
303: - ❌ **DON'T** inject validators via DI (instantiate manually)
304: 
305: ## Example Workflow
306: 
307: ```powershell
308: # 1. Check build errors
309: dotnet build {Project}.sln
310: 
311: # Output:
312: # {Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Handlers/Commands/Create{Entity}CommandHandler.cs(15,25):
313: # error CS0246: The type or namespace name '{Entity}' could not be found
314: 
315: # 2. Fix: Add using statement
316: # Edit {Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Handlers/Commands/Create{Entity}CommandHandler.cs
317: # Add: using {Project}.Domain;
318: 
319: # 3. Verify
320: dotnet build {Project}.sln
321: # Output: Build succeeded. 0 Warning(s). 0 Error(s).
322: 
323: # 4. Report
324: # Fixed CS0246 in Create{Entity}CommandHandler.cs by adding 'using {Project}.Domain;'
325: ```
326: 
327: ## Related Skills
328: 
329: - [`clean-architecture-rules`](../skills/clean-architecture-rules/SKILL.md) - Dependency rules and layer responsibilities
330: - [`cqrs-mediatr-guidelines`](../skills/cqrs-mediatr-guidelines/SKILL.md) - Command/Query patterns and manual validation
331: - [`dotnet-efcore-guidelines`](../skills/dotnet-efcore-guidelines/SKILL.md) - EF Core patterns, entities, and migrations
332: 
333: ## Output Format
334: 
335: Report completion with:
336: 1. **Summary**: Number of errors fixed
337: 2. **Details**: Each error code, file, line number, and fix applied
338: 3. **Verification**: Build success confirmation
339: 4. **Remaining Issues**: Any unfixed errors or warnings
340: 
341: Focus on minimal, precise fixes that resolve errors without introducing new complexity.
````

## File: .claude/agents/plan-reviewer.md
````markdown
  1: ---
  2: name: plan-reviewer
  3: description: Reviews development plans for .NET best practices, EF Core performance, security, and Clean Architecture compliance for {Project}.
  4: tools: All tools
  5: ---
  6: 
  7: > **Project-Agnostic Plan Review Agent**
  8: >
  9: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
 10: 
 11: You are a **Senior .NET Architect** reviewing implementation plans before code is written. You prevent architecture violations, performance bottlenecks, and security issues in the {Project} platform.
 12: 
 13: ## Technology Stack
 14: 
 15: - **.NET**: 10.0
 16: - **Database**: Entity Framework Core + PostgreSQL + PostGIS
 17: - **Architecture**: Clean Architecture with CQRS
 18: - **Security**: OIDC/JWT Authentication
 19: - **Testing**: xUnit, Moq, FluentAssertions
 20: 
 21: ## CRITICAL RULES (Must Enforce)
 22: 
 23: These rules are strictly enforced. Any plan that violates these rules must be rejected or require significant rework. For detailed explanations and examples, refer to the respective skills.
 24: 
 25: 1.  **Repositories Return ENTITIES, Never DTOs**: Repositories **MUST** return domain entities. DTO mapping always happens in the Application layer handlers via AutoMapper.
 26:     -   **Reference**: `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines` (repository return types), `dotnet-efcore-guidelines` (repository pattern).
 27: 2.  **Validators Use Manual Instantiation (NOT DI)**: Validators are instantiated manually within handlers, with all required dependencies passed to their constructor. They are **NOT** injected via Dependency Injection.
 28:     -   **Reference**: `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines` (validation integration), `clean-architecture-rules` (manual validator instantiation).
 29: 3.  **Navigation Properties Are Readonly**: Navigation properties on link/mapping tables are **readonly for queries only**. Writes **MUST** go through the link table's repository directly.
 30:     -   **Reference**: `dotnet-efcore-guidelines` (key principles & conventions).
 31: 4.  **Use `int` Instead of `long`**: Unless explicitly required for large values (e.g., file sizes, pagination cursors), use `int` for lookup table IDs and `Guid` for main entities.
 32:     -   **Reference**: `dotnet-efcore-guidelines` (key principles & conventions).
 33: 5.  **No Default Values in Entities**: **DO NOT** add default values in domain entity property initializers. Defaults are set in application handlers or via `IEntityTypeConfiguration`.
 34:     -   **Reference**: `dotnet-efcore-guidelines` (key principles & conventions).
 35: 6.  **Command Response Consistency**: Create/update flows should return a consistent command response envelope. Delete flows may use `bool` when that is the established project convention.
 36:     -   **Reference**: `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines` (command patterns).
 37: 7.  **GET = AllowAnonymous, Write = Authorize**: **`GET`** endpoints should be `[AllowAnonymous]`. **`POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`** endpoints **MUST** be `[Authorize]`.
 38:     -   **Reference**: `auth-patterns` (controller endpoint authorization).
 39: 8.  **Extract User ID with Fallback**: When extracting the user ID from JWT claims, **ALWAYS** use the provided fallback pattern (`sub` → `nameidentifier` → `sid`).
 40:     -   **Reference**: `auth-patterns` (user ID extraction).
 41: 
 42: ## Critical Review Areas
 43: 
 44: ### 1. Database & EF Core Performance
 45: 
 46: -   **N+1 Query Problems**: Plans must prevent N+1 queries. Use `.Include()` or projections for efficient data retrieval.
 47:     -   **Reference**: `dotnet-efcore-guidelines` (querying patterns).
 48: -   **Transaction Requirements**: Multi-step write operations that modify multiple aggregates or require atomicity **MUST** be wrapped in a database transaction.
 49:     -   **Reference**: `dotnet-efcore-guidelines` (key principles & conventions - though specific transaction guidance might need to be added).
 50: -   **Migration Strategy**: Any plan involving schema changes must include a clear migration strategy (e.g., `dotnet ef migrations add`, handling nullability).
 51:     -   **Reference**: `dotnet-efcore-guidelines` (migrations).
 52: 
 53: ### 2. Clean Architecture & CQRS Compliance
 54: 
 55: -   **CQRS Separation**: Reads (Queries) and Writes (Commands) **MUST** be separate. Plans should not propose mixing read/write operations in a single request.
 56:     -   **Reference**: `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines` (CQRS pattern overview).
 57: -   **Layer Dependencies**: Plans must respect Clean Architecture layer dependency rules. No layer should reference a layer it shouldn't.
 58:     -   **Reference**: `clean-architecture-rules` (dependency rules).
 59: -   **Repository Usage**: Repositories should return domain entities, and DTO mapping should occur in handlers.
 60:     -   **Reference**: `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines`, `dotnet-efcore-guidelines`.
 61: -   **Validator Pattern**: Validators **MUST** be manually instantiated in handlers with dependencies.
 62:     -   **Reference**: `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines` (validation integration), `clean-architecture-rules` (manual validator instantiation).
 63: 
 64: ### 3. Security & Authorization
 65: 
 66: -   **Authorization / Ownership Enforcement**: Plans must explicitly address how authorization (role-based) and resource-level ownership checks will be enforced, typically in MediatR handlers.
 67:     -   **Reference**: `auth-patterns` (resource-level authorization), `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines` (handler patterns).
 68: -   **Endpoint Authorization Patterns**: Ensure `GET` endpoints are `[AllowAnonymous]` and write operations are `[Authorize]`.
 69:     -   **Reference**: `auth-patterns` (controller endpoint authorization).
 70: -   **User ID Extraction**: Plans should specify the use of the robust user ID extraction fallback pattern.
 71:     -   **Reference**: `auth-patterns` (user ID extraction).
 72: 
 73: ### 4. Testing Strategy
 74: 
 75: -   **Test Coverage**: Plans **MUST** include a testing strategy, detailing how unit and integration tests will verify the implemented features and architectural compliance.
 76:     -   **Reference**: `error-tracking` (for overall testing strategy and Sentry integration for test monitoring).
 77: 
 78: ## Key Principles
 79: 
 80: -   ✅ **Prevent Architectural Violations**: Leverage skills (`clean-architecture-rules`, `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines`) to identify and prevent deviations from established patterns.
 81: -   ✅ **Optimize Performance**: Identify potential N+1 queries, missing transactions, or inefficient data access. Refer to `dotnet-efcore-guidelines`.
 82: -   ✅ **Ensure Security**: Verify robust authorization, authentication patterns, and proper user ID extraction. Refer to `auth-patterns`.
 83: -   ✅ **Promote Testability**: Ensure plans support comprehensive unit and integration testing. Refer to `error-tracking`.
 84: -   ✅ **Maintain Consistency**: All plans should align with existing codebase conventions and patterns.
 85: 
 86: ## Related Skills
 87: 
 88: - [`clean-architecture-rules`](../skills/clean-architecture-rules/SKILL.md) - **CRITICAL**: Dependency rules, layer responsibilities, manual validator instantiation.
 89: - [`cqrs-mediatr-guidelines`](../skills/cqrs-mediatr-guidelines/SKILL.md) - **CRITICAL**: CQRS patterns, repository return types, DTO mapping, command/query patterns, validation.
 90: - [`dotnet-efcore-guidelines`](../skills/dotnet-efcore-guidelines/SKILL.md) - **CRITICAL**: EF Core patterns, querying, migrations, data types, transaction management.
 91: - [`auth-patterns`](../skills/auth-patterns/SKILL.md) - Authentication and authorization patterns, user ID extraction, CORS.
 92: - [`error-tracking`](../skills/error-tracking/SKILL.md) - Testing strategy, logging, and error handling.
 93: 
 94: ## Review Output Format
 95: 
 96: Provide reviews in this markdown format:
 97: 
 98: ```markdown
 99: # Implementation Plan Review: [Feature Name]
100: 
101: **Date**: YYYY-MM-DD
102: **Reviewer**: Claude Code
103: **Plan Version**: v1.0
104: 
105: ---
106: 
107: ## Executive Summary
108: 
109: [2-3 sentence overview of plan quality and major concerns]
110: 
111: ---
112: 
113: ## 🔴 Critical Risks (Must Address Before Implementation)
114: 
115: ### 1. [Risk Title]
116: 
117: **Issue**: [Description of the problem and why it's critical, referencing specific violated rules/skills.]
118: 
119: **Impact**: [What could go wrong if not addressed (e.g., security vulnerability, performance bottleneck).]
120: 
121: **Recommendation**: [Specific fix with reference to a skill section and/or example code if appropriate.]
122: 
123: ---
124: 
125: ## 🟡 Missing Considerations (Should Address)
126: 
127: ### 1. [Consideration Title]
128: 
129: **Gap**: [What the plan is missing, referencing a skill if applicable.]
130: 
131: **Recommendation**: [What should be added to the plan.]
132: 
133: ---
134: 
135: ## 🟢 Suggestions (Nice to Have)
136: 
137: ### 1. [Suggestion Title]
138: 
139: **Current Approach**: [What the plan proposes.]
140: 
141: **Alternative**: [Better approach with justification and skill reference.]
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## Architecture Compliance Checklist
146: 
147: | Rule | Status | Notes |
148: |------|--------|-------|
149: | Repositories return entities (not DTOs) | ✅ / ❌ | [Comments referencing cqrs-mediatr-guidelines, dotnet-efcore-guidelines] |
150: | Validators use manual instantiation | ✅ / ❌ | [Comments referencing cqrs-mediatr-guidelines, clean-architecture-rules] |
151: | Commands return BaseCommandResponse<Guid> | ✅ / ❌ | [Comments referencing cqrs-mediatr-guidelines] |
152: | GET = AllowAnonymous, Write = Authorize | ✅ / ❌ | [Comments referencing auth-patterns] |
153: | UserId extraction with fallback | ✅ / ❌ | [Comments referencing auth-patterns] |
154: | Use int instead of long | ✅ / ❌ | [Comments referencing dotnet-efcore-guidelines] |
155: | No default values in entities | ✅ / ❌ | [Comments referencing dotnet-efcore-guidelines] |
156: | Navigation properties are readonly | ✅ / ❌ | [Comments referencing dotnet-efcore-guidelines] |
157: | N+1 query prevention | ✅ / ❌ | [Comments referencing dotnet-efcore-guidelines] |
158: | Transactions for multi-step writes | ✅ / ❌ | [Comments referencing dotnet-efcore-guidelines] |
159: | Clear migration strategy | ✅ / ❌ | [Comments referencing dotnet-efcore-guidelines] |
160: | CQRS separation of concerns | ✅ / ❌ | [Comments referencing cqrs-mediatr-guidelines] |
161: | Layer dependency adherence | ✅ / ❌ | [Comments referencing clean-architecture-rules] |

 71: ### 2. NuGet Package Evaluation
 72: 
 73: **When researching libraries, ALWAYS check:**
 74: 
 75: | Criteria | How to Check | Red Flags |

 77: | **.NET 10 Support** | Check target frameworks in nuget.org | `net8.0` only (too old), no `net10.0` |

## File: .claude/skills/dotnet-efcore-guidelines/SKILL.md
````markdown
  1: ---
  2: name: dotnet-efcore-guidelines
  3: description: Entity Framework Core best practices for Clean Architecture projects. Covers DbContext, entity configurations, repository pattern, migrations, and PostgreSQL-specific features.
  4: type: domain
  5: enforcement: suggest
  6: priority: high
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: # .NET + Entity Framework Core Guidelines
 10: 
 11: > **Project-Agnostic EF Core Patterns**
 12: >
 13: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
 14: 
 15: ## Purpose
 16: 
 17: This skill provides comprehensive best practices for using Entity Framework Core with PostgreSQL in Clean Architecture projects. It details conventions for DbContext, entity configurations, repository patterns, migrations, and PostgreSQL-specific features.
 18: 
 19: ## When This Skill Activates
 20: 
 21: **Triggered by**:
 22: - Keywords: "ef core", "entity framework", "dbcontext", "repository", "migration", "database", "postgres", "postgresql"
 23: - File patterns: `**/Persistence/**/*.cs`, `**/Repositories/**/*.cs`, `**/*DbContext.cs`, `**/Configurations/**/*.cs`
 24: 
 25: ## EF Core Architecture
 26: 
 27: The persistence layer (`{Project}.Persistence`) is responsible for data access and storage. It implements interfaces defined in the Application layer, adhering to Clean Architecture principles.
 28: 
 29: ```mermaid
 30: graph TD
 31:     subgraph Application Layer
 32:         A[I{Entity}Repository] --> B[{Entity}]
 33:         B[{Entity}] --> C[Domain Layer]
 34:     end
 35: 
 36:     subgraph Persistence Layer
 37:         D[{DbContext}] --> B
 38:         E[{Entity}Repository] --> D
 39:         E --> A
 40:     end
 41: 
 42:     A -- Implemented by --> E
 43:     C -- Used by --> B
 44:     D -- Configures --> B
 45: ```
 46: 
 47: ## Resources
 48: 
 49: *For more detailed examples, refer to the `resources/` folder within this skill.*
 50: 
 51: | Resource | Description |
 52: |----------|-------------|
 53: | [dbcontext-patterns.md](resources/dbcontext-patterns.md) | DbContext configuration, `SaveChangesAsync` override |
 54: | [entity-configuration.md](resources/entity-configuration.md) | `IEntityTypeConfiguration`, TPT, PostgreSQL functions |
 55: | [repository-pattern.md](resources/repository-pattern.md) | `GenericRepository`, custom repositories |
 56: | [querying-patterns.md](resources/querying-patterns.md) | `Include`, `Select`, projections, performance |
 57: | [migrations.md](resources/migrations.md) | Creating and applying migrations |
 58: | [named-query-filters.md](resources/named-query-filters.md) | EF Core 10 named global query filters for soft delete and tenancy |
 59: 
 60: ## Quick Reference
 61: 
 62: ### 1. DbContext Pattern (with Pooling)
 63: 
 64: **EF Core 10+ Pattern**: Use DbContext pooling with property injection for scoped dependencies (e.g., TenantContext).
 65: 
 66: #### DbContext Configuration
 67: 
 68: ```csharp
 69: // File: {Project}.Persistence/{DbContext}.cs
 70: public class {DbContext} : DbContext
 71: {
 72:     // Property injection for pooled DbContext (set by DI after pool retrieval)
 73:     public ITenantContext? TenantContext { get; set; }
 74: 
 75:     public {DbContext}(DbContextOptions<{DbContext}> options) : base(options) { }
 76: 
 77:     protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder modelBuilder)
 78:     {
 79:         base.OnModelCreating(modelBuilder);
 80: 
 81:         // Apply all IEntityTypeConfiguration<T> from assembly
 82:         modelBuilder.ApplyConfigurationsFromAssembly(typeof({DbContext}).Assembly);
 83:     }
 84: 
 85:     // Override SaveChangesAsync for auditing/soft delete logic
 86:     public override Task<int> SaveChangesAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
 87:     {
 88:         foreach (var entry in ChangeTracker.Entries())
 89:         {
 90:             // Set CreatedAt, UpdatedAt, CreatedBy, UpdatedBy
 91:             // Use TenantContext?.UserId for audit fields
 92:         }
 93:         return base.SaveChangesAsync(cancellationToken);
 94:     }
 95: 
 96:     public DbSet<{Entity}> {Entities} { get; set; } = null!;
 97: }
 98: ```
 99: 
100: #### Registration with Pooling
101: 
102: ```csharp
103: // File: {Project}.Persistence/DependencyInjection.cs
104: builder.Services.AddDbContextPool<{DbContext}>((provider, options) =>
105: {
106:     options.UseNpgsql(connectionString)
107:         .UseSnakeCaseNamingConvention()
108:         .EnableSensitiveDataLogging(isDevelopment);
109: });
110: ```
111: 
112: **Key Benefits**: Pooling reuses DbContext instances for up to 10x performance improvement on high-throughput workloads.
113: 
114: *For more details, see [dbcontext-patterns.md](resources/dbcontext-patterns.md).*
115: 
116: ### 2. Entity Configuration
117: 
118: All entity-specific configurations are done using `IEntityTypeConfiguration<T>` in separate classes.
119: 
120: ```csharp
121: // File: {Project}.Persistence/Configurations/Entities/{Entity}Configuration.cs
122: public class {Entity}Configuration : IEntityTypeConfiguration<{Entity}>
123: {
124:     public void Configure(EntityTypeBuilder<{Entity}> builder)
125:     {
126:         // Project Standard: Table Per Type (TPT) inheritance strategy
127:         builder.UseTptMappingStrategy();
128: 
129:         // Project Standard: UUIDv7 primary keys for main entities
130:         builder.Property(e => e.Id).HasDefaultValueSql("uuidv7()");
131: 
132:         // Database-level defaults are acceptable here, not in domain entities
133:         builder.Property(e => e.ViewCount).HasDefaultValue(0);
134: 
135:         builder.Property(e => e.Title).HasMaxLength(200).IsRequired();
136:         builder.Property(e => e.Description).HasMaxLength(5000);
137: 
138:         // Example relationship configuration
139:         builder.HasOne(e => e.{ParentEntity})
140:             .WithMany()
141:             .HasForeignKey(e => e.{ParentEntity}Id)
142:             .OnDelete(DeleteBehavior.Restrict);
143: 
144:         // EF Core 10+: named query filters (can be toggled selectively)
145:         builder.HasQueryFilter(name: "SoftDelete", predicate: e => !e.IsDeleted);
146:         builder.HasQueryFilter(name: "TenantFilter", predicate: e => e.TenantId == tenantId);
147:     }
148: }
149: ```
150: 
151: *For more details, see [entity-configuration.md](resources/entity-configuration.md).*
152: 
153: ### 3. Repository Pattern
154: 
155: Repositories abstract data access. Interfaces reside in the Application layer, and implementations are in the Persistence layer.
156: 
157: **CRITICAL RULE**: Repositories **MUST** return **DOMAIN ENTITIES**, not DTOs. DTO mapping always happens in the Application layer handlers via AutoMapper.
158: 
159: ```csharp
160: // File: {Project}.Application/Contracts/Persistence/I{Entity}Repository.cs (Application Layer)
161: public interface I{Entity}Repository : IGenericRepository<{Entity}, {IdType}>
162: {
163:     Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}WithDetails(); // Returns List<{Entity}>
164:     Task<{Entity}?> Get{Entity}WithDetails({IdType} id); // Returns {Entity}?
165: }
166: 
167: // File: {Project}.Persistence/Repositories/{Entity}Repository.cs (Persistence Layer)
168: public class {Entity}Repository : GenericRepository<{Entity}, {IdType}>, I{Entity}Repository
169: {
170:     private readonly {DbContext} _dbContext;
171: 
172:     public {Entity}Repository({DbContext} dbContext) : base(dbContext) => _dbContext = dbContext;
173: 
174:     public async Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}WithDetails()
175:     {
176:         return await _dbContext.{Entities}
177:             .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
178:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity1})
179:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity2})
180:             .ToListAsync(); // Returns entities
181:     }
182: }
183: ```
184: 
185: *For more details, see [repository-pattern.md](resources/repository-pattern.md).*
186: 
187: ### 4. Querying Patterns
188: 
189: Efficient querying is crucial for performance. Avoid N+1 issues by using eager loading (`Include`) and projections (`Select`).
190: 
191: ```csharp
192: // Example: Query with eager loading and projection to DTO (in Application Layer Handler)
193: public async Task<List<{Entity}ListDto>> Handle(Get{Entity}ListRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
194: {
195:     var {entities} = await _{entity}Repository.Get{Entities}WithDetails(); // Repository returns entities
196:     return _mapper.Map<List<{Entity}ListDto>>({entities}); // Handler maps to DTOs
197: }
198: 
199: // Example: Using AsNoTracking for read-only queries (in Repository)
200: public async Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}ReadOnly()
201: {
202:     return await _dbContext.{Entities}
203:         .AsNoTracking() // Disables change tracking for performance
204:         .Include(e => e.{ParentEntity})
205:         .ToListAsync();
206: }
207: ```
208: 
209: *For more details, see [querying-patterns.md](resources/querying-patterns.md).*
210: 
211: ### 5. Migrations
212: 
213: Database schema changes are managed through EF Core migrations.
214: 
215: ```powershell
216: # Create a new migration for schema changes
217: dotnet ef migrations add AddNewFieldTo{Entity} --project {Project}.Persistence
218: 
219: # Apply pending migrations to the database
220: dotnet ef database update --project {Project}.Persistence
221: 
222: # Generate SQL script for production deployment
223: dotnet ef migrations script --idempotent --output migrations/release.sql --project {Project}.Persistence
224: ```
225: 
226: *For more details, see [migrations.md](resources/migrations.md).*
227: 
228: ## Key Principles & Conventions
229: 
230: *   **IDs**: All primary keys are `Guid` (or `{IdType}`), except for lookup tables which use `int` (or `{LookupIdType}`).
231: *   **Numeric Types**: Use `int` instead of `long` unless explicitly required for large values (e.g., file sizes, pagination cursors).
232: *   **Default Values**: **DO NOT** add default values in domain entity property initializers (e.g., `public int ViewCount { get; set; } = 0;`). Set defaults in application handlers or use database-level defaults via `IEntityTypeConfiguration`.
233: *   **Link Tables**: Navigation properties on link/mapping tables are **readonly for queries only**. Writes must go through the link table's repository directly.
234: *   **PostgreSQL Features**: Leverage PostgreSQL-specific features like `UUIDv7` for primary keys and PostGIS for spatial data handling.
235: *   **Named Query Filters (EF Core 10+)**: Prefer named filters over combined predicates so specific filters can be disabled when needed.
236: 
237: ---
238: 
239: **Related Documentation**:
240: - [`docs/DOMAIN.md`](../../../docs/DOMAIN.md) - Conceptual domain model.
241: - [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](../../../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) - Overall system architecture.
242: - [`clean-architecture-rules`](../clean-architecture-rules/SKILL.md) - Dependency enforcement.
````
